title.en: Volume 308 Biographies 196: Treacherous Officials - Hu Weiyong, Chen Ying, Yan Song, Zhou Yanru, Wen Tiren, Ma ShiYing
title.raw: 卷三百〇八 列傳第一百九十六 奸臣 胡惟庸 陳瑛 嚴嵩 周延儒 溫體仁 馬士英 Volume 308 Biographies 196: Treacherous Officials - Hu Weiyong, Chen Ying, Yan Song, Zhou Yanru, Wen Tiren, Ma ShiYing

sentences.zh: 奸臣：胡惟庸 陳寧 陳瑛附:馬麟等 嚴嵩附:趙文華等 周延儒 溫體仁 馬士英

translations.literal: Treacherous officials: Hu Weiyong, Chen Ning, Chen Ying with appended biographies of Ma Lin and others, Yan Song with appended biographies of Zhao Wenhua and others, Zhou Yanru, Wen Tiren, Ma Shiying
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous Officials: Hu Weiyong; Chen Ning; Chen Ying (with appended biographies of Ma Lin and others); Yan Song (with appended biographies of Zhao Wenhua and others); Zhou Yanru; Wen Tiren; Ma Shiying

sentences.zh: （阮大鋮）〉

translations.literal: (Ruan Dacheng)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ruan Dacheng)]〉

sentences.zh: 《宋史》論君子小人，取象於陰陽，其說當矣。

translations.literal: The History of Song discusses gentlemen and petty men, taking imagery from yin and yang; its doctrine is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In its discussion of gentlemen and petty men, the History of Song draws on the imagery of yin and yang—a sound approach.

sentences.zh: 然小人世所恒有，不容概被以奸名。

translations.literal: Yet petty men are ever present in the world; one cannot broadly cover them all with the name of treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men are always with us, and not every one of them deserves to be branded a traitor.

sentences.zh: 必其竊弄威柄、構結禍亂、動搖宗祏、屠害忠良、心跡俱惡、終身陰賊者，始加以惡名而不敢辭。

translations.literal: Only those who usurp power in secret, weave together calamity and disorder, shake the imperial altars, slaughter the loyal and good, whose hearts and deeds are alike wicked, and who are covertly villainous all their lives—only then is the evil name applied, and they dare not refuse it.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a man secretly wields power, foments rebellion, endangers the dynasty, murders the loyal, and shows a lifetime of concealed malice in both heart and deed may the name of traitor be laid on him without protest.

sentences.zh: 有明一代，巨奸大惡，多出於寺人內豎，求之外廷諸臣，蓋亦鮮矣。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty, great traitors and great evils mostly came from eunuchs and palace attendants; to seek them among the outer-court ministers was, on the whole, rare.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming, the worst villains were usually eunuchs and palace insiders; truly monstrous ministers at court were comparatively few.

sentences.zh: 當太祖開國之初，胡惟庸凶狡自肆，竟坐叛逆誅死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the founding of the state by Taizu, Hu Weiyong was fierce and cunning and indulged himself, and in the end was put to death on a charge of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizu's reign, Hu Weiyong grew brazen in his cruelty and treachery and was eventually executed for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陳瑛在成祖時，以刻酷濟其奸私，逢君長君，荼毒善類。

translations.literal: Chen Ying in the time of Chengzu used harsh cruelty to advance his treacherous private ends, currying favor with the ruler and encouraging his excesses, and poisoning the good.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzu, Chen Ying used cruelty to serve his private schemes, flattered the emperor into ever harsher rule, and ravaged the upright.

sentences.zh: 此其所值，皆英武明斷之君，而包藏禍心，久之方敗。

translations.literal: Those whom they encountered were all heroic, martial, clear-sighted, and decisive rulers, yet they harbored evil intent and were not exposed until long afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these men served emperors who were vigorous and decisive, yet they concealed their designs for years before they were undone.

sentences.zh: 令遇庸主，其為惡可勝言哉！

translations.literal: Had they met mediocre rulers, how could their evil be fully told!
translations.idiomatic: Had they served a weak emperor, the harm they might have done is beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 厥後權歸內豎，懷奸固寵之徒，依附結納，禍流搢紳。

translations.literal: Thereafter power returned to the inner attendants; those who harbored treachery to secure favor attached themselves and formed cliques, and calamity flowed to the gentry officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as power passed to the eunuchs, schemers who clung to imperial favor built factions, and disaster spread through the civil service.

sentences.zh: 惟世宗朝，閹宦斂跡，而嚴嵩父子濟惡，貪得無厭。

translations.literal: Only in the reign of Shizong did the castrated attendants withdraw their tracks, while Yan Song father and son aided each other's evil and were insatiably greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Shizong did the eunuchs fall back, while Yan Song and his son compounded each other's crimes in bottomless greed.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝手除逆党，而周延儒、溫體仁懷私植黨，誤國覆邦。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie personally removed the rebellious faction, yet Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren harbored private interests and planted factions, misleading the state and overturning the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanglie drove out the traitors with his own hand, yet Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren built private factions that misled the state and brought the dynasty to ruin.

sentences.zh: 南都末造，本無足言，馬士英庸瑣鄙夫，饕殘恣惡。

translations.literal: In the last days of the Southern Capital there was, in the main, nothing worth speaking of; Ma Shiying was a mediocre, petty, base fellow, gluttonous, cruel, and wanton in evil.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Capital's final days scarcely merit mention: Ma Shiying was a vulgar mediocrity, rapacious and cruel without restraint.

sentences.zh: 之數人者，內無閹尹可依，而外與群邪相比，罔恤國事，職為亂階。

translations.literal: These several men had no eunuch chiefs within on whom to rely, yet outwardly they aligned with a host of evil men, heedless of state affairs, making it their office to be steps to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Unlike earlier villains, these men could not lean on eunuch patrons; instead they banded with other corrupt officials, ignored the nation's welfare, and made themselves agents of chaos.

sentences.zh: 究其心跡，殆將與巳、檜同科。

translations.literal: Examining their hearts and tracks, they would nearly share the same category as [Li] Si and [Qin] Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by their hearts and deeds, they belong in the same company as Li Si and Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 籲可畏哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: How dreadful indeed!

sentences.zh: 作《奸臣傳》。

translations.literal: This composes the 'Biographies of Treacherous Officials.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence this chapter, the Biographies of Treacherous Officials.

sentences.zh: 胡惟庸

translations.literal: Hu Weiyong
translations.idiomatic: Hu Weiyong

sentences.zh: 胡惟庸，定遠人。

translations.literal: Hu Weiyong was a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Weiyong was a native of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖於和州，授元帥府奏差。

translations.literal: He joined Taizu at Hezhou and was appointed memorial courier of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Taizu at Hezhou and was made a memorial courier in the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋轉宣使，除寧國主簿，進知縣，遷吉安通判，擢湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be an envoy, appointed chief clerk of Ningguo, advanced to magistrate, moved to be assistant prefect of Ji'an, and promoted to surveillance commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an envoy, then chief clerk of Ningguo, magistrate, assistant prefect of Ji'an, and finally surveillance commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，召為太常少卿，進本寺卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to director of that court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu regime he was summoned to be vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon promoted to its director.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年拜中書省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was appointed vice grand councilor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he was appointed vice grand councilor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 已，代汪廣洋為左丞。

translations.literal: Thereafter he replaced Wang Guangyang as left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He later replaced Wang Guangyang as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，右丞相廣洋左遷廣東行省參政，帝難其人，久不置相，惟庸獨專省事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year the right grand councilor Guangyang was demoted to provincial administrator of Guangdong; the emperor found it difficult to choose a man, and for a long time appointed no grand councilor, while Weiyong alone monopolized the affairs of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 6 the right grand councilor Wang Guangyang was demoted to Guangdong; the emperor could find no suitable replacement and left the post vacant so long that Weiyong alone controlled the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七月拜右丞相。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed right grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was made right grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左丞相，復以廣洋為右丞相。

translations.literal: After a long time he was advanced to left grand councilor, and Guangyang was again made right grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was promoted to left grand councilor while Wang Guangyang was restored as right grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 自楊憲誅，帝以惟庸為才，寵任之。

translations.literal: Since Yang Xian was executed, the emperor regarded Weiyong as talented and favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Xian's execution the emperor saw talent in Weiyong and showered him with trust.

sentences.zh: 惟庸亦自勵，嘗以曲謹當上意，寵遇日盛，獨相數歲，生殺黜陟，或不奏徑行。

translations.literal: Weiyong also urged himself on; he once used subtle deference to match the emperor's intent; favor and treatment grew daily; for several years as sole grand councilor, matters of life, death, dismissal, and promotion were sometimes carried out without memorial and report.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong in turn applied himself, winning favor through obsequious care; as sole grand councilor for years he sometimes ordered executions and appointments without even informing the throne.

sentences.zh: 內外諸司上封事，必先取閱，害己者，輒匿不以聞。

translations.literal: Sealed memorials from all inner and outer offices had first to be taken and read by him; those harmful to himself he would hide and not report.
translations.idiomatic: He intercepted sealed memorials from every department, suppressing any that threatened him.

sentences.zh: 四方躁進之徒及功臣武夫失職者，爭走其門，饋遺金帛、名馬、玩好，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Those eager for advancement from the four directions and martial meritorious officials who had lost their posts all rushed to his gate, presenting gold, silk, famous horses, and curios—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious men from every quarter and disgraced military nobles flocked to his door with gifts of gold, silk, fine horses, and curios beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 大將軍徐達深疾其奸，從容言於帝。

translations.literal: The great general Xu Da deeply hated his treachery and spoke of it at leisure to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Xu Da detested his corruption and spoke of it privately to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 惟庸遂誘達閽者福壽以圖達，為福壽所發。

translations.literal: Weiyong then enticed Xu's gatekeeper Fushou to plot against Da; this was exposed by Fushou.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong then tried to suborn Xu's gatekeeper Fushou to murder him, but Fushou exposed the plot.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉基亦嘗言其短。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Liu Ji had also spoken of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Liu Ji had also criticized him.

sentences.zh: 久之基病，帝遣惟庸挾醫視，遂以毒中之。

translations.literal: After a long time Ji fell ill; the emperor sent Weiyong with a physician to attend him, and he was thus poisoned to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji fell ill the emperor sent Weiyong with a physician to treat him—and Weiyong had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 基死，益無所忌。

translations.literal: When Ji died, he was all the more without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Ji dead, he grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 與太師李善長相結，以兄女妻其從子佑。

translations.literal: He allied with Grand Preceptor Li Shanchang, giving his elder brother's daughter in marriage to Shanchang's nephew You.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with Grand Preceptor Li Shanchang, marrying his elder brother's daughter to Shanchang's nephew You.

sentences.zh: 學士吳伯宗劾惟庸，幾得危禍。

translations.literal: Academician Wu Bozong impeached Weiyong and nearly met with deadly calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Wu Bozong impeached Weiyong and nearly paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 自是，勢益熾。

translations.literal: From this time his power grew ever more fierce.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his power only grew.

sentences.zh: 其定遠舊宅井中，忽生石筍，出水數尺，諛者爭引符瑞，又言其祖父三世塚上，皆夜有火光燭天。

translations.literal: In the well of his old house at Dingyuan a stone bamboo shoot suddenly grew, rising several feet above the water; flatterers vied to cite it as an omen, and also said that on the graves of his grandfather and father for three generations, every night there were flames lighting the sky.
translations.idiomatic: A stone formation like bamboo shoots sprang up several feet from the well at his Dingyuan estate; sycophants hailed it as a portent, and claimed that flames lit the sky nightly above three generations of his ancestors' tombs.

sentences.zh: 惟庸益喜自負，有異謀矣。

translations.literal: Weiyong was all the more pleased and proud of himself, and already had a different design.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong swelled with pride and began to harbor treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 吉安侯陸仲亨自陝西歸，擅乘傳。

translations.literal: Marquis Lu Zhongheng of Ji'an, returning from Shaanxi, usurped the use of relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Lu Zhongheng of Ji'an, returning from Shaanxi, had illegally used the imperial courier service.

sentences.zh: 帝怒責之，曰：「中原兵燹之餘，民始復業，籍戶買馬，艱苦殊甚。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily rebuked him, saying: 'After the warfare in the Central Plain, the people have only just resumed their occupations; registering households to buy horses is exceedingly arduous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him in anger: 'After the wars in the Central Plain the people have only just returned to their fields; registering households to supply relay horses is hardship enough.

sentences.zh: 使皆效爾所為，民雖盡鬻子女，不能給也。

translations.literal: If all were to imitate what you have done, though the people sold all their sons and daughters, they could not supply it.'
translations.idiomatic: If every official imitated you, the people could sell every child they had and still not meet the demand.'

sentences.zh: 」責捕盜於代縣。

translations.literal: He was charged to capture bandits in Dai County.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Dai County to hunt down bandits.

sentences.zh: 平諒侯費聚奉命撫蘇州軍民，日嗜酒色。

translations.literal: Marquis Fei Ju of Pingliang, ordered to pacify the military and civilians of Suzhou, daily indulged in wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Fei Ju of Pingliang, sent to oversee Suzhou's troops and people, spent his days in wine and women.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責往西北招降蒙古，無功，又切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and charged him to go to the northwest to induce the Mongols to surrender; he achieved nothing, and was again sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sent him to the northwest to win Mongol surrenders, and when he failed rebuked him again harshly.

sentences.zh: 二人大懼。

translations.literal: The two men were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 惟庸陰以權利脅誘二人，二人素戇勇，見惟庸用事，密相往來。

translations.literal: Weiyong secretly used power and profit to coerce and entice the two; the two were by nature blunt and brave; seeing Weiyong in power, they secretly associated with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong secretly lured them with promises of power; both were rash and bold by nature, and seeing Weiyong's dominance they began to meet with him in secret.

sentences.zh: 嘗過惟庸家飲，酒酣，惟庸屏左右言：「吾等所為多不法，一旦事覺，如何？

translations.literal: Once, passing Weiyong's house to drink, when the wine was warm, Weiyong dismissed those at his sides and said: 'What we have done is mostly unlawful; once the matter is discovered, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking at Weiyong's home, he dismissed the servants and said, 'We have broken too many laws—what will become of us if we are found out?'

sentences.zh: 」二人益惶懼，惟庸乃告以己意，令在外收集軍馬。

translations.literal: The two were all the more fearful; Weiyong then told them his own intent and ordered them to gather troops and horses outside.
translations.idiomatic: They grew still more afraid; Weiyong then revealed his plan and told them to raise troops and horses in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與陳寧坐省中，閱天下軍馬籍，令都督毛驤取衛士劉遇賢及亡命魏文進等為心膂，曰：「吾有所用爾也。

translations.literal: He also once sat with Chen Ning in the Secretariat, reviewing the registers of troops and horses throughout the realm, and ordered the commander-in-chief Mao Zang to take guardsman Liu Yuxian and the fugitive Wei Wenjin and others as heart and backbone, saying: 'I have use for you.'
translations.idiomatic: Another time he sat with Chen Ning in the Secretariat reviewing the empire's military rolls, and told Commander Mao Zang to recruit guardsman Liu Yuxian, the fugitive Wei Wenjin, and others as his inner circle, saying, 'I have work for you.'

sentences.zh: 」太僕寺丞李存義者，善長之弟，惟庸婿李佑父也，惟庸令陰說善長。

translations.literal: Li Cunyi, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was Shanchang's younger brother and the father of Weiyong's son-in-law Li You; Weiyong ordered him to persuade Shanchang in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunyi of the Court of the Imperial Stud—Li Shanchang's younger brother and father of Weiyong's son-in-law Li You—was told to win Shanchang over in secret.

sentences.zh: 善長已老，不能強拒，初不許，已而依違其間。

translations.literal: Shanchang was already old and could not strongly refuse; at first he did not consent, but afterward wavered between the two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Shanchang was old and could not firmly refuse; he first declined, then wavered.

sentences.zh: 惟庸益以為事可就，乃遣明州衛指揮林賢下海招倭，與期會。

translations.literal: Weiyong all the more thought the affair could succeed, and then sent the commander of Mingzhou Guard, Lin Xian, to go to sea to recruit Japanese pirates and arrange a rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong grew confident the plot could succeed and sent Commander Lin Xian of Mingzhou Guard to sea to recruit Japanese pirates for a coordinated strike.

sentences.zh: 又遣元故臣封績致書稱臣於元嗣君，請兵為外應。

translations.literal: He also sent the former Yuan minister Feng Ji to write a letter declaring himself subject to the Yuan successor ruler, requesting troops as an external response.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the former Yuan minister Feng Ji to write to the Yuan heir, professing allegiance and begging for troops as an external force.

sentences.zh: 事皆未發。

translations.literal: The affairs had all not yet broken out.
translations.idiomatic: None of this had yet come to light.

sentences.zh: 會惟庸子馳馬於市，墜死車下，惟庸殺挽車者。

translations.literal: It happened that Weiyong's son galloped a horse in the market and fell dead beneath a cart; Weiyong killed the cart-puller.
translations.idiomatic: Then Weiyong's son was killed when his horse bolted in the market and he was thrown under a cart; Weiyong had the carter executed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命償其死。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered that his death be compensated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Weiyong to pay with his life for the carter's death.

sentences.zh: 惟庸請以金帛給其家，不許。

translations.literal: Weiyong requested to give gold and silk to the family; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong offered gold and silk to the family, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 惟庸懼，乃與御史大夫陳寧、中丞涂節等謀起事，陰告四方及武臣從己者。

translations.literal: Weiyong was afraid, and then with Censor-in-chief Chen Ning, Vice Censor Tu Jie, and others plotted to rise in revolt, secretly informing the four directions and military officials who would follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Weiyong plotted rebellion with Censor-in-chief Chen Ning, Vice Censor Tu Jie, and others, secretly summoning allies across the empire and among the military.

sentences.zh: 十二年九月，占城來貢，惟庸等不以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year Champa came to offer tribute; Weiyong and the others did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 12 an embassy arrived from Champa, but Weiyong and his colleagues never reported it.

sentences.zh: 中官出見之，入奏。

translations.literal: A palace attendant went out to see them and entered to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch met them and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，敕責省臣。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and issued an edict rebuking the Secretariat ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and rebuked the Secretariat in an edict.

sentences.zh: 惟庸及廣洋頓首謝罪，而微委其咎於禮部，部臣又委之中書。

translations.literal: Weiyong and Guangyang knocked their heads and apologized, yet subtly shifted the blame to the Ministry of Rites; the ministry officials in turn shifted it to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong and Wang Guangyang kowtowed in apology, but subtly blamed the Ministry of Rites, which in turn blamed the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，盡囚諸臣，窮詰主者。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, imprisoned all the ministers, and pressed to the end to find the responsible party.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger deepened; he imprisoned every official involved and demanded to know who was responsible.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賜廣洋死，廣洋妾陳氏從死。

translations.literal: Before long Guangyang was granted death; Guangyang's concubine Lady Chen followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Guangyang was sentenced to death; his concubine Lady Chen died with him.

sentences.zh: 帝詢之，乃入官陳知縣女也。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired and learned that she was the daughter of Magistrate Chen who had entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On inquiry the emperor learned she was the daughter of Magistrate Chen, a woman taken into the palace after his conviction.

sentences.zh: 大怒曰：「沒官婦女，止給功臣家。

translations.literal: He said in great anger: 'Women of confiscated officials are given only to meritorious households.
translations.idiomatic: He raged: 'Women from disgraced officials are allotted only to meritorious households.

sentences.zh: 文臣何以得給？

translations.literal: How may civil officials receive them?'
translations.idiomatic: What right had a civil minister to take one?'

sentences.zh: 」乃敕法司取勘。

translations.literal: He then ordered the judicial offices to take up investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the judiciary to investigate.

sentences.zh: 於是惟庸及六部堂屬咸當坐罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiyong and the chiefs and subordinates of the six ministries were all liable to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong and the chiefs of all six ministries were now liable to punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，涂節遂上變，告惟庸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Tu Jie then submitted a sudden report denouncing Weiyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Tu Jie turned informer and denounced Weiyong.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞商暠時謫為中書省吏，亦以惟庸陰事告。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-chief Shang Ao, at the time demoted to a clerk of the Secretariat, also reported Weiyong's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-chief Shang Ao, then demoted to a Secretariat clerk, also reported Weiyong's secret plots.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下廷臣更訊，詞連寧、節。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and handed the case to court ministers for renewed interrogation; the testimony implicated Ning and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered a full court inquiry; the testimony implicated Chen Ning and Tu Jie as well.

sentences.zh: 廷臣言：「節本預謀，見事不成，始上變告，不可不誅。

translations.literal: The court ministers said: 'Jie originally took part in the plot; seeing the affair could not succeed, he then submitted a sudden report; he cannot escape execution.'
translations.idiomatic: The court argued: 'Tu Jie was in on the plot from the start and informed only when it failed—he too must die.'

sentences.zh: 」乃誅惟庸、寧並及節。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiyong, Ning, and Jie as well were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong, Chen Ning, and Tu Jie were all executed.

sentences.zh: 惟庸既死，其反狀猶未盡露。

translations.literal: After Weiyong's death, the full extent of his rebellion was still not exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Weiyong's execution the full scope of his treason was not yet known.

sentences.zh: 至十八年，李存義為人首告，免死，安置崇明。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year Li Cunyi was denounced by another; he was spared death and settled on Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 Li Cunyi was denounced by another; his life was spared and he was exiled to Chongming.

sentences.zh: 十九年十月，林賢獄成，惟庸通倭事始著。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year Lin Xian's case was concluded, and Weiyong's communication with the Japanese pirates first became clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 19 Lin Xian's case was concluded, and Weiyong's collusion with Japanese pirates first came to light.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，藍玉征沙漠，獲封績，善長不以奏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Lan Yu campaigned in the desert and captured Feng Ji; Shanchang did not memorialize this.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 Lan Yu's desert campaign captured Feng Ji, but Li Shanchang never reported it.

sentences.zh: 至二十三年五月，事發，捕績下吏，訊得其狀，逆謀益大著。

translations.literal: By the fifth month of the twenty-third year the affair broke out; Feng Ji was arrested and handed to the officials; interrogation obtained the facts, and the treasonous plot became all the more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 23 the plot surfaced; Feng Ji was arrested and under interrogation revealed everything, and the conspiracy grew unmistakably clear.

sentences.zh: 會善長家奴盧仲謙首善長與惟庸往來狀，而陸仲亨家奴封帖木亦首仲亨及唐勝宗、費聚、趙庸三侯與惟庸共謀不軌。

translations.literal: It happened that Shanchang's household slave Lu Zhongqian reported Shanchang's dealings with Weiyong, while Lu Zhongheng's household slave Feng Tiemuer also reported Zhongheng and the three marquises Tang Shengzong, Fei Ju, and Zhao Yong plotting irregular conduct with Weiyong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shanchang's slave Lu Zhongqian then reported his master's dealings with Weiyong, and Lu Zhongheng's slave Feng Tiemuer reported that Zhongheng and Marquises Tang Shengzong, Fei Ju, and Zhao Yong had joined Weiyong's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 帝發怒，肅清逆黨，詞所連及坐誅者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor erupted in anger and purged the rebellious faction; those implicated in the testimony and put to death numbered more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage unleashed a purge of the traitor faction; more than thirty thousand people were implicated and executed.

sentences.zh: 乃為《昭示奸黨錄》，佈告天下。

translations.literal: He then composed the Record of the Exposure of the Treacherous Faction and proclaimed it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He issued the Record of the Exposure of the Treacherous Faction and proclaimed it to the empire.

sentences.zh: 株連蔓引，迄數年未靖云。

translations.literal: Implicating and extending branches and tendrils, for several years there was no peace—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The dragnet of guilt-by-association continued for years before the turmoil subsided.

sentences.zh: 陳寧，茶陵人。

translations.literal: Chen Ning was a man of Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ning was a native of Chaling.

sentences.zh: 元末為鎮江小吏，從軍至集慶，館於軍帥家，代軍帥上書言事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was a minor clerk in Zhenjiang; he followed the army to Jiqing, lodged in a military commander's house, and on the commander's behalf submitted a memorial on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he was a minor clerk in Zhenjiang; he followed the army to Jiqing, lodged with a commander, and drafted a memorial in the commander's name.

sentences.zh: 太祖覽之稱善，召試檄文，詞意雄偉，乃用為行省掾吏。

translations.literal: Taizu read it and praised it; he summoned him to test his proclamation drafts; the wording was grand and imposing, and he was then employed as a clerk of the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu read it with approval, tested him with a draft proclamation, found his style bold and imposing, and made him a clerk in the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 時方四征，羽書帝午，寧酬答整暇，事無留滯，太祖益才之。

translations.literal: At the time campaigns were being waged on four fronts; military dispatches arrived like the sun at noon; Ning answered them with composed leisure, and nothing was delayed; Taizu all the more regarded him as talented.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were then being fought on four fronts and dispatches poured in without cease; Ning handled them with calm efficiency and Taizu came to value him highly.

sentences.zh: 淮安納款，奉命徵其兵，抵高郵，為吳人所獲。

translations.literal: When Huai'an submitted, he was ordered to levy its troops; reaching Gaoyou, he was captured by Wu men.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'an surrendered he was sent to levy its troops; at Gaoyou he was captured by Wu forces.

sentences.zh: 寧抗論不屈，釋還，擢廣德知府。

translations.literal: Ning argued defiantly and would not yield; he was released and returned, and was promoted to prefect of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Ning argued boldly and refused to submit; he was released and promoted to prefect of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 會大旱，乞免民租，不許。

translations.literal: It happened that there was a great drought; he begged to remit the people's land tax; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he petitioned to remit the land tax, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 寧自詣太祖奏曰：「民饑如此，猶征租不已，是為張士誠驅民也。

translations.literal: Ning himself went to Taizu and memorialized, saying: 'The people are starving like this, yet rent is still levied without cease—this is driving the people to Zhang Shicheng.'
translations.idiomatic: Ning went in person to Taizu and said, 'The people are starving, yet we still collect rent—you will drive them straight into Zhang Shicheng's arms.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖壯而聽之。

translations.literal: Taizu was impressed and heeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was moved and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 辛丑除樞密院都事。

translations.literal: In xinchou he was appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year he was appointed director in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 癸卯遷提刑按察司僉事。

translations.literal: In guimao he was transferred to surveillance vice commissioner of the Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the guimao year he was made surveillance vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年改浙東按察使。

translations.literal: The following year he was changed to surveillance commissioner of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed surveillance commissioner of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 有小隸訟其隱過，寧已擢中書參議，太祖親鞫之，寧首服，系應天獄一歲。

translations.literal: A minor clerk sued him for concealed faults; Ning had already been promoted to Secretariat participant; Taizu personally interrogated him; Ning confessed first and was imprisoned in the Yingtian jail for one year.
translations.idiomatic: A minor clerk sued him for hidden misconduct. Though Ning had already been promoted to Secretariat participant, Taizu personally tried the case; Ning confessed and spent a year in Yingtian prison.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，冬盡將決，太祖惜其才，命諸將數其罪而宥之，用為太倉市舶提舉。

translations.literal: In the Wu year, winter was ending and execution was imminent; Taizu prized his talent, ordered the generals to count his crimes and pardon him, and employed him as maritime trade commissioner of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: As winter ended and execution neared in the Wu year, Taizu valued his talent, had his crimes enumerated and then pardoned him, and appointed him maritime trade commissioner at Taicang.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年召拜司農卿，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was summoned and appointed minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, and transferred to minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 he was summoned as minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and soon made minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年出為松江知府。

translations.literal: The following year he went out as prefect of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out as prefect of Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 用嚴為治，積蠹弊，多所厘革。

translations.literal: He governed with severity, and where long-standing abuses had accumulated, he reformed many of them.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with harsh severity and cut through many long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 尋改山西行省參政。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to provincial administrator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to provincial administrator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 召拜參知政事，知吏、戶、禮三部事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed vice grand councilor, managing the affairs of the Ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice grand councilor in charge of the Ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and Rites.

sentences.zh: 寧，初名亮，至是賜名寧。

translations.literal: Ning, whose original name was Liang, at this time was granted the name Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Liang, he was now granted the name Ning.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐事出知蘇州。

translations.literal: In the third year, on account of an offense he went out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was demoted to prefect of Suzhou for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋改浙江行省參政，未行，用胡惟庸薦，召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to provincial administrator of Zhejiang; before he departed, on Hu Weiyong's recommendation he was summoned as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Zhejiang provincial administrator, but before he could leave, Hu Weiyong recommended him and he was summoned as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗禦東閣，免冠而櫛。

translations.literal: Taizu once attended the Eastern Pavilion, removed his cap and combed his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu was at the Eastern Pavilion with his cap off, combing his hair.

sentences.zh: 寧與侍御史商暠入奏事，太祖見之，遂移入便殿，遣人止寧毋入。

translations.literal: Ning and attendant censor Shang Ao entered to memorialize; Taizu saw them and then moved into the side hall, sending someone to stop Ning from entering.
translations.idiomatic: Ning and attendant censor Shang Ao came to report; the emperor saw them, withdrew to a side hall, and sent word that Ning should not enter.

sentences.zh: 櫛已，整冠出閣，始命入見。

translations.literal: When the combing was done, he straightened his cap and came out of the pavilion; only then was Ning ordered to be received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished combing, straightened his cap, and emerged, Ning was at last admitted.

sentences.zh: 六年命兼領國子監事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered concurrently to oversee the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was ordered to oversee the Directorate of Education as well.

sentences.zh: 俄拜右御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 八月遣釋奠先師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was sent to perform the libation sacrifice to the First Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was sent to perform the libation to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 丞相胡惟庸、參政馮冕、誠意伯劉基不陪祀而受胙，太祖以寧不舉奏，亦停俸半月。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Hu Weiyong, Participant Feng Mian, and Earl of Sincerity Liu Ji did not attend the sacrifice yet received sacrificial meat; Taizu because Ning did not memorialize this also withheld his salary for half a month.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Hu Weiyong, Participant Feng Mian, and Earl of Sincerity Liu Ji skipped the sacrifice yet still received sacrificial meat; because Ning failed to report this, Taizu docked his salary for half a month.

sentences.zh: 自是，不預祭者不頒胙。

translations.literal: From this time, those who did not take part in the sacrifice were not issued sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who did not attend the sacrifice received no sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左御史大夫。

translations.literal: After a long time he was advanced to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寧有才氣，而性特嚴刻。

translations.literal: Ning had talent and spirit, but his nature was especially harsh and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was gifted, but by nature he was exceptionally harsh and cruel.

sentences.zh: 其在蘇州徵賦苛急，嘗燒鐵烙人肌膚。

translations.literal: When he was in Suzhou levying taxes he was harsh and urgent, and once burned iron to brand people's skin.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Suzhou he collected taxes with brutal urgency and once branded people's skin with heated iron.

sentences.zh: 吏民苦之，號為陳烙鐵。

translations.literal: Officials and people suffered; they called him Chen the Branding Iron.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners suffered under him and nicknamed him Chen the Branding Iron.

sentences.zh: 及居憲台，益務威嚴。

translations.literal: When he occupied the Censorate he all the more pursued awe and severity.
translations.idiomatic: At the Censorate he pursued intimidation all the more.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗責之，寧不能改。

translations.literal: Taizu once rebuked him, but Ning could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rebuked him, but Ning would not reform.

sentences.zh: 其子孟麟亦數諫，寧怒，捶之數百，竟死。

translations.literal: His son Menglin also repeatedly remonstrated; Ning in anger beat him several hundred times, and he died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: His son Menglin remonstrated repeatedly; Ning beat him hundreds of times in a rage until the boy died.

sentences.zh: 太祖深惡其不情，曰：「寧於其子如此，奚有於君父耶！

translations.literal: Taizu deeply hated his lack of human feeling and said: 'Ning treats his own son like this—what would he do to his ruler and father!'
translations.idiomatic: Taizu despised his heartlessness and said, 'If Ning treats his own son like this, what would he do to his sovereign and father!'

sentences.zh: 」寧聞之懼，遂與惟庸通謀。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Ning was afraid, and then joined in conspiracy with Weiyong.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified by this, Ning threw in his lot with Weiyong's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，惟庸事發，寧亦伏誅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year Weiyong's affair broke out, and Ning also was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 13, when Weiyong's plot was exposed, Ning too was executed.

sentences.zh: 瑛天性殘忍，受帝寵任，益務深刻，專以搏擊為能。

translations.literal: Ying by nature was cruel; receiving the emperor's favor and trust, he all the more pursued severity, making attack and strike his sole ability.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Chen Ying was cruel; favored by the emperor, he grew ever harsher and made persecution his specialty.

sentences.zh: 甫蒞事，即言：「陛下應天順人，萬姓率服，而廷臣有不順命、效死建文者，如侍郎黃觀、少卿廖升、修撰王叔英、紀善周是修、按察使王良、知縣顏伯瑋等，其心與叛逆無異，請追戮之。

translations.literal: As soon as he took office he said: 'Your Majesty received Heaven's mandate and the people submit; yet among court ministers there are those who do not obey orders and would die for Jianwen, such as Vice Minister Huang Guan, Junior Minister Liao Sheng, Compiler Wang Shuying, Recorder Zhou Shixiu, Surveillance Commissioner Wang Liang, Magistrate Yan Bowei, and others—their hearts differ not from rebellion; I beg that they be pursued and executed.'
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he said, 'Your Majesty has Heaven's mandate and the people obey, yet ministers such as Vice Minister Huang Guan, Junior Minister Liao Sheng, Compiler Wang Shuying, Recorder Zhou Shixiu, Surveillance Commissioner Wang Liang, and Magistrate Yan Bowei would rather die for Jianwen than serve you—their hearts are no different from rebellion; I beg that they be hunted down and killed.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕誅奸臣，不過齊、黃數輩，後二十九人中如張紞王鈍、鄭賜、黃福、尹昌隆，皆宥而用之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I executed treacherous ministers—no more than the several men of Qi and Huang; among the later twenty-nine, such as Zhang Shuo, Wang Dun, Zheng Ci, Huang Fu, and Yin Changlong, all were pardoned and employed.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, 'I punished only a handful of traitors like Qi and Huang; of the twenty-nine others, men such as Zhang Shuo, Wang Dun, Zheng Ci, Huang Fu, and Yin Changlong were all pardoned and employed.'

sentences.zh: 況汝所言，有不與此數者，勿問。

translations.literal: Moreover, among what you speak, if there are any not of this number, do not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: And if any you name are not among those men, leave them alone.

sentences.zh: 」後瑛閱方孝孺等獄詞，遂簿觀、叔英等家，給配其妻女，疏族、外親莫不連染。

translations.literal: Afterward Ying reviewed the case records of Fang Xiaoru and others, then registered the households of Guan, Shuying, and the rest, assigning their wives and daughters, and collateral and external kin—none escaped implication.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ying reviewed Fang Xiaoru's case files, registered the households of Guan, Shuying, and the rest, assigned their wives and daughters to servitude, and implicated every collateral and in-law kin.

sentences.zh: 胡閏之獄，所籍數百家，號冤聲徹天。

translations.literal: In Hu Ying's case, several hundred households were confiscated; cries of injustice filled the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: In Hu Ying's case hundreds of households were confiscated; cries of injustice shook the heavens.

sentences.zh: 兩列御史皆掩泣，瑛亦色慘，謂人曰：「不以叛逆處此輩，則吾等為無名。

translations.literal: Censors on both rows all covered their faces weeping; Ying's face too was grim, and he said to others: 'If we do not treat these people as rebels, then we are good for nothing.'
translations.idiomatic: Censors on both sides wept openly; Ying too looked grim and said, 'Unless we treat these men as rebels, we are good for nothing.'

sentences.zh: 」於是諸忠臣無遺種矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the loyal ministers left no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the loyal ministers were exterminated to the last man.

sentences.zh: 瑛為都御史數年，所論劾勳戚、大臣十余人，皆陰希帝指。

translations.literal: Ying as chief censor for several years impeached more than ten meritorious nobles and great ministers, all secretly conforming to the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: As chief censor for years, Ying impeached more than a dozen meritorious nobles and great ministers, always reading the emperor's mood.

sentences.zh: 其他所劾順昌伯王佐，都督陳俊，指揮王恕，都督曹遠，指揮房昭，僉都御史俞士吉，大理少卿袁復，御史車舒，都督王瑞，指揮林泉、牛諒，通政司參議賀銀等，先後又數十人，俱得罪。

translations.literal: Others he impeached included Marquis Wang Zuo of Shunchang, Commander Chen Jun, Commander Wang Nu, Commander Cao Yuan, Commander Fang Zhao, Vice Censor-in-chief Yu Shiji, Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu, Censor Che Shu, Commander Wang Rui, Commanders Lin Quan and Niu Liang, and Participant He Yin of the Secretariat of Transmission, and several dozen more in succession—all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought down Marquis Wang Zuo of Shunchang, Commanders Chen Jun, Wang Nu, Cao Yuan, and Fang Zhao, Vice Censor-in-chief Yu Shiji, Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu, Censor Che Shu, Commander Wang Rui, Commanders Lin Quan and Niu Liang, Secretariat participant He Yin, and dozens more besides.

sentences.zh: 帝以為能發奸，寵任之，然亦知其殘刻，所奏讞不盡從。

translations.literal: The emperor thought him able to expose treachery and favored and entrusted him, yet also knew his cruelty; memorials on criminal cases were not all followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued him for exposing wrongdoing yet knew his cruelty and did not approve every case he brought.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人芮善弟夫婦為盜所殺，心疑其所親，訟於官。

translations.literal: Rui Shan, a Secretariat draftsman, and his brother and wife were killed by bandits; he suspected their kin and sued at court.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat draftsman Rui Shan's brother and wife were murdered by bandits; he suspected relatives and sued.

sentences.zh: 刑部驗非盜，縱之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice examined the case and found they were not bandits, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice found no bandits and released the suspects.

sentences.zh: 善白帝刑部故出盜，帝命御史鞫治，果非盜。

translations.literal: Shan told the emperor the Ministry deliberately released bandits; the emperor ordered censors to investigate; in truth they were not bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shan told the emperor the Ministry had deliberately freed the killers; censors investigated and confirmed they were innocent.

sentences.zh: 瑛因劾善妄奏，當下獄。

translations.literal: Ying therefore impeached Shan for false memorial and demanded he be imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ying then impeached Shan for false reporting and demanded his arrest.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「兄弟同氣，得賊惟恐逸之，善何罪，其勿問。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Brothers share the same breath; to catch the killer one fears only that he will escape—what crime has Shan? Do not inquire.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Brothers are of one flesh—a man who has lost kin fears only that the killer will escape; what crime has Shan committed? Let it drop.'

sentences.zh: 車裏宣慰使刀暹答侵威遠州地，執其知州刀算黨以歸。

translations.literal: Dao Tianda, pacification commissioner of Cheli, encroached on Weiyuan prefecture land and seized its prefect Dao Suandang and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Tianda, pacification commissioner of Cheli, seized land in Weiyuan and carried off its prefect Dao Suandang.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使諭之，刀暹答懼，歸地及所執知州，遣弟刀臘等貢方物謝罪。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to instruct him; Dao Tianda was afraid, returned the land and the seized prefect, and sent his younger brother Dao La and others to offer local products in apology.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys; Dao Tianda, afraid, returned the land and the prefect and sent his brother Dao La with tribute to apologize.

sentences.zh: 瑛請先下刀臘法司，且逮治刀暹答。

translations.literal: Ying requested first to hand Dao La to the judiciary and also to arrest and punish Dao Tianda.
translations.idiomatic: Ying asked that Dao La be sent to the judiciary first and Dao Tianda arrested.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蠻僚之性稍不相得則相仇，改則已。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The nature of barbarian officials—if they slightly fail to get along they become enemies; if they reform, let it be.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Barbarian chiefs feud at the slightest provocation; when they submit, accept it.'

sentences.zh: 今服罪而復治之，何以處不服者。

translations.literal: Now they have submitted in guilt—if we punish them again, how shall we treat those who do not submit?'
translations.idiomatic: They have apologized—if we punish them again, what of those who refuse to submit?'

sentences.zh: 」遂赦弗問。

translations.literal: He then pardoned and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 知嘉興縣李鑒廷見謝罪，帝問故。

translations.literal: Magistrate Li Jian of Jiaxing was summoned to audience to apologize; the emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Jian of Jiaxing was summoned to apologize; the emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 瑛言：「鑒籍奸党姚瑄，瑄弟亨當連坐，而鑒釋亨不籍，宜罪。

translations.literal: Ying said: 'Jian's household was registered because of the traitor faction member Yao Xuan; Xuan's younger brother Heng should be implicated in joint punishment, yet Jian released Heng without registering him—he should be punished.'
translations.idiomatic: Ying said Jian's family had been registered because of traitor Yao Xuan; Xuan's brother Heng should have been included, but Jian released Heng without registering him and should be punished.

sentences.zh: 」鑒言：「都察院文止籍瑄，未有亨名。

translations.literal: Jian said: 'The Censorate document registered only Xuan; Heng's name was not listed.'
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied that the Censorate order named only Xuan, not Heng.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「院文無名而不籍，不失為慎重。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The Censorate document had no name and he did not register—this is not losing carefulness.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'If the document named no one else, not registering Heng was prudent.'

sentences.zh: 」鑒得免。

translations.literal: Jian was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was acquitted.

sentences.zh: 戶部人材高文雅言時政，因及建文事，辭意率直，帝命議行之。

translations.literal: Gao Wenya of the Ministry of Personnel, a man of talent, spoke on current affairs and touched on Jianwen matters; his wording was blunt and direct; the emperor ordered discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wenya, a talented man in the Ministry of Personnel, spoke frankly on current affairs including the Jianwen reign; the emperor ordered his proposals considered.

sentences.zh: 瑛劾文雅狂妄，請置之法。

translations.literal: Ying impeached Wenya for arrogance and requested he be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Ying impeached Wenya for arrogance and demanded legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「草野之人何知忌諱，其言有可采，奈何以直而廢之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'How would a man of the wilds know taboos? If his words have something worth adopting, how can we discard them for bluntness?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'How would a rustic know court taboos? If his words have merit, why discard them for bluntness?'

sentences.zh: 瑛刻薄，非助朕為善者。

translations.literal: Ying is harsh—he is not one who helps me do good.
translations.idiomatic: Ying is harsh—he does not help me govern well.

sentences.zh: 」以文雅付吏部，量材授官。

translations.literal: Wenya was handed to the Ministry of Personnel and an office was granted according to his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wenya was sent to the Ministry of Personnel and given an appointment suited to his ability.

sentences.zh: 海運糧漂沒，瑛請治官軍罪，責之償。

translations.literal: Sea-transport grain was washed away and lost; Ying requested punishment of the official troops' crime and held them liable to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: When sea-transport grain was lost at sea, Ying demanded that the transport troops be punished and forced to pay compensation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「海濤險惡，官軍免溺死，幸矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Sea waves are perilous and vicious; that the official troops escaped drowning is already fortunate.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'The sea is treacherous; that the troops escaped drowning is fortune enough.'

sentences.zh: 」悉釋不問。

translations.literal: All were released and not inquired into.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 瑛之奸險附會，一意苛刻，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Ying's treacherous cunning, forced alignment, and single-minded harshness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's treachery, opportunism, and relentless harshness were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 帝北巡，皇太子監國。

translations.literal: The emperor toured the north; the crown prince supervised the state.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor toured the north, the crown prince governed as regent.

sentences.zh: 瑛言兵部主事李貞受皁隸葉轉等四人金，請下貞獄。

translations.literal: Ying said that Li Zhen, a director in the Ministry of War, received gold from the clerks Ye Zhuan and four others, and requested that Zhen be imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ying reported that Ministry of War director Li Zhen had taken bribes from clerks including Ye Zhuan and asked that Zhen be imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 無何，貞妻擊登聞鼓訴冤。

translations.literal: Before long Zhen's wife struck the Denunciation Drum to plead injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhen's wife beat the Denunciation Drum to protest his innocence.

sentences.zh: 皇太子命六部大臣廷鞫之，自辰至午，貞等不至，惟葉轉至。

translations.literal: The crown prince ordered the great ministers of the six ministries to interrogate at court; from the chen hour to the wu hour Zhen and the others did not come—only Ye Zhuan arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ordered the six ministries to try the case in open court; from morning until noon Zhen and the others failed to appear—only Ye Zhuan came.

sentences.zh: 訊之，雲貞不承，不勝拷掠死，三皁錄皆笞死三日矣，貞實未嘗受金。

translations.literal: On interrogation he said Zhen did not confess; unable to bear torture he died; the three clerks had all been beaten to death three days before; Zhen in truth had never received gold.
translations.idiomatic: Under questioning he said Zhen had denied the charge; broken by torture he died; the three clerks had already been beaten to death three days earlier; Zhen had never taken a bribe.

sentences.zh: 先是，袁綱、覃珩兩御史俱至兵部索皁隸，貞猝無以應，兩御史銜之，興此獄。

translations.literal: Earlier, the two censors Yuan Gang and Tan Heng had both come to the Ministry of War to demand clerks; Zhen suddenly had none to offer; the two censors bore a grudge and raised this case.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Censors Yuan Gang and Tan Heng had come to the Ministry demanding clerks; Zhen had none ready to hand over; the two censors bore a grudge and fabricated the case.

sentences.zh: 於是刑科給事中耿通等言瑛及綱、珩朋奸蒙蔽，擅殺無辜，請罪瑛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Geng Tong of the Penal Section and others said Ying together with Gang and Heng in factional treachery deceived and concealed, and on their own authority killed the innocent; they requested punishment of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Geng Tong and others then charged that Ying, Gang, and Heng had conspired to deceive the court and murdered innocent men, and demanded Ying be punished.

sentences.zh: 皇太子曰：「瑛大臣，蓋為下所欺，不能覺察耳。

translations.literal: The crown prince said: 'Ying is a great minister; he was probably deceived by subordinates and could not detect it.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, 'Ying is a senior minister; he was probably deceived by his subordinates and failed to see through them.'

sentences.zh: 」置勿問，械系綱、珩，以其罪狀奏行在。

translations.literal: The matter was set aside and not inquired into; Gang and Heng were shackled and imprisoned, and their crimes were memorialized to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the charge against Ying, put Gang and Heng in chains, and reported their crimes to the emperor on campaign.

sentences.zh: 又有學官坐事謫充太學膳夫者，皇太子令法司與改役，瑛格不行，中允劉子春等復劾瑛方命自恣。

translations.literal: There was also a school official punished for an offense and demoted to serve as a cook in the Imperial Academy; the crown prince ordered the judiciary to change his service; Ying blocked and would not carry it out; Junior Mentor Liu Zichun and others again impeached Ying for defying orders and acting willfully.
translations.idiomatic: When a disgraced school official was demoted to cook in the Imperial Academy, the crown prince ordered a lighter assignment; Ying refused to comply; Junior Mentor Liu Zichun and others again impeached Ying for defying orders.

sentences.zh: 皇太子謂瑛曰：「卿用心刻薄，不明政體，殊非大臣之道。

translations.literal: The crown prince said to Ying: 'You are harsh in intent, do not understand the substance of government, and are utterly unlike the way of a great minister.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince told Ying, 'Your heart is cruel, you do not understand how government should work, and this is no way for a great minister to behave.'

sentences.zh: 」時太子深惡瑛，以帝方寵任，無如何。

translations.literal: At this time the crown prince deeply hated Ying, but because the emperor was then favoring and employing him, nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince deeply loathed Ying, but with the emperor still favoring him there was nothing to be done.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝亦浸疏瑛。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor also gradually distanced Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor too grew distant from Ying.

sentences.zh: 九年春，瑛得罪下獄死，天下快之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year Ying offended, was imprisoned, and died; the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 9 Ying fell from favor, died in prison, and the empire rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 帝以篡得天下，御下多用重典。

translations.literal: The emperor, having seized the realm, in governing subordinates often used heavy statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Having seized the throne, the emperor often ruled his subjects with harsh laws.

sentences.zh: 瑛首承風旨，傾誣排陷者無算。

translations.literal: Ying was the first to receive the wind of his intent; those he overturned, falsely accused, and entrapped were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was foremost in carrying out that intent; the men he framed and destroyed were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 一時臣工多效其所為，如紀綱、馬麟、丁玨、秦政學、趙緯、李芳，皆以傾險聞。

translations.literal: For a time many officials imitated what he did, such as Ji Gang, Ma Lin, Ding Jue, Qin Zhengxue, Zhao Wei, and Li Fang—all were known for overturning and treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials of the day imitated him—Ji Gang, Ma Lin, Ding Jue, Qin Zhengxue, Zhao Wei, and Li Fang were all notorious for their treacherous schemes.

sentences.zh: 綱在《佞幸傳》。

translations.literal: Gang is in the 'Biographies of Favorites.'
translations.idiomatic: Gang's biography appears in the chapter on imperial favorites.

sentences.zh: 馬麟 等

translations.literal: Ma Lin and others
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin and others

sentences.zh: 玨，山陽人。

translations.literal: Jue was a man of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Jue was a native of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年，裏社賽神，誣以聚眾謀不軌，坐死者數十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle, at a village community god-competition, he falsely accused them of gathering a crowd to plot irregular conduct; several dozen were put to death on the charge.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 4 he denounced a village festival as a seditious assembly; dozens were executed on his false charge.

sentences.zh: 法司因稱玨忠，特擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: The judiciary therefore praised Jue's loyalty and specially promoted him to supervising secretary of the Penal Section.
translations.idiomatic: The judiciary praised his loyalty and specially promoted him to supervising secretary of the Penal Section.

sentences.zh: 伺察百僚小過，輒上聞。

translations.literal: He watched for small faults among the hundred officials and immediately reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: He spied on officials for the smallest faults and reported them at once.

sentences.zh: 居官十年，貪黷不顧廉恥。

translations.literal: In office for ten years he was greedy and corrupt without regard for integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years in office he was corrupt and shameless.

sentences.zh: 母喪未期，起復視事，輒隨眾大祀齋宮，復與慶成宴，為御史俞信等所劾，論大不敬當死。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period for his mother had ended he was recalled to resume duties; he then followed the crowd to the fasting palace for the great sacrifice and again joined the celebration banquet; he was impeached by Censor Yu Xin and others and judged guilty of great irreverence, deserving death.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning before the period had ended, he attended the great sacrifice in the fasting palace and the celebration banquet; Censor Yu Xin impeached him for grave irreverence, a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕素疑其奸邪，若悉行所言，廷臣豈有一人免耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I have long suspected his treacherous evil; if all he said were carried out, would a single court minister escape?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'I have long suspected his treachery; if everything he reported were acted on, would a single minister survive?'

sentences.zh: 」遂謫戍邊。

translations.literal: He was then banished to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to frontier garrison duty instead.

sentences.zh: 政學，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Zhengxue was a man of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zhengxue was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Yongle year 2.

sentences.zh: 曆行在禮部郎中，務掇人過失，肆為奸貪。

translations.literal: He served as director in the traveling Ministry of Rites, devoted to picking out people's faults, and wantonly practiced treachery and greed.
translations.idiomatic: As director in the traveling Ministry of Rites he hunted for others' faults and indulged in treachery and graft.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，有罪伏誅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year, guilty, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 16 he was found guilty and executed.

sentences.zh: 緯初為大興教諭，燕兵起，與城守有勞。

translations.literal: Wei at first was instructor of Daxing; when the Yan army rose he had merit in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wei was first an instructor in Daxing; when the Yan army rose he distinguished himself in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 擢禮科給事中，坐罪謫思南宣慰司教授。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section; on account of an offense he was demoted to professor of the Sinan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section, he was later demoted to professor in Sinan for an offense.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，復原官，務捃摭朝士過。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle he was restored to his original office and devoted himself to gathering and exposing court officials' faults.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 7 he was restored to office and devoted himself to exposing court officials' faults.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷浙江副使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was made vice commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，仁宗見其名曰：「此人尚在耶！

translations.literal: Later he entered court; Renzong saw his name and said: 'This man is still alive!'
translations.idiomatic: When he later came to court, Renzong saw his name and exclaimed, 'This man is still alive!'

sentences.zh: 是無異蛇蠍。

translations.literal: He is no different from snakes and scorpions.
translations.idiomatic: He is no different from a snake or scorpion.

sentences.zh: 」遂謫嘉興典史。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to recorder of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to recorder of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 芳，潁上人。

translations.literal: Fang was a man of Yingshang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang was a native of Yingshang.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Yongle year 13.

sentences.zh: 曆刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He served as supervising secretary of the Penal Section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supervising secretary of the Penal Section.

sentences.zh: 宣宗數禦便殿，與大臣議事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong often attended the side hall and discussed affairs with great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong often met ministers in the side hall to discuss policy.

sentences.zh: 芳言：「洪武中，大臣面議時政，必給事中二人與俱，請復其舊。

translations.literal: Fang said: 'In the Hongwu reign, when great ministers discussed current affairs face to face, two supervising secretaries always accompanied them; I beg that this old practice be restored.'
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, 'Under Hongwu, two supervising secretaries always attended when ministers discussed policy with the emperor face to face—I beg that practice be restored.'

sentences.zh: 」帝是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 芳輒自矜，百司所為，少不如意，即詣帝前奏之，人比之紀綱。

translations.literal: Fang then prided himself on it; whatever the hundred offices did, if it was slightly not to his liking he would go before the emperor and memorialize it; people compared him to Ji Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang grew arrogant; at the slightest dissatisfaction with any department he ran to the emperor; men compared him to Ji Gang.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝亦惡其奸，黜為海鹽丞，棄官歸。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor also hated his treachery, demoted him to assistant magistrate of Haiyan, and he abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor came to loathe him, demoted him to assistant magistrate of Haiyan, and he resigned.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩，字惟中，分宜人。

translations.literal: Yan Song, style Weizhong, was a man of Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, courtesy name Weizhong, was a native of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 長身戍削，疏眉目，大音聲。

translations.literal: Tall in stature and lean, with sparse brows and eyes and a loud voice.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and lean, with sparse features and a booming voice.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治十八年進士，改庶起士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi, was changed to a commoner graduate of the Hanlin, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Hongzhi year 18, entered the Hanlin as a commoner graduate, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸，讀書鈐山十年，為詩古文辭，頗著清譽。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home, reading books at Qianshan for ten years, composing poetry and ancient-style prose, and gained a fair reputation for purity.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness and read at Qianshan for ten years, writing poetry and prose that won him a reputation for refinement.

sentences.zh: 還朝，久之進侍講，署南京翰林院事。

translations.literal: Returning to court, after a long time he was advanced to attendant expositor and acted in the affairs of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was eventually made attendant expositor and acting head of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 召為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was summoned as chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年曆禮部右侍郎，奉世宗命祭告顯陵，還言：「臣恭上寶冊及奉安神床，皆應時雨霽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he served as vice minister of the right in the Ministry of Rites; obeying Shizong's command he performed sacrificial announcement at the Xianling tomb, and on returning said: 'Your servant respectfully presented the precious register and installed the spirit couch, and in both cases timely rain cleared.'
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 7, as vice minister of Rites he performed sacrifices at Xianling and reported, 'When I presented the precious register and installed the spirit couch, timely rain cleared each time.'

sentences.zh: 又石產棗陽，群鸛集繞，碑入漢江，河流驟漲。

translations.literal: Also stones produced jujubes at Yang, flocks of egrets gathered and circled, and when the stele entered the Han River the river suddenly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Stones at Yang bore jujube patterns, egrets flocked and circled, and when the stele entered the Han River the waters surged.

sentences.zh: 請命輔臣撰文刻石，以紀天眷。

translations.literal: He requested that assisting ministers draft an essay and carve it in stone to record Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that assisting ministers compose and carve an inscription to record Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部左侍郎，進南京禮部尚書，改吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to minister of Rites at Nanjing, and changed to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became left vice minister of Personnel, then minister of Rites at Nanjing, then minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 居南京五年，以賀萬壽節至京師。

translations.literal: He remained at Nanjing five years, and came to the capital for the imperial birthday celebration.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in Nanjing he came to the capital for the imperial birthday.

sentences.zh: 會廷議更修《宋史》，輔臣請留嵩以禮部尚書兼翰林學士董其事。

translations.literal: When the court discussed revising the History of Song, assisting ministers requested that Song be kept as minister of Rites concurrently with Hanlin academician to direct the work.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated revising the History of Song, ministers asked that Song stay as minister of Rites and Hanlin academician to direct it.

sentences.zh: 及夏言入內閣，命嵩還掌部事。

translations.literal: When Xia Yan entered the Grand Secretariat, Song was ordered back to manage the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yan entered the Grand Secretariat, Song was ordered back to run the ministry.

sentences.zh: 帝將祀獻皇帝明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to sacrifice to the late Emperor Xian in the Bright Hall, paired with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to sacrifice to Emperor Xian in the Bright Hall, paired with the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 已，又欲稱宗入太廟。

translations.literal: Thereafter he also wished to enshrine him as an ancestor in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to enshrine him as an ancestor in the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 嵩與群臣議沮之，帝不悅，著《明堂或問》示廷臣。

translations.literal: Song and the court ministers discussed and obstructed this; the emperor was displeased and issued Clarifying Questions on the Bright Hall to show the court.
translations.idiomatic: Song and the ministers opposed this; the emperor was displeased and issued Clarifying Questions on the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 嵩惶恐，盡改前說，條畫禮儀甚備。

translations.literal: Song was fearful and completely changed his former view, setting forth the ritual in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Song panicked, reversed his position entirely, and laid out the rites in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 禮成，賜金幣。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, gold and silk were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were done, he received gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 自是，益務為佞悅。

translations.literal: From this time he all the more strove to flatter and please.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he flattered the emperor all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝上皇天上帝尊號、寶冊，尋加上高皇帝尊諡聖號以配，嵩乃奏慶雲見，請受群臣朝賀。

translations.literal: When the emperor bestowed the honorific title and precious register of the Supreme Lord of Heaven, and soon added the honorific sage title of the High Emperor for pairing, Song then memorialized that auspicious clouds had appeared and requested that the court ministers offer congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor bestowed titles on the Supreme Lord and paired the High Emperor, Song reported auspicious clouds and asked ministers to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 又為《慶雲賦》、《大禮告成頌》奏之，帝悅，命付史館。

translations.literal: He also composed 'Rhapsody on Auspicious Clouds' and 'Ode on the Completion of the Great Rites' and memorialized them; the emperor was pleased and ordered them sent to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a rhapsody and an ode on the great rites; the emperor was pleased and sent them to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保，從幸承天，賞賜與輔臣埒。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, accompanied the emperor to Chengtian, and rewards equaled those of assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, accompanied the emperor to Chengtian, and received rewards equal to grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 嵩歸日驕。

translations.literal: When Song returned he grew arrogant day by day.
translations.idiomatic: After returning, Song grew daily more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 諸宗籓請恤乞封，挾取賄賂。

translations.literal: Princes of the imperial clan who requested condolence or enfeoffment were squeezed for bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen seeking favors were extorted for bribes.

sentences.zh: 子世蕃又數關說諸曹。

translations.literal: His son Shifan also repeatedly intervened in the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifan also repeatedly intervened in government bureaus.

sentences.zh: 南北給事、御史交章論貪污大臣，皆首嵩。

translations.literal: Northern and southern supervising secretaries and censors in succession memorialized on corrupt great ministers, all naming Song first.
translations.idiomatic: Censors north and south repeatedly impeached corrupt ministers, always naming Song first.

sentences.zh: 嵩每被論，亟歸誠於帝，事輒已。

translations.literal: Whenever Song was impeached he quickly professed loyalty to the emperor and the matter would end.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever impeached, Song quickly professed loyalty to the emperor and the matter died.

sentences.zh: 帝或以事諮嵩，所條對平無奇，帝必故稱賞，欲以諷止言者。

translations.literal: When the emperor sometimes consulted Song on affairs, his answers were flat and unremarkable, yet the emperor would deliberately praise them, wishing to use this to admonish and stop the speakers.
translations.idiomatic: When consulted, his answers were dull, yet the emperor deliberately praised them to silence critics.

sentences.zh: 嵩科第先夏言，而位下之。

translations.literal: Song's examination cohort preceded Xia Yan's, yet his rank was below Yan's.
translations.idiomatic: Song had passed the examinations before Xia Yan, yet ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 始倚言，事之謹，嘗置酒邀言，躬詣其第，言辭不見。

translations.literal: At first he relied on Yan, serving him carefully; he once set out wine to invite Yan and personally went to his house, but Yan declined to see him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he relied on Yan, serving him humbly; he once brought wine to Yan's door, but Yan refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 嵩布席，展所具啟，跽讀。

translations.literal: Song spread his mat, displayed the memorials he had prepared, and knelt to read them.
translations.idiomatic: Song spread his mat, laid out his prepared memorials, and knelt to read them aloud.

sentences.zh: 言謂嵩實下己，不疑也。

translations.literal: Yan thought Song was truly beneath himself and did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan believed Song was genuinely his inferior and suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝以奉道嘗御香葉冠，因刻沈水香冠五，賜言等。

translations.literal: Because the emperor practiced the Way he once wore a crown of fragrant leaves; he then carved five crowns of sinking-water incense and bestowed them on Yan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, practicing Daoism, wore a crown of fragrant leaves and carved five incense crowns for Yan and others.

sentences.zh: 言不奉詔，帝怒甚。

translations.literal: Yan did not obey the edict; the emperor was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused the edict; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 嵩因召對冠之，籠以輕紗。

translations.literal: Song therefore wore the crown when summoned to audience, covering it with light gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Song wore the crown at his next audience, veiled in light gauze.

sentences.zh: 帝見，益內親嵩。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw this he was all the more inwardly close to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as devotion and drew closer to Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩遂傾言，斥之。

translations.literal: Song then overturned Yan and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Song then turned on Yan and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 言去，醮祀青詞，非嵩無當帝意者。

translations.literal: When Yan left, for Daoist rituals and green-lotus prayers none but Song suited the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan gone, only Song could write the Daoist prayers the emperor wanted.

sentences.zh: 二十一年八月拜武英殿大學士，入直文淵閣，仍掌禮部事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, entered the Wenyuan Pavilion in attendance, and still managed the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 21 he was made grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, entered the Wenyuan Pavilion, and still ran the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時嵩年六十餘矣。

translations.literal: At this time Song was already more than sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Song was already past sixty.

sentences.zh: 精爽溢發，不異少壯。

translations.literal: His spirit overflowed with vigor, no different from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His vigor seemed undiminished by age.

sentences.zh: 朝夕直西苑板房，未嘗一歸洗沐，帝益謂嵩勤。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he attended the plank rooms of the Western Garden and never once returned home to bathe; the emperor all the more thought Song diligent.
translations.idiomatic: He attended the Western Garden morning and night without returning home to bathe; the emperor deemed him ever more diligent.

sentences.zh: 久之，請解部事，遂專直西苑。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested to be relieved of ministry affairs and then attended only at the Western Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he resigned the ministry and attended only at the Western Garden.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜嵩銀記，文曰「忠勤敏達。

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed on Song a silver tally inscribed: Loyal, diligent, keen, and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a silver tally inscribed Loyal, diligent, keen, and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 」尋加太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 翟鑾資序在嵩上，帝待之不如嵩。

translations.literal: Zhai Luan's seniority in office was above Song's, yet the emperor treated him less well than Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Luan outranked Song, yet the emperor favored Song more.

sentences.zh: 嵩諷言官論之，鑾得罪去。

translations.literal: Song incited censors to impeach him, and Luan was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Song incited censors against him and Luan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書許贊、禮部尚書張璧同入閣，皆不預聞票擬事，政事一歸嵩。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Xu Zan and Minister of Rites Zhang Bi entered the Grand Secretariat together, yet neither took part in drafting rescripts; government affairs all returned to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zan and Zhang Bi joined the Grand Secretariat but neither drafted rescripts; power rested entirely with Song.

sentences.zh: 贊嘗歎曰：「何奪我吏部，使我旁睨人。

translations.literal: Zan once sighed and said: Why take my ministry from me and make me watch others from the side.
translations.idiomatic: Zan once sighed, Why strip me of the ministry and leave me watching from the sidelines?

sentences.zh: 」嵩欲示厚同列，且塞言者意，因以顯夏言短，乃請凡有宣召，乞與成國公硃希忠、京山侯崔元及贊、璧偕入，如祖宗朝謇、夏、三楊故事，帝不聽，然心益喜嵩，累進吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士、少傅兼太子太師。

translations.literal: Song wished to show generosity to colleagues and also to stop the speakers' mouths; because he wished to expose Xia Yan's faults, he requested that whenever there was an imperial summons he enter together with Marquis Zhu Xizhong of Chengguo, Marquis Cui Yuan of Jingshan, and Zan and Bi, as in the Hongwu reign when Yan, Xia, and the three Yangs were summoned—but the emperor did not listen; yet in his heart he was all the more pleased with Song, and repeatedly promoted him to minister of Personnel, grand secretary of the Hall of Prudent Conduct, junior tutor and grand preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
