translations.idiomatic: To appear generous and silence critics while exposing Xia Yan's faults, Song asked to enter audiences with Zhu Xizhong, Cui Yuan, Zan, and Bi as in Hongwu times; the emperor refused but liked him more, promoting him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝微覺嵩橫。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor slightly perceived Song's overbearing conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor sensed Song's arrogance.

sentences.zh: 時贊老病罷，璧死，乃復用夏言，帝為加嵩少師以慰之。

translations.literal: At this time Zan was old and ill and retired, Bi died, and Xia Yan was again employed; the emperor added Song as junior master to console him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zan retired ill and Bi died, Xia Yan returned; the emperor made Song junior master to console him.

sentences.zh: 言至，復盛氣陵嵩，頗斥逐其黨，嵩不能救。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived he again bore down on Song with overbearing air and drove out many of his faction; Song could not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan returned in triumph, humbled Song, and expelled his followers; Song could not protect them.

sentences.zh: 子世蕃方官尚寶少卿，橫行公卿間。

translations.literal: His son Shifan was then junior director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and swaggered among the nobles and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifan, junior director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, bullied officials freely.

sentences.zh: 言欲發其罪，嵩父子大懼，長跪榻下泣謝，乃已。

translations.literal: Yan wished to expose his crimes; the Song father and son were greatly afraid, knelt long at the couch and wept in apology, and Yan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan threatened to expose Shifan's crimes, father and son knelt weeping at his couch until Yan relented.

sentences.zh: 知陸炳與言惡，遂與比而傾言。

translations.literal: Knowing that Lu Bing hated Yan, he then allied with Bing to overturn Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Lu Bing hated Yan, Song allied with him to destroy Yan.

sentences.zh: 世蕃遷太常少卿，嵩猶畏言，疏遣歸省墓。

translations.literal: Shifan was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Song still feared Yan and memorialized sending him home to sweep the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan was made vice minister of Imperial Sacrifices; Song still feared Yan and sent him home to tend the family tomb.

sentences.zh: 嵩尋加特進，再加華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: Song was soon given special advancement and again made grand secretary of the Hall of Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Song soon received special advancement and became grand secretary of the Hall of Canopy.

sentences.zh: 窺言失帝眷，用河套事構言及曾銑，俱棄市。

translations.literal: Seeing that Yan had lost the emperor's favor, he used the Ordos affair to frame Yan and Zeng Xu, and both were executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan lost favor, Song framed him and Zeng Xu over the Ordos affair; both were executed.

sentences.zh: 已而南京吏部尚書張治、國子祭酒李本以疏遠擢入閣，益不敢預可否。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Zhi, minister of Personnel at Nanjing, and Li Ben, chancellor of the Imperial Academy, were promoted into the Grand Secretariat from afar and dared still less to approve or disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi and Li Ben were soon promoted into the Grand Secretariat from distant posts and dared not contradict him.

sentences.zh: 嵩既傾殺言，益偽恭謹。

translations.literal: After Song had overturned and killed Yan he was all the more falsely respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Having destroyed Yan, Song feigned humility all the more.

sentences.zh: 言嘗加上柱國，帝亦欲加嵩，嵩乃辭曰：「尊無二上，上非人臣所宜稱。

translations.literal: Yan had once been given the title Pillar of the State; the emperor also wished to give it to Song; Song then declined, saying: In honor there is no second above; above is not what a subject should be called.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been made Pillar of the State; when the emperor offered Song the same title, he declined: Honor admits no second; above is not for subjects.

sentences.zh: 國初雖設此官，左相國達，功臣第一，亦止為左柱國。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty this office was indeed established, yet the left chancellor Guo Da and the first among meritorious officials received only the left Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Though the title existed at the founding, even Guo Da received only left Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下免臣此官，著為令典，以昭臣節。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to spare me this office and establish it as a statutory model to display a minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to spare me this title and fix it as precedent for ministers' integrity.

sentences.zh: 」帝大喜，允其辭，而以世蕃為太常卿。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, granted his request, and made Shifan director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, granted his request, and made Shifan director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嵩無他才略，惟一意媚上，竊權罔利。

translations.literal: Song had no other talent or strategy; he devoted himself solely to flattering the emperor and usurping power for private profit.
translations.idiomatic: Song had no real talent—only flattery, usurped power, and private gain.

sentences.zh: 帝英察自信，果刑戮，頗護己短，嵩以故得因事激帝怒，戕害人以成其私。

translations.literal: The emperor was sharp and self-confident, severe in punishment, and quite protective of his own faults; Song therefore could by affairs stir the emperor's anger and harm people to accomplish his private ends.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was sharp, severe, and touchy about his faults; Song exploited this to destroy enemies.

sentences.zh: 張經、李天寵、王忬之死，嵩皆有力焉。

translations.literal: The deaths of Zhang Jing, Li Tianchong, and Wang Yu—Song had power in all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Song had a hand in the deaths of Zhang Jing, Li Tianchong, and Wang Yu.

sentences.zh: 前後劾嵩、世蕃者，謝瑜、葉經、童漢臣、趙錦、王宗茂、何維柏、王曄、陳塏、厲汝進、沈練、徐學詩、楊繼盛、周鈇、吳時來、張翀、董傳策皆被譴。

translations.literal: Those who before and after impeached Song and Shifan—Xie Yu, Ye Jing, Tong Hanchen, Zhao Jin, Wang Zongmao, He Weibo, Wang Ye, Chen Kai, Li Rujin, Shen Lian, Xu Xueshi, Yang Jisheng, Zhou Fu, Wu Shilai, Zhang Chong, and Dong Chuance—were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who impeached Song and Shifan—including Xie Yu, Ye Jing, Yang Jisheng, and Dong Chuance—were all punished.

sentences.zh: 經、煉用他過置之死，繼盛附張經疏尾殺之。

translations.literal: Jing and Lian were put to death on other pretexts; Jisheng was killed appended to Zhang Jing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Lian died on other charges; Jisheng was killed appended to Zhang Jing's memorial.

sentences.zh: 他所不悅，假遷除考察以斥者甚眾，皆未嘗有跡也。

translations.literal: Whomever he disliked he falsely removed through transfer, evaluation, and inspection in great numbers, yet there was never any trace.
translations.idiomatic: Others he removed through transfers and evaluations without a trace of cause.

sentences.zh: 俺答薄都城，慢書求貢。

translations.literal: Altan Khan pressed on the capital and in an insolent letter requested tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan threatened the capital and insolently demanded tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝召嵩與李本及禮部尚書徐階入對西苑。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Song, Li Ben, and Minister of Rites Xu Jie to audience in the Western Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Song, Li Ben, and Xu Jie to the Western Garden.

sentences.zh: 嵩無所規畫，委之禮部。

translations.literal: Song had no plan and left it to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Song offered no plan and deferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝悉用階言，稍輕嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Jie's words entirely and slightly slighted Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Xu Jie's advice and valued Song less.

sentences.zh: 嵩復以間激帝怒，杖司業趙貞吉而謫之。

translations.literal: Song again used an opportunity to stir the emperor's anger, had the director of studies Zhao Zhenji beaten and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Song again inflamed the emperor's anger and had Zhao Zhenji beaten and banished.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書丁汝夔受嵩指，不敢趣諸將戰。

translations.literal: Minister of War Ding Ruai received Song's instruction and dared not urge the generals to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Ding Ruai, under Song's orders, dared not press the generals to fight.

sentences.zh: 寇退，帝欲殺汝夔。

translations.literal: When the bandits retreated the emperor wished to kill Ruai.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew the emperor wanted Ruai executed.

sentences.zh: 嵩懼其引己，謂汝夔曰：「我在，毋慮也。

translations.literal: Song feared he would implicate him and said to Ruai: While I am here, have no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Song feared Ruai would implicate him and said, While I am here, have no fear.

sentences.zh: 」汝夔臨死始知為嵩紿。

translations.literal: Only when Ruai was about to die did he know he had been deceived by Song.
translations.idiomatic: Ruai learned only at the scaffold that Song had deceived him.

sentences.zh: 大將軍仇鸞，始為曾銑所劾，倚嵩傾銑，遂約為父子。

translations.literal: The great general Qiu Luan had at first been impeached by Zeng Xu; relying on Song he overturned Xu, and they then agreed to be father and son.
translations.idiomatic: General Qiu Luan, once impeached by Zeng Xu, relied on Song to destroy Xu and treated him as a father.

sentences.zh: 已而鸞挾寇得帝重，嵩猶兒子蓄之，浸相惡。

translations.literal: Before long Luan leveraged the bandits to gain the emperor's weight; Song still kept him like a son, but gradually they came to hate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Luan then leveraged the raids to win favor; Song still treated him as a son until they grew hostile.

sentences.zh: 嵩密疏毀鸞，帝不聽，而頗納鸞所陳嵩父子過，少疏之。

translations.literal: Song secretly memorialized to slander Luan; the emperor did not listen, yet somewhat accepted Luan's reports of the Song father and son's faults and grew somewhat distant.
translations.idiomatic: Song secretly slandered Luan; the emperor ignored him but accepted Luan's reports of the Songs' faults and grew cooler.

sentences.zh: 嵩當入直，不召者數矣。

translations.literal: When Song should have entered attendance he was not summoned for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Song went days without summons to attendance.

sentences.zh: 嵩見徐階、李本入西內，即與俱入。

translations.literal: Seeing Xu Jie and Li Ben enter the inner palace, he entered together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xu Jie and Li Ben enter the inner palace, he went in with them.

sentences.zh: 至西華門，門者以非詔旨格之。

translations.literal: At the Xihua Gate the gatekeepers blocked them, saying there was no imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xihua Gate guards barred them for lack of an edict.

sentences.zh: 嵩還第，父子對泣。

translations.literal: Song returned home and father and son wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Song returned home and wept with his son.

sentences.zh: 時陸炳掌錦衣，與鸞爭寵，嵩乃結炳共圖鸞。

translations.literal: At this time Lu Bing controlled the Brocade Guard and vied with Luan for favor; Song then allied with Bing to plot against Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bing of the Brocade Guard rivaled Luan; Song allied with Bing against him.

sentences.zh: 會鸞病死，炳訐鸞陰事，帝追戮之。

translations.literal: It happened that Luan died of illness; Bing denounced Luan's secret affairs and the emperor pursued posthumous punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan died, Bing denounced his secret crimes and the emperor punished him posthumously.

sentences.zh: 於是益信任嵩，遣所乘龍舟過海子召嵩，載直西內如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he trusted Song all the more, sent his dragon boat across the sea to summon Song, and carried him straight into the inner palace as before.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted Song still more, sent his dragon boat to fetch him, and carried him into the inner palace as before.

sentences.zh: 世蕃尋遷工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Shifan was soon transferred to left vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan was soon made left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 倭寇江南，用趙文華督察軍情，大納賄賂以遣嵩，致寇亂益甚。

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates ravaged Jiangnan, Zhao Wenhua was used to supervise military affairs; he took great bribes to send to Song, and the bandit disorder grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenhua was sent to supervise the anti-pirate campaign; he bribed Song heavily and the raids grew worse.

sentences.zh: 及胡宗憲誘降汪直、徐海，文華乃言：「臣與宗憲策，臣師嵩所授也。

translations.literal: When Hu Zongxian induced Wang Zhi and Xu Hai to surrender, Wenhua then said: My strategies with Zongxian were taught me by my teacher Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Zongxian induced Wang Zhi and Xu Hai to surrender, Wenhua claimed the strategy came from his teacher Song.

sentences.zh: 」遂命嵩兼支尚書俸無謝，自是褒賜皆不謝。

translations.literal: He was then ordered that Song concurrently receive ministerial salary without thanks; from this time rewards were accepted without thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Song was granted ministerial salary without need for thanks; thereafter he accepted rewards without formal gratitude.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以嵩直廬隘，撤小殿材為營室，植花木其中，朝夕賜禦膳、法酒。

translations.literal: The emperor once found Song's duty room cramped, removed materials from a small hall to build quarters, planted flowers and trees, and morning and evening bestowed imperial meals and ritual wine.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Song's quarters cramped, the emperor built him new rooms with garden and daily imperial meals and wine.

sentences.zh: 嵩年八十，聽以肩輿入禁苑。

translations.literal: Song was eighty and permitted to enter the forbidden garden in a sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty Song was allowed a sedan chair in the forbidden garden.

sentences.zh: 帝自十八年葬章聖太后後，即不視朝，自二十年宮婢之變，即移居西苑萬壽宮，不入大內，大臣希得謁見，惟嵩獨承顧問，禦劄一日或數下，雖同列不獲聞，以故嵩得逞志。

translations.literal: After burying Empress Zhangsheng in year 18 the emperor ceased holding court; after the palace-women incident in year 20 he moved to the Wanshou Palace in the Western Garden and did not enter the great inner palace; great ministers rarely obtained audience; only Song received consultation; imperial notes came one or several a day that even colleagues did not hear—thus Song could carry out his will.
translations.idiomatic: After year 18 the emperor stopped holding court; after year 20 he lived only in the Western Garden; ministers rarely saw him; only Song received his notes and could do as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 然帝雖甚親禮嵩，亦不盡信其言，間一取獨斷，或故示異同，欲以殺離其勢。

translations.literal: Yet though the emperor was very intimate and courteous to Song, he did not fully believe his words; occasionally he took independent decisions or deliberately showed disagreement, wishing to break up their power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor did not fully trust Song, sometimes deciding alone or feigning disagreement to divide his power.

sentences.zh: 嵩父子獨得帝窾要，欲有所救解，嵩必順帝意痛詆之，而婉曲解釋以中帝所不忍。

translations.literal: The Song father and son alone grasped the emperor's inner intent; when they wished to save someone Song would first fiercely denounce him as the emperor wished, then gently explain to hit what the emperor could not bear to do.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Songs knew the emperor's mind; to save a man Song would first denounce him harshly, then gently intercede.

sentences.zh: 即欲排陷者，必先稱其善，而以微言中之，或觸帝所恥與諱。

translations.literal: When they wished to entrap someone they would first praise his virtues and then strike with subtle words, or touch what the emperor was ashamed of or tabooed.
translations.idiomatic: To destroy a man they first praised him, then struck with a subtle phrase touching the emperor's shame or taboo.

sentences.zh: 以是移帝喜怒，往往不失。

translations.literal: Thus they shifted the emperor's joy and anger and often did not miss.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they steered the emperor's moods with uncanny success.

sentences.zh: 士大夫輻輳附嵩，時稱文選郎中萬寀、職方郎中方祥等為嵩文武管家。

translations.literal: Officials clustered to attach to Song; at the time Wan Cai of the Ministry of Personnel and Fang Xiang of the Bureau of Military Appointments were called Song's civil and military stewards.
translations.idiomatic: Officials flocked to Song; Wan Cai and Fang Xiang were called his civil and military stewards.

sentences.zh: 尚書吳鵬、歐陽必進、高燿、許論輩，皆惴惴事嵩。

translations.literal: Ministers Wu Peng, Ouyang Bijin, Gao Yao, Xu Lun, and their kind all served Song in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Wu Peng, Ouyang Bijin, Gao Yao, and Xu Lun all served Song in terror.

sentences.zh: 嵩握權久，遍引私人居要地。

translations.literal: Song held power long and everywhere introduced private persons to important posts.
translations.idiomatic: Long in power, Song placed his men in every key post.

sentences.zh: 帝亦浸厭之，而漸親徐階。

translations.literal: The emperor also gradually grew tired of him and gradually drew close to Xu Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tired of him and drew closer to Xu Jie.

sentences.zh: 會階所厚吳時來、張翀、董傳策各疏論嵩，嵩因密請究主使者，下詔獄，窮治無所引。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Shilai, Zhang Chong, and Dong Chuance, whom Jie favored, each memorialized against Song; Song therefore secretly requested investigation of the ringleaders; they were sent to the imperial prison and pressed to the end but implicated no one.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie's allies memorialized against Song, Song had them imprisoned but could find no ringleader.

sentences.zh: 帝乃不問，而慰留嵩，然心不能無動，階因得間傾嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor then did not inquire further but comforted and kept Song; yet in his heart he could not be unmoved, and Jie thus found openings to overturn Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured Song but was shaken; Jie found openings against him.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書缺，嵩力援歐陽必進為之，甫三月即斥去。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Personnel was vacant Song strongly supported Ouyang Bijin for it; in only three months he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Song installed Ouyang Bijin as minister of Personnel; within three months he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 趙文華忤旨獲譴，嵩亦不能救。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenhua offended the edict and was punished; Song also could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenhua offended the emperor and was punished; Song could not save him.

sentences.zh: 有詔二王就婚邸第，嵩力請留內。

translations.literal: There was an edict that the two princes go to their wedding residences; Song strongly requested they remain within.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the two princes to their wedding residences; Song begged they stay in the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，嵩亦不能力持。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; Song also could not hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; Song could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 嵩雖警敏，能先意揣帝指，然帝所下手詔，語多不可曉，惟世蕃一覽了然，答語無不中。

translations.literal: Though Song was alert and could anticipate the emperor's intent, the emperor's handwritten edicts were often incomprehensible; only Shifan understood at a glance and answered without missing.
translations.idiomatic: Song could read the emperor's mood, but the emperor's own edicts were often obscure; only Shifan understood them instantly.

sentences.zh: 及嵩妻歐陽氏死，世蕃當護喪歸，嵩請留侍京邸。

translations.literal: When Song's wife Lady Ouyang died Shifan should have returned for mourning; Song requested he remain to serve in the capital residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Ouyang died Shifan should have mourned at home; Song kept him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，然自是不得入直所代嵩票擬，而日縱淫樂於家。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted it, but from this time he could not enter attendance to draft rescripts for Song and daily indulged in music and women at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, but Shifan no longer drafted for his father and indulged himself at home.

sentences.zh: 嵩受詔多不能答，遣使持問世蕃。

translations.literal: Song often could not answer edicts and sent messengers to ask Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Song could not answer edicts and sent to ask Shifan.

sentences.zh: 值其方耽女樂，不以時答。

translations.literal: When he was deep in female entertainments he did not answer in time.
translations.idiomatic: Absorbed in entertainment, Shifan answered late.

sentences.zh: 中使相繼促嵩，嵩不得已自為之，往往失旨。

translations.literal: Eunuchs came in succession to urge Song; Song had no choice but to answer himself and often missed the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs pressed Song; he answered himself and often missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 所進青詞，又多假手他人不能工，經此積失帝歡。

translations.literal: The green-lotus prayers submitted were also mostly drafted by others and not skillful; through this he accumulated loss of the emperor's pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: His prayers were drafted by others and grew clumsy; the emperor's favor waned.

sentences.zh: 會萬壽宮火，嵩請暫徙南城離宮，南城，英宗為太上皇時所居也，帝不悅。

translations.literal: When the Wanshou Palace burned Song requested temporary removal to the separate palace of the southern city; the southern city was where Emperor Yingzong lived as retired emperor; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanshou Palace burned Song asked to move to the southern city where Yingzong had lived; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 而徐階營萬壽營甚稱旨，帝益親階，顧問多不及嵩，即及嵩，祠祀而已。

translations.literal: Xu Jie's rebuilding of Wanshou won great approval; the emperor drew still closer to Jie; consultation often did not reach Song, and when it reached Song it was only sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie's rebuilding pleased the emperor; consultation passed Song by except for rituals.

sentences.zh: 嵩懼，置酒要階，使家人羅拜，舉觴屬曰：「嵩旦夕且死，此曹惟公乳哺之。

translations.literal: Song was afraid, set out wine to invite Jie, had his household kowtow in a row, raised his cup and entrusted: Song will soon die; these people rely only on you to nurse them.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Song feasted Jie, had his household kowtow, and begged him to protect his family after death.

sentences.zh: 」階謝不敢。

translations.literal: Jie declined and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jie humbly refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝入方士藍道行言，有意去嵩。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor, through the Daoist Lan Daoxing, showed intention to remove Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, through the Daoist Lan Daoxing, the emperor showed he meant to remove Song.

sentences.zh: 御史鄒應龍避雨內侍家，知其事，抗疏極論嵩父子不法，曰：「臣言不實，乞斬臣首以謝嵩、世蕃。

translations.literal: Censor Zou Yinglong, avoiding rain at an eunuch's house, learned of this and submitted a bold memorial fiercely discussing the Song father and son's unlawfulness, saying: If my words are untrue I beg my head be cut off to apologize to Song and Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zou Yinglong learned of the plot and memorialized fiercely, offering his head if he lied.

sentences.zh: 」帝降旨慰嵩，而以嵩溺愛世蕃，負眷倚，令致仕，馳驛歸，有司歲給米百石，下世蕃於理。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict comforting Song, yet because Song doted on Shifan and betrayed trust ordered him to retire and return by courier post with a hundred piculs of grain yearly; Shifan was handed to the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted Song but ordered him to retire for indulging Shifan; Shifan was sent to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 嵩為世蕃請罪，且求解，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Song pleaded Shifan's crime and asked release; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Song pleaded for Shifan; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 法司奏論世蕃及其子錦衣鵠、鴻，客羅龍文，戍邊遠。

translations.literal: The judiciary memorialized judgment on Shifan and his sons the brocade-guard Hong and Hong, and the client Luo Longwen, to garrison the far frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The judiciary sentenced Shifan, his sons, and client Luo Longwen to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，特宥鴻為民，使侍嵩，而錮其奴嚴年於獄，擢應龍通政司參議。

translations.literal: The edict followed this but specially pardoned Hong to be a commoner to serve Song, while imprisoning the slave Yan Nian and promoting Yinglong to Secretariat participant.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed, pardoned one son to serve Song, imprisoned the slave Yan Nian, and promoted Yinglong.

sentences.zh: 時四十一年五月也。

translations.literal: This was the fifth month of the forty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fifth month of year 41.

sentences.zh: 龍文官中書，交關為奸利，而年最黠惡，士大夫競稱萼山先生者也。

translations.literal: Longwen was a Secretariat drafter who traded for illicit profit; Nian was the most cunning and evil; officials vied to call him Mr. Eshan.
translations.idiomatic: Longwen traded in office; the slave Nian was the vilest; officials called him Mr. Eshan.

sentences.zh: 嵩既去，帝追念其贊玄功，意忽忽不樂，諭階欲遂傳位，退居西內，專祈長生。

translations.literal: After Song left the emperor recalled his service in the Mystic Way and was restless; he told Jie he wished to abdicate, retire to the inner west, and seek long life alone.
translations.idiomatic: After Song left the emperor missed his Daoist service and told Jie he wished to abdicate and seek immortality.

sentences.zh: 階極陳河，帝曰：「卿等不欲，必皆奉君命，同輔玄修乃可。

translations.literal: Jie strongly argued against it; the emperor said: If you do not wish it you must all obey the ruler's command and jointly assist in mystic cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Jie objected; the emperor said all must assist his mystic cultivation.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩既退，其子世蕃已伏法，敢更言者，並應龍俱斬。

translations.literal: Song has retired and Shifan is executed; whoever speaks again, together with Yinglong, shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Song is gone and Shifan dead; whoever speaks again, with Yinglong, shall die.

sentences.zh: 」嵩知帝念己，乃賂帝左右，發道行陰事，系刑部，俾引階。

translations.literal: Song knew the emperor missed him and bribed those around him, exposing Daoxing's secret affairs; he was sent to the Ministry of Justice to implicate Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Song bribed the emperor's attendants to expose Daoxing and implicate Jie.

sentences.zh: 道行不承，坐論死，得釋。

translations.literal: Daoxing did not confess; sentenced to death, he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxing refused to implicate Jie; sentenced to death, he was released.

sentences.zh: 嵩初歸至南昌，值萬壽節，使道士藍田玉建醮鐵柱宮。

translations.literal: When Song first returned to Nanchang it was the imperial birthday; he had the Daoist Lan Tianyu perform rituals at the Iron Pillar Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Nanchang for the birthday, Song had Lan Tianyu perform rituals.

sentences.zh: 田玉善召鶴，嵩因取其符籙，並己祈鶴文上之，帝優詔褒答。

translations.literal: Tianyu was skilled at summoning cranes; Song took his talismans and his own crane-prayer text and memorialized them; the emperor replied with gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent Tianyu's talismans and a crane prayer; the emperor replied graciously.

sentences.zh: 嵩因言：「臣年八十有四，惟一子世蕃及孫鵠皆遠戍，乞移便地就養，終臣餘年。

translations.literal: Song therefore said: Your servant is eighty-four; I have only one son Shifan and grandson Hong both exiled far; I beg they be moved to a convenient place to support me in my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: Song begged that Shifan and his grandson be moved nearer so he could be supported in old age.

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 其明年，南京御史林潤奏：「江洋巨盜多入逃軍羅龍文、嚴世蕃家。

translations.literal: The next year Nanjing Censor Lin Run memorialized: Great river-and-sea bandits mostly flee into the homes of deserter Luo Longwen and Yan Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing censor Lin Run reported that pirates sheltered with Luo Longwen and Yan Shifan.

sentences.zh: 龍文居深山，乘軒衣蟒，有負險不臣之志。

translations.literal: Longwen lived deep in the mountains, rode in sedan chairs and wore python robes, and had the will of one who relies on danger and will not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Longwen lived in the mountains in python robes with the air of a rebel.

sentences.zh: 世蕃得罪後，與龍文日誹謗時政。

translations.literal: After Shifan's offense he and Longwen daily slandered current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Shifan's fall he and Longwen daily slandered the government.

sentences.zh: 其治第役眾四千，道路皆言兩人通倭，變且不測。

translations.literal: In building his residence he used four thousand laborers; on the roads all said the two communicated with Japanese pirates and rebellion might come at any time.
translations.idiomatic: He employed four thousand builders; rumor said he colluded with Japanese pirates.

sentences.zh: 」詔下潤逮捕，下法司論斬，皆伏誅，黜嵩及諸孫皆為民。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Run to arrest them; the judiciary judged decapitation and all were executed; Song and his grandsons were demoted to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Run arrested them; all were executed; Song and his grandsons were made commoners.

sentences.zh: 嵩竊政二十年，溺信惡子，流毒天下，人咸指目為奸臣。

translations.literal: Song usurped government twenty years, blindly trusted his wicked son, and poison flowed through the realm; all pointed at him as a traitor minister.
translations.idiomatic: Song held power twenty years, trusted his wicked son, and was universally called a traitor.

sentences.zh: 其坐世蕃大逆，則徐階意也。

translations.literal: That he was charged with Shifan's great treason was Xu Jie's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of great treason against Shifan was Xu Jie's design.

sentences.zh: 又二年，嵩老病，寄食墓舍以死。

translations.literal: Two years later Song was old and ill, living on food at a tomb lodge until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the aged Song died in a tomb lodge.

sentences.zh: 世蕃，短項肥體，眇一目，由父任入仕。

translations.literal: Shifan had a short neck and fat body, one blind eye, and entered office through his father's appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan was short-necked, fat, one-eyed, and entered office through his father.

sentences.zh: 以築京師外城勞，由太常卿進工部左侍郎，仍掌尚寶司事。

translations.literal: For labor on the outer wall of the capital he was advanced from director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to left vice minister of Works while still managing the Court of Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: For building the outer wall he rose from director of Imperial Sacrifices to left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 剽悍陰賊，席父寵，招權利無厭。

translations.literal: Fierce, cruel, and treacherous, he relied on his father's favor and sought power and profit without end.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and treacherous, he abused his father's favor for endless gain.

sentences.zh: 然頗通國典，曉暢時務。

translations.literal: Yet he was fairly versed in state institutions and understood current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he knew the institutions and current affairs well.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂天下才，惟己與陸炳、楊博為三。

translations.literal: He once said the talents of the realm were only himself, Lu Bing, and Yang Bo—three.
translations.idiomatic: He said the empire had only three talents: himself, Lu Bing, and Yang Bo.

sentences.zh: 炳死，益自負。

translations.literal: When Bing died he was all the more self-important.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing died he grew still more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 嵩耄昏，且旦夕直西內，諸司白事，輒曰：「以質東樓。

translations.literal: Song was senile and attended the inner west morning and evening; when offices reported affairs he would say: Take it to East Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Senile Song attended the inner west daily and referred all business to East Tower.

sentences.zh: 」東樓，世蕃別號也。

translations.literal: East Tower was Shifan's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: East Tower was Shifan's nickname.

sentences.zh: 朝事一委世蕃，九卿以下浹日不得見，或停至暮而遣之。

translations.literal: Court affairs were entirely entrusted to Shifan; the nine ministers and below might not be seen for days, or be kept until evening and then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan ran everything; ministers might wait all day unseen.

sentences.zh: 士大夫側目屏息，不肖者奔走其門，筐篚相望於道。

translations.literal: Officials glared and held their breath; the unworthy rushed to his gate, gifts filling the road.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy feared him; the base crowded his gate with gifts.

sentences.zh: 世蕃熟諳中外官饒瘠險易，責賄多寡，毫髮不能匿。

translations.literal: Shifan knew whether officials at home and abroad were rich or poor, dangerous or safe, and how much bribe was due—nothing could be hidden.
translations.idiomatic: He knew every official's wealth and the bribe due—nothing was hidden.

sentences.zh: 其治第京師，連三四坊，堰水為塘數十畝，羅珍禽奇樹其中，日擁賓客縱倡樂，雖大僚或父執，虐之酒，不困不已。

translations.literal: His residence in the capital spanned three or four wards; he dammed water into ponds of dozens of acres, stocked with rare birds and strange trees; daily he entertained guests with music; even great officials or his father's peers he forced to drink until they could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His capital mansion spanned several wards with ponds and rare creatures; he forced even seniors to drink without mercy.

sentences.zh: 居母喪亦然。

translations.literal: Even during mourning for his mother it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He did the same even while mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 好古尊彝、奇器、書畫，趙文華、鄢懋卿、胡宗憲之屬，所到輒輦致之，或索之富人，必得然後已。

translations.literal: He loved ancient bronzes, curios, calligraphy, and painting; Zhao Wenhua, Yan Maoqing, Hu Zongxian, and their kind wherever they went carted them in, or extorted them from the rich until obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He extorted antiquities from Wenhua, Maoqing, Zongxian, and the rich.

sentences.zh: 被應龍劾戍雷州，未至而返，益大治園亭。

translations.literal: Impeached by Yinglong he was sent to garrison Leizhou, but before arriving he returned and all the more greatly built gardens and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Leizhou he turned back and built greater gardens.

sentences.zh: 其監工奴見袁州推官郭諫臣，不為起。

translations.literal: His overseer slaves saw Yuanzhou assistant magistrate Guo Jianchen and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His slaves would not rise for Assistant Magistrate Guo Jianchen.

sentences.zh: 御史林潤嘗劾懋卿，懼相報，因與諫臣謀發其罪，且及冤殺楊繼盛、沈練狀。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Run had once impeached Maoqing and feared reprisal; he therefore plotted with Jianchen to expose Shifan's crimes and also the wrongful deaths of Yang Jisheng and Shen Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Run, fearing Maoqing, joined Jianchen to expose Shifan and the murders of Yang Jisheng and Shen Lian.

sentences.zh: 世蕃喜，謂其黨曰：「無恐，獄且解。

translations.literal: Shifan rejoiced and told his faction: Do not fear—the case will be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan told his men the case would be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」法司黃光升等以讞詞白徐階，階曰：「諸公欲生之乎？

translations.literal: Huang Guangshang and others of the judiciary brought the indictment to Xu Jie; Jie said: Do you gentlemen wish him to live?
translations.idiomatic: The judiciary showed Jie the indictment; he asked whether they wanted Shifan to live.

sentences.zh: 」僉曰：「必欲死之。

translations.literal: All said: We must want him to die.
translations.idiomatic: All said they wanted him dead.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「若是，適所以生之也。

translations.literal: He said: If so, that is exactly how to let him live.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said that was exactly how to let him live.

sentences.zh: 夫楊、沈之獄，嵩皆巧取上旨。

translations.literal: The cases of Yang and Shen—Song cleverly took the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Song had taken the emperor's intent in the Yang and Shen cases.

sentences.zh: 今顯及之，是彰上過也。

translations.literal: Now making it explicit would display the emperor's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Making it explicit would expose the emperor's error.

sentences.zh: 必如是，諸君且不測，嚴公子騎款段出都門矣。

translations.literal: If so, you gentlemen would be in peril and Young Master Yan would ride a pony out the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Then they would be in danger and Shifan would ride free from the capital.

sentences.zh: 」為手削其草，獨按龍文與汪直姻舊，為交通賄世蕃乞官。

translations.literal: He personally revised the draft, charging only that Longwen was old kin of Wang Zhi and trafficked bribes to beg offices for Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Jie revised the charge to Longwen's ties with Wang Zhi and bribery for offices.

sentences.zh: 世蕃用彭孔言，以南昌倉地有王氣，取以治第，制擬王者。

translations.literal: Shifan used Peng Kongyan's claim that Nanchang granary land had kingly qi, took it to build a residence, and modeled it on a king.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan seized Nanchang granary land said to have kingly qi and built a princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 又結宗人典楧陰伺非常，多聚亡命。

translations.literal: He also joined clansman Dian Mu to watch for irregular events and gathered many fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: He joined clansmen to watch for rebellion and gathered fugitives.

sentences.zh: 龍文又招直餘黨五百人，謀為世蕃外投日本，先所發遣世蕃班頭牛信，亦自山海衛棄伍北走，誘致外兵，共相回應。

translations.literal: Longwen also recruited five hundred remnants of Zhi's party to plan that Shifan flee abroad to Japan; the foreman Niu Xin whom Shifan had earlier sent north also deserted and lured foreign troops in mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: Longwen recruited Zhi's remnants for Shifan to flee to Japan; the foreman Niu Xin deserted north to summon foreign troops.

sentences.zh: 即日令光升等疾書奏之。

translations.literal: That very day he ordered Guangshang and others to write and memorialize urgently.
translations.idiomatic: That day Jie ordered urgent memorialization.

sentences.zh: 世蕃聞，詫曰：「死矣。

translations.literal: When Shifan heard he exclaimed: Dead!
translations.idiomatic: Shifan heard and cried, Dead!

sentences.zh: 」遂斬於市。

translations.literal: He was then beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，黃金可三萬餘兩，白金二百萬餘兩，他珍寶服玩所值又數百萬。

translations.literal: His household was confiscated: gold of more than thirty thousand taels, silver of more than two million, other treasures, garments, and curios worth several million more.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscation yielded tens of thousands of taels of gold and millions in silver and treasures.

sentences.zh: 趙文華 等

translations.literal: Zhao Wenhua and others
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenhua and others

sentences.zh: 趙文華，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Wenhua was a man of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenhua was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing year 8.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以考察謫東平州同知。

translations.literal: On evaluation he was demoted to assistant prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation demoted him to assistant prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 久之，累官至通政使。

translations.literal: After a long time he rose in successive offices to commissioner of the Secretariat of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he became commissioner of the Secretariat of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 性傾狡，未第時在國學，嚴嵩為祭酒，才之。

translations.literal: By nature treacherous and cunning; before passing the examinations he was in the National University when Yan Song was chancellor and Song valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous by nature, he had impressed Song when Song was university chancellor.

sentences.zh: 後仕於朝，而嵩日貴幸，遂相與結為父子。

translations.literal: Later serving at court, as Song daily grew honored and favored, they joined as father and son.
translations.idiomatic: In court, as Song rose, they became sworn father and son.

sentences.zh: 嵩念己過惡多，得私人在通政，劾疏至，可預為計，故以文華任之。

translations.literal: Song thought his own faults many; with a private man in Transmission, when impeachment memorials arrived he could plan ahead—therefore he placed Wenhua there.
translations.idiomatic: Song placed him in Transmission to intercept impeachment memorials in advance.

sentences.zh: 文華欲自結於帝，進百華仙酒，詭曰：「臣師嵩服之而壽。

translations.literal: Wenhua wished to attach himself to the emperor and presented Hundred-Flower Immortal Wine, falsely saying: My teacher Song took it and lived long.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua presented Immortal Wine to the emperor, claiming Song's longevity came from it.

sentences.zh: 」帝飲甘之，手敕問嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor found it sweet and by hand-edict asked Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found it sweet and asked Song by personal edict.

sentences.zh: 嵩驚曰；

translations.literal: Song said in alarm:
translations.idiomatic: Song said in alarm:

sentences.zh: 「文華安得為此！

translations.literal: How could Wenhua do this!
translations.idiomatic: How could Wenhua do this!

sentences.zh: 」乃宛轉奏曰：「臣生平不近藥餌，犬馬之壽誠不知何以然。

translations.literal: He then tactfully memorialized: Your servant in life has never approached medicines; I truly do not know why I have the span of a dog or horse.
translations.idiomatic: He tactfully replied that he never took medicine and did not know why he lived so long.

sentences.zh: 」嵩恨文華不先白己，召至直所詈責之。

translations.literal: Song hated that Wenhua had not informed him first, summoned him to the duty room and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Song hated that Wenhua had not told him first and reviled him at the duty room.

sentences.zh: 文華跪泣，久不敢起。

translations.literal: Wenhua knelt weeping and long did not dare rise.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua knelt weeping and dared not rise.

sentences.zh: 徐階、李本見之為解，乃令去。

translations.literal: Xu Jie and Li Ben saw this and interceded, and he was then told to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie and Li Ben interceded and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 嵩休沐歸，九卿進謁，嵩猶怒文華，令從吏扶出之。

translations.literal: When Song rested and returned home the nine ministers came to audience; Song was still angry at Wenhua and ordered attendants to support him out.
translations.idiomatic: On rest day the nine ministers called; Song still raged and had Wenhua carried out.

sentences.zh: 文華大窘，厚賂嵩妻。

translations.literal: Wenhua was greatly embarrassed and bribed Song's wife heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua bribed Song's wife heavily.

sentences.zh: 嵩妻教文華伺嵩歸，匿於別室，酒酣，嵩妻為之解，文華即出拜，嵩乃待之如初。

translations.literal: Song's wife taught Wenhua to watch for Song's return, hide in a side room, and when wine was warm she interceded; Wenhua then came out to bow and Song treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Song's wife hid Wenhua, interceded when Song was drunk, and restored their bond.

sentences.zh: 以建議築京師外城，加工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: For proposing to build the outer wall of the capital he was added as right vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: For proposing the outer wall he was made right vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 東南倭患棘，文華獻七事。

translations.literal: Southeastern Japanese trouble was urgent; Wenhua presented seven measures.
translations.idiomatic: With Japanese raids urgent, Wenhua presented seven proposals.

sentences.zh: 首以祭海神為言，請遣官望祭於江陰、常熟。

translations.literal: The first spoke of sacrificing to the sea god and requested officials be sent to offer distant sacrifice at Jiangyin and Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: First he proposed sacrifices to the sea god at Jiangyin and Changshu.

sentences.zh: 次訟有司掩骼輕徭。

translations.literal: Next memorialized that officials cover exposed bones and lighten corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Next he urged covering exposed bones and lightening corvée.

sentences.zh: 次增募水軍。

translations.literal: Next increase recruitment of naval troops.
translations.idiomatic: Next he urged more naval recruits.

sentences.zh: 次蘇、松、常、鎮民田，一夫過百畝者，重科其賦，且預徵官田稅三年。

translations.literal: Next in Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang, for civilian fields where one man exceeded a hundred mu, heavily tax them and also levy official-field tax three years in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed heavy taxes on large holdings in the lower Yangtze and three-year advance levies.

sentences.zh: 次募富人輸財力自效，事寧論功。

translations.literal: Next recruit the rich to offer wealth and strength for merit when affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed recruiting rich donors for later reward.

sentences.zh: 次遣重臣督師。

translations.literal: Next send a weighty minister to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed sending a senior minister to supervise troops.

sentences.zh: 次招通番舊黨並海鹽徒，易以忠義之名，令偵伺賊情，因以為間。

translations.literal: Next recruit old associates of overseas trade and coastal salt smugglers, change them to the name of loyalty and righteousness, have them spy on bandit intelligence, and use them as agents.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed turning smugglers into spies against the pirates.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書聶豹議行其五事，惟增田賦、遣重臣二事不行。

translations.literal: Minister of War Nie Bao discussed implementing five; only increased land tax and sending a weighty minister were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Bao adopted five measures; increased land tax and a senior commander were rejected.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪豹官，而用嵩言即遣文華祭告海神，因察賊情。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, stripped Bao of office, and following Song's words immediately sent Wenhua to sacrifice to the sea god and inspect bandit conditions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Bao and sent Wenhua to sacrifice to the sea god and inspect the raids.

sentences.zh: 當是時，總督尚書張經方征四方及狼士兵，議大舉，自以位文華上，心輕之。

translations.literal: At this time Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing was campaigning with troops from the four directions and Lang soldiers and planned a great offensive; he thought himself above Wenhua in rank and looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing planned a major campaign and looked down on Wenhua.

sentences.zh: 文華不悅。

translations.literal: Wenhua was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua was displeased.

sentences.zh: 狼兵稍有斬獲功，文華厚犒之，使進剿，至漕涇戰敗，亡頭目十四人。

translations.literal: The Lang soldiers had some merit in beheading the enemy; Wenhua richly rewarded them and made them advance to attack; at Caojing they were defeated and fourteen commanders died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua rewarded Lang troops who were defeated at Caojing with fourteen commanders lost.

sentences.zh: 文華恚，數趣經進兵。

translations.literal: Wenhua was resentful and repeatedly urged Jing to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua repeatedly pressed Jing to attack.

sentences.zh: 經慮文華輕淺泄師期，不以告。

translations.literal: Jing feared Wenhua's shallowness would leak the campaign schedule and did not tell him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing feared Wenhua would leak plans and told him nothing.

sentences.zh: 文華益怒，劾經養寇失機，疏方上，經大捷王江涇。

translations.literal: Wenhua grew angrier, impeached Jing for nurturing bandits and missing the opportunity; as the memorial was going up Jing won a great victory at Wangjiangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua impeached Jing for delay just as Jing won at Wangjiangjing.

sentences.zh: 文華攘其功，謂己與巡按胡宗憲督師所致，經竟論死。

translations.literal: Wenhua seized the merit, saying he and Surveillance Commissioner Hu Zongxian had supervised the army to achieve it; Jing was in the end sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua claimed the victory for himself and Zongxian; Jing was executed.

sentences.zh: 又劾浙江巡撫李天寵罪，薦宗憲代，天寵亦論死。

translations.literal: He also impeached Zhejiang Grand Coordinator Li Tianchong and recommended Zongxian to replace him; Tianchong was also sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed Li Tianchong and installed Zongxian, who also had Tianchong executed.

sentences.zh: 帝益以文華為賢，命鑄督察軍務關防，即軍中賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor all the more thought Wenhua worthy and ordered casting of a seal for supervising military affairs, bestowed in camp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cast him a military supervision seal in camp.

sentences.zh: 文華自此出總督上，益恣行無忌。

translations.literal: From this time Wenhua stood above the grand coordinator and all the more acted without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua now outranked the grand coordinator and acted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 欲分蘇松巡撫曹邦輔滸墅關破賊功，不得，則以陶宅之敗，重劾邦輔。

translations.literal: He wished to divide Grand Coordinator Cao Bangfu's merit in breaking bandits at Puxuguan and could not; he then used the defeat at Taozhai to impeach Bangfu heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Denied a share of Bangfu's victory, he used the Taozhai defeat to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 陶宅之戰，實文華、宗憲兵先潰也。

translations.literal: At the battle of Taozhai it was in truth Wenhua and Zongxian's troops that fled first.
translations.idiomatic: At Taozhai Wenhua and Zongxian's troops had fled first.

sentences.zh: 兵科給事中夏栻得其情，劾文華欺誕。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xia Shi of the Military Section got the facts and impeached Wenhua for deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shi impeached Wenhua for deceit.

sentences.zh: 吏科給事中孫浚亦白邦輔冤狀。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Sun Jun of the Personnel Section also reported Bangfu's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun reported Bangfu's injustice.

sentences.zh: 帝終信文華言，邦輔坐遣戍。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end believed Wenhua and Bangfu was sent to garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Wenhua; Bangfu was exiled.

sentences.zh: 文華既殺經、天寵，復先後論罷總督周琉、楊宜，至是又傾邦輔，勢益張。

translations.literal: After Wenhua had killed Jing and Tianchong he again in succession argued down coordinators Zhou Liu and Yang Yi; now he overturned Bangfu and his power grew.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Jing and Tianchong and removed Liu, Yang, and Bangfu, his power swelled.

sentences.zh: 文武將吏爭輸貨其門，顛倒功罪，牽制兵機，紀律大乖，將吏人人解體，徵兵半天下，賊寇愈熾。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers vied to offer bribes at his gate, inverted merit and guilt, obstructed military timing, discipline was greatly lost, officers lost heart, conscription took half the realm, and bandits grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Officers bribed him, discipline collapsed, and the pirates grew worse.

sentences.zh: 文華又陳防守事宜，請籍閒田百萬畝給兵，為屯守計，而令裏居縉紳，分督郡邑兵事。

translations.literal: Wenhua again presented defense measures, requesting registration of a million mu of idle fields for troops as garrison plan, and ordering gentry at home to divide supervision of commandery and county military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed garrison farms and gentry-led local defense.

sentences.zh: 為兵部所駁而寢。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War rejected it and it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War rejected it.

sentences.zh: 官軍既屢敗，文華知賊未易平，欲委責去。

translations.literal: After repeated defeats Wenhua knew bandits were not easily pacified and wished to shift blame and leave.
translations.idiomatic: After defeats he knew the pirates could not be quickly beaten and wished to leave.

sentences.zh: 會川兵破賊周浦，俞大猷破賊海洋，文華遂言水陸成功，江南清晏，請還朝。

translations.literal: It happened that Sichuan troops broke bandits at Zhoupu and Yu Dayou broke bandits at Haiyang; Wenhua then said land and sea success was achieved and Jiangnan was tranquil, and requested return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When victories came he claimed Jiangnan was pacified and asked to return.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 比還，敗報踵至，帝疑其妄，數詰嵩，嵩曲為解，帝意終不釋。

translations.literal: When he returned defeat reports followed in succession; the emperor suspected his falsehood and repeatedly questioned Song; Song twisted explanations but the emperor's mind was never eased.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat reports followed his return; the emperor doubted him and questioned Song in vain.

sentences.zh: 會吏部尚書李默發策試選人，中言「漢武征四夷，而海內虛耗。

translations.literal: It happened that Minister of Personnel Li Mo issued policy questions testing candidates; one answered saying Han Wu campaigned on the four barbarians and within the seas were drained.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Mo's examination essay quoted Han Wu's costly campaigns.

sentences.zh: 唐憲復淮、蔡，而晚業不終。

translations.literal: Tang Xianzong recovered Huai and Cai yet his late reign did not end well.
translations.idiomatic: It cited Tang recovery of Huai and Cai yet decline at the end.

sentences.zh: 」文華劾其謗訕，默坐死。

translations.literal: Wenhua impeached him for slander and Mo was put to death on the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua impeached him for slander; Mo was executed.

sentences.zh: 帝以是謂文華忠，進工部尚書，且加太子太保。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore thought Wenhua loyal, advanced him to minister of Works, and added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed Wenhua loyal and made him minister of Works and Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 是時，嵩年老，慮一旦死，有後患，因薦文華文學，宜供奉青詞，直內閣。

translations.literal: At this time Song was old and feared that if he died suddenly there would be later trouble; he therefore recommended Wenhua's literary talent as fit to supply green-lotus prayers and attend the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Old Song recommended Wenhua for the Grand Secretariat and green-lotus prayers.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 而東南警遝至，部議再遣大臣督師，已命兵部侍郎沈良材矣，嵩令文華自請行，為帝言江南人矯首望文華。

translations.literal: Yet southeastern alarms came in succession; the ministry discussed sending a great minister again to supervise the army; they had already appointed Vice Minister Shen Liangcai of War when Song had Wenhua request the mission himself, telling the emperor that Jiangnan people craned their necks hoping for Wenhua.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry had named Shen Liangcai when Song had Wenhua volunteer, claiming Jiangnan awaited him.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，命兼右副都御史，總督江南、浙江諸軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it so and ordered him concurrently right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and other military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him grand coordinator of Jiangnan and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時宗憲先以文華薦代楊宜為總督，及文華再出，宗憲欲藉文華以通於嵩，諂奉無不至。

translations.literal: At this time Zongxian had earlier been recommended by Wenhua to replace Yang Yi as grand coordinator; when Wenhua went out again Zongxian wished to use Wenhua to reach Song and flattered him in every way.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxian flattered Wenhua to reach Song.

sentences.zh: 文華素不知兵，亦倚宗憲，兩人交甚歡。

translations.literal: Wenhua by nature did not know warfare yet relied on Zongxian; the two were on very friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: Ignorant of war, Wenhua relied on Zongxian; they were intimate.

sentences.zh: 已而宗憲平徐海，俘陳東，文華以大捷聞，歸功上玄。

translations.literal: Before long Zongxian pacified Xu Hai and captured Chen Dong; Wenhua reported a great victory and attributed merit to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongxian captured Chen Dong, Wenhua reported victory to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，祭告郊廟社稷，加文華少保，廕子錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, sacrificed to suburban altars, state, and grain gods, added Wenhua as junior guardian, and ennobled his son in the Brocade Guard as a thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sacrificed and ennobled Wenhua's son in the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 召還朝，文華乃推功元輔嵩，辭升廕，帝優詔不允。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, Wenhua then pushed merit to chief assistant Song and declined advancement and ennoblement; the emperor graciously refused his refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he credited Song and declined rewards; the emperor refused his refusal.

sentences.zh: 文華既寵貴，志日驕，事中貴及世蕃，漸不如初，諸人憾之。

translations.literal: Once favored and honored, Wenhua grew proud day by day; in serving the inner eunuchs and Shifan he was gradually not as at first; many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: As he rose he grew proud and slack with the eunuchs and Shifan; many resented him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣使賜文華，值其醉，拜跪不如禮，帝聞惡其不敬。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent envoys to bestow gifts on Wenhua; he was drunk and his bow and kneel were not according to ritual; the emperor heard and hated his disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk when the emperor's envoys came, he was rude in ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又嘗進方士藥，帝服之盡，使小璫再索之，不應。

translations.literal: He also once presented a Daoist's medicine; the emperor took it all and had a young eunuch ask again; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the emperor Daoist medicine and ignored a request for more.

sentences.zh: 西苑造新閣，不以時告成。

translations.literal: A new pavilion was built in the Western Garden and was not reported finished in time.
translations.idiomatic: A Western Garden pavilion was late.

sentences.zh: 帝一日登高，見西長安街有高甍，問誰宅。

translations.literal: One day the emperor climbed high and saw a tall ridge on West Chang'an Street and asked whose residence it was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw a grand roof on West Chang'an Street and asked whose house it was.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「趙尚書新宅也。

translations.literal: Those at his side said: Vice Minister Zhao's new residence.
translations.idiomatic: They said it was Vice Minister Zhao's new house.

sentences.zh: 」旁一人曰：「工部大木，半為文華作宅，何暇營新閣。

translations.literal: Another said: The great timber of the Ministry of Works—half was used for Wenhua's residence; how could he spare time to build the new pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Another said half the ministry timber built Wenhua's house instead of the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 」帝益慍。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 會三殿災，帝欲建正陽門樓，責成甚亟，文華猝不能辦。

translations.literal: It happened that the three halls burned; the emperor wished to build the Zhengyang Gate tower and demanded completion urgently; Wenhua suddenly could not deliver.
translations.idiomatic: When the three halls burned he could not rebuild the Zhengyang Gate tower in time.

sentences.zh: 帝積怒，且聞其連歲視師黷貨要功狀，思逐之，乃諭嵩曰：「門樓庀材遲，文華似不如昔。

translations.literal: The emperor accumulated anger and also heard of his years supervising the army, taking bribes and demanding merit; he wished to drive him out and told Song: Materials for the gate tower are slow; Wenhua seems not as before.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by delays and corruption, the emperor told Song Wenhua was not as before.

sentences.zh: 」嵩猶未知帝意，力為掩覆，且言：「文華觸熱南征，因致疾，宜增侍郎一人專督大工。

translations.literal: Song still did not know the emperor's intent and strongly covered for him, saying: Wenhua, heated in the southern campaign, fell ill; one should add a vice minister solely to supervise the great works.
translations.idiomatic: Song covered for him and proposed adding a vice minister for construction.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 文華因上章稱疾，請賜假靜攝旬月。

translations.literal: Wenhua therefore memorialized illness and requested leave for quiet recuperation for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua memorialized illness and asked ten days' leave.

sentences.zh: 帝手批曰：「大工方興，司空是職。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in the margin: Great works are rising; the minister of works is the office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote that the minister of works must oversee great works.

sentences.zh: 文華既有疾，可回籍休養。

translations.literal: If Wenhua has illness he may return home to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: If ill, he may return home.

sentences.zh: 」制下，舉朝相賀。

translations.literal: When the decree came down the whole court congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejoiced when the decree came.

sentences.zh: 帝雖逐文華猶以為未盡其罪，而言官無攻者，帝怒無所泄。

translations.literal: Though the emperor had driven out Wenhua he still thought the crime not fully exhausted, yet censors did not attack; the emperor's anger had nowhere to vent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought Wenhua insufficiently punished but censors were silent.

sentences.zh: 會其子錦衣千戶懌思以齋祀停封章日請假送父，帝大怒，黜文華為民，戍其子邊衛。

translations.literal: It happened that his son, a thousand-household of the Brocade Guard, Yi, because of fasting sacrifices stopped sealing memorials and daily asked leave to send off his father; the emperor was greatly angry, demoted Wenhua to commoner, and garrisoned his son in the frontier guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son's improper leave enraged the emperor; Wenhua was made a commoner and his son exiled.

sentences.zh: 以禮科失糾劾，令對狀。

translations.literal: Because the Rites Section failed to impeach, they were ordered to answer at court.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Section was ordered to answer for failing to impeach.

sentences.zh: 於是都給事中謝江以下六人，並廷杖削籍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chief Supervising Secretary Xie Jiang and six below were all beaten at court and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretary Xie Jiang and six others were beaten and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 文華故病蠱，及遭譴臥舟中，意邑邑不自聊，一夕手捫其腹，腹裂，臟腑出，遂死。

translations.literal: Wenhua had long suffered gu poison; when punished he lay in the boat, restless and ill at ease; one night he felt his belly and it split, organs came out, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ill with gu poison, he split open his belly in the boat and died.

sentences.zh: 後給事中羅嘉賓等核軍餉，文華所侵盜以十萬四千計。

translations.literal: Later Supervising Secretary Luo Jiabin and others audited military funds; Wenhua's embezzlement totaled one hundred four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Audit found he had embezzled 104,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 有詔征諸其家，至萬曆十一年征猶未及半，有司援恩詔祈免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered collection from his household; by the eleventh year of Wanli collection was still not half done; officials cited amnesty edicts begging exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Collection from his estate was still incomplete in Wanli year 11.

sentences.zh: 神宗不許，戍其子慎思於煙瘴地。

translations.literal: Shenzong did not permit and garrisoned his son Shensi in miasmal lands.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong refused and exiled his son Shensi.

sentences.zh: 鄢懋卿，豐城人。

translations.literal: Yan Maoqing was a man of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Maoqing was a native of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢御史，屢遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: From courier he was promoted to censor and repeatedly rose to vice minister of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: From courier he rose to vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，轉左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was transferred to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 he became left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋進左副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 懋卿以才自負，見嚴嵩柄政，深附之，為嵩父子所暱。

translations.literal: Maoqing was self-confident in talent; seeing Yan Song hold government he attached deeply and was intimate with the Song father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and arrogant, he attached to the Song father and son.

sentences.zh: 會戶部以兩浙、兩淮、長蘆、河東鹽政不舉，請遣大臣一人總理，嵩遂用懋卿。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ministry of Revenue, because salt administration in the two Zhejiangs, two Huai regions, Changlu, and Hedong was not managed, requested one great minister to oversee; Song then used Maoqing.
translations.idiomatic: When salt administration failed, Song installed Maoqing as overseer.

sentences.zh: 舊制，大臣理鹽政，無總四運司者。

translations.literal: By old regulation great ministers managing salt had never overseen all four transport offices.
translations.idiomatic: No minister had ever held all four salt circuits.

sentences.zh: 至是懋卿盡握天下利柄，倚嚴氏父子，所至市權納賄，監司郡邑吏膝行蒲伏。

translations.literal: Now Maoqing grasped the profit handles of the realm, relied on the Yan father and son, sold power and took bribes wherever he went; surveillance commissioners and commandery and county officials crawled on knees.
translations.idiomatic: He held all salt profits, sold power, and made officials crawl.

sentences.zh: 懋卿性奢侈，至以文錦被廁床，白金飾溺器。

translations.literal: Maoqing was luxurious by nature, even using brocade for toilet bedding and white gold for urinals.
translations.idiomatic: He used brocade bedding and gold urinals.

sentences.zh: 嵊時遺嚴氏及諸權貴，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Each time he sent gifts to the Yan family and powerful figures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He sent countless gifts to the Yans and the powerful.

sentences.zh: 其按部，常與妻偕行，制五彩輿，令十二女子舁之，道路傾駭。

translations.literal: On inspection tours he often traveled with his wife in a five-colored sedan borne by twelve girls; the road was shaken in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled with his wife in a twelve-bearer sedan that stunned the roads.

sentences.zh: 淳安知縣海瑞、慈谿知縣霍與瑕，以抗忤罷去。

translations.literal: Chun'an Magistrate Hai Rui and Cixi Magistrate Huo Yuxia were dismissed for resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates Hai Rui and Huo Yuxia were dismissed for defying him.

sentences.zh: 御史林潤嘗劾懋卿要索屬吏，饋遺巨萬，濫受民訟，勒富人賄，置酒高會，日費千金，虐殺不辜，怨咨載路，苛斂淮商，幾至激變，五大罪。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Run once impeached Maoqing for extorting subordinates, gifts of tens of thousands, accepting popular lawsuits at will, forcing the rich to bribe, holding grand banquets costing a thousand cash a day, cruelly killing the innocent, complaints filling the road, harsh levies on Huai merchants nearly causing revolt—five great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Run charged him with five great crimes including extortion and near rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 四十年召為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was summoned as right vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he was summoned as right vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 兩淮餘鹽，歲征銀六十萬兩，及懋卿增至一百萬。

translations.literal: Surplus salt in the two Huai regions yearly levied six hundred thousand taels of silver; under Maoqing it increased to one million.
translations.idiomatic: Huai surplus salt rose from 600,000 to 1,000,000 taels under him.

sentences.zh: 懋卿去，巡鹽御史徐爌極言其害，乃復六十萬之舊。

translations.literal: When Maoqing left, salt censor Xu Huang spoke extremely of the harm and it returned to the old six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After he left the levy returned to 600,000.

sentences.zh: 嵩敗，御史鄭洛劾懋卿及大理卿萬寀朋奸黷貨，兩人皆落職。

translations.literal: When Song fell, Censor Zheng Luo impeached Maoqing and Court of Justice Minister Wan Cai for factional corruption; both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's fall Zheng Luo impeached Maoqing and Wan Cai; both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既而寀匿嚴氏銀八萬兩，懋卿紿得其二萬，事皆露，兩人先後戍邊。

translations.literal: Before long Cai hid eighty thousand taels of Yan silver and Maoqing obtained twenty thousand by fraud; when exposed both were garrisoned on the frontier in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Cai hid Yan silver; Maoqing seized part; both were exiled.

sentences.zh: 時坐嚴氏黨被論者，前兵部右侍郎柏鄉魏謙吉、工部左侍郎南昌劉伯躍、南京刑部右侍郎德安何遷、右副都御史信陽董威、僉都御史萬安張雨、應天府尹祥符孟淮、南京光祿卿南昌胡植、南京光祿少卿武進白啟常、右諭德蘭谿唐汝楫、南京太常卿掌國子監事新城王材、太僕丞新喻張春及嵩婿廣西副使袁應樞等數十人，黜謫有差。

translations.literal: At this time those punished as Yan faction included former right vice minister of War Wei Qianji of Baixiang, left vice minister of Works Liu Boyue of Nanchang, right vice minister of Justice at Nanjing He Qian of De'an, right vice censor-in-chief Dong Wei of Xinyang, vice censor-in-chief Zhang Yu of Wan'an, prefect of Yingtian Meng Huai of Xiangfu, director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing Hu Zhi of Nanchang, junior director of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing Bai Qichang of Wujin, right mentor Tang Ruji of Lanxi, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing acting in the Imperial Academy Wang Cai of Xincheng, vice director of the Imperial Stud Zhang Chun of Xinyu, and Song's son-in-law Vice Commissioner Yuan Yingshu of Guangxi—several dozen in all—with dismissal and demotion varying.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens associated with the Yan faction were punished, from Wei Qianji to Yuan Yingshu, with varying penalties.

sentences.zh: 植與嵩鄉里，嘗勸嵩殺楊繼盛。

translations.literal: Zhi was Song's townsman and once urged Song to kill Yang Jisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Song's townsman, had urged killing Yang Jisheng.

sentences.zh: 啟常官禮部郎，匿喪遷光祿，與材、汝楫俱為世蕃狎客。

translations.literal: Qichang was a director in the Ministry of Rites, concealed mourning and was transferred to Imperial Entertainments; with Cai and Ruji he was all Shifan's intimate guests.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang concealed mourning; he, Cai, and Ruji were Shifan's intimates.

sentences.zh: 啟常至以粉墨塗面供歡笑。

translations.literal: Qichang even painted his face with cosmetics to supply amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang even painted his face for amusement.

sentences.zh: 而材、汝楫俱出入嵩臥內，關通請屬，尤為人所惡云。

translations.literal: Cai and Ruji both entered and left Song's bedchamber, communicating requests—especially hated by people.
translations.idiomatic: Cai and Ruji passed in and out of Song's bedroom trading favors and were especially hated.

sentences.zh: 周延儒

translations.literal: Zhou Yanru
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yanru

sentences.zh: 周延儒，字玉繩，宜興人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yanru, style Yuyong, was a man of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yanru, courtesy name Yuyong, was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年會試、殿試皆第一。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he was first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 41 he topped both metropolitan and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，年甫二十餘。

translations.literal: Appointed compiler, he was just over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler in his early twenties.

sentences.zh: 美麗自喜，與同年生馮銓友善。

translations.literal: Handsome and pleased with himself, he was friendly with fellow graduate Feng Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and vain, he befriended fellow graduate Feng Quan.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，遷右中允，掌司經局事。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was transferred to right junior mentor and managed the Classics Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he managed the Classics Bureau as right junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 尋以少詹事掌南京翰林院事。

translations.literal: Soon as junior mentor he managed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon headed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，召為禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie ascended he was summoned as right vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuanglie ascended he was summoned as right vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 延儒性警敏，善伺意指。

translations.literal: Yanru was alert and clever and good at reading intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru was clever at reading the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年冬，錦州兵嘩，督師袁崇煥請給餉。

translations.literal: In the first winter of Chongzhen year 1 Jinzhou troops mutinied; Grand Secretary Yuan Chonghuan requested pay.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 1 Jinzhou troops mutinied; Yuan Chonghuan asked for pay.

sentences.zh: 帝御文華殿，召問諸大臣，皆請發內帑。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the Wenhua Hall and summoned the great ministers; all requested disbursement from the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenhua Hall all ministers asked for inner treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 延儒揣帝意，獨進曰：「關門昔防敵，今且防兵。

translations.literal: Yanru guessed the emperor's intent and alone advanced: The passes once guarded against enemies, now must guard against troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru alone said the passes now must guard against their own troops.

sentences.zh: 寧遠嘩，餉之，錦州嘩，復餉之，各邊且效尤。

translations.literal: If Ningyuan mutinies and is paid, Jinzhou mutinies and is paid again, every border will follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: Paying mutineers at Ningyuan and Jinzhou would invite imitation everywhere.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿謂何如？

translations.literal: The emperor said: What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his view.

sentences.zh: 」延儒曰：「事迫，不得不發。

translations.literal: Yanru said: The affair is urgent and cannot but be paid.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said payment was urgent.

sentences.zh: 但當求經久之策。

translations.literal: But one should seek a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: But a long-term plan was needed.

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之，降旨責群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded, issued an edict rebuking the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded and rebuked the ministers.

sentences.zh: 居數日，復召問，延儒曰：「餉莫如粟，山海粟不缺，缺銀耳。

translations.literal: After several days he summoned again; Yanru said: Pay is best in grain; Shanhai is not short of grain, only silver.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Yanru said grain, not silver, should be used.

sentences.zh: 何故嘩？

translations.literal: Why mutiny?
translations.idiomatic: Why mutiny then?

sentences.zh: 嘩必有隱情，安知非驕弁構煽以脅崇煥邪？

translations.literal: Mutiny must have hidden cause—how do we know arrogant officers did not incite it to coerce Chonghuan?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps arrogant officers incited it to coerce Chonghuan?

sentences.zh: 」帝方疑邊將要脅，聞延儒言，大說，由此屬意延儒。

translations.literal: The emperor was just suspecting border generals of coercion; hearing Yanru he was greatly pleased and from this entrusted Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, suspecting generals, was pleased and favored Yanru.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大學士劉鴻訓罷，命會推，廷臣以延儒望輕置之，列成基命、錢謙益、鄭以偉、李騰芳、孫慎行、何如寵、薛三省、盛以弘、羅喻義、王永光、曹於汴十一人名上。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun retired; collective recommendation was ordered; court ministers, thinking Yanru's standing light, set him aside and listed eleven names including Cheng Jiming, Qian Qianyi, Zheng Yiwei, Li Tengfang, Sun Shenxing, He Rulong, Xue Sanxing, Sheng Yihong, Luo Yuyi, Wang Yongguang, and Cao Yubian.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hongxun retired, ministers omitted Yanru and listed eleven others.

sentences.zh: 帝以延儒不預，大疑。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yanru was not included, was greatly suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was suspicious that Yanru was omitted.

sentences.zh: 及溫體仁訐謙益，延儒助之。

translations.literal: When Wen Tiren attacked Qianyi, Yanru assisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Tiren attacked Qianyi, Yanru helped.

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，黜謙益，盡罷會推者不用。

translations.literal: The emperor then erupted in anger, dismissed Qianyi, and dismissed all who had been in the collective recommendation without using them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Qianyi and all on the recommendation list.

sentences.zh: 二年三月召對延儒於文華殿，漏下數十刻乃出，語秘不得聞。

translations.literal: In the third month of year 2 he was summoned to audience with Yanru at Wenhua Hall; the clepsydra ran dozens of marks before he emerged; the words were secret and could not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: In month 3 of year 2 he had a secret long audience at Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 御史黃宗昌劾其生平穢行，御史李長春論獨對之非。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Zongchang impeached his lifetime foul conduct; Censor Li Changchun discussed the impropriety of solitary audience.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached his conduct and solitary audience.

sentences.zh: 延儒乞罷，不允。

translations.literal: Yanru begged to resign; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to resign in vain.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中錢允鯨言：「延儒與馮銓密契，延儒柄政，必為逆黨翻局。

translations.literal: Nanjing Supervising Secretary Qian Yunjing said: Yanru and Feng Quan are secretly allied; if Yanru holds government he will reverse the case for the traitor faction.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yunjing warned Yanru would reverse the traitor case with Feng Quan.

sentences.zh: 」延儒疏辨，帝優詔褒答。

translations.literal: Yanru memorialized in defense; the emperor replied with gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru defended himself; the emperor replied graciously.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，京師有警，特旨拜延儒禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，參機務。

translations.literal: That twelfth month there was alarm in the capital; by special edict Yanru was made minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, participating in secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In month 12 he was made minister of Rites and Eastern Pavilion grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 明年二月加太子太保，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month he was added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and changed to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In month 2 of the next year he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 六月，體仁亦入。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Wen Tiren also entered.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren entered the cabinet in month 6.

sentences.zh: 九月，成基命致仕，延儒遂為首輔。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Cheng Jiming retired; Yanru then became chief assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Jiming retired in month 9, Yanru became chief assistant.

sentences.zh: 尋加少保，改武英殿。

translations.literal: Soon added junior guardian and changed to the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior guardian of the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 體仁既並相，務為柔佞，帝意漸響之。

translations.literal: After Tiren also became chancellor he strove to be soft and flattering; the emperor's mind gradually turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren flattered the emperor and won favor.

sentences.zh: 而體仁陽曲謹媚延儒，陰欲奪其位，延儒不知也。

translations.literal: Yet Tiren outwardly was careful and flattering to Yanru while secretly wishing to seize his place; Yanru did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren flattered Yanru outwardly while plotting his fall.

sentences.zh: 體仁與吏部尚書王永光謀起逆案王之臣、呂純如等。

translations.literal: Tiren with Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang plotted to raise Wang Zhichen and Lu Chunru in the traitor case.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren and Wang Yongguang plotted to raise traitor-case figures.

sentences.zh: 或謂延儒曰：「彼將翻逆案，而外歸咎於公。

translations.literal: Someone told Yanru: They will reverse the traitor case and outwardly blame you.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Yanru he would be blamed for reversing the traitor case.

sentences.zh: 」延儒愕然。

translations.literal: Yanru was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru was startled.

sentences.zh: 會帝以之臣問，延儒曰：「用之臣，亦可雪崔呈秀矣。

translations.literal: When the emperor asked about Zhichen, Yanru said: Using Zhichen could also whitewash Cui Chengxiu.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about Zhichen, Yanru said it would whitewash Cui Chengxiu.

sentences.zh: 」帝悟而止。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and stopped.

sentences.zh: 體仁益欲傾延儒。

translations.literal: Tiren all the more wished to overturn Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren pressed harder against Yanru.

sentences.zh: 四年春。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 4.

sentences.zh: 延儒姻婭陳於泰廷對第一，及所用大同巡撫張廷拱、登萊巡撫孫元化皆有私，時論籍籍。

translations.literal: Yanru's affinal kin Chen Yutai was first in palace examination; and the Datong grand coordinator Zhang Tinggong and Deng-Lai grand coordinator Sun Yuanhua whom he used all had private ties; public opinion was noisy.
translations.idiomatic: His kin Chen Yutai topped the palace exam; his appointees Zhang Tinggong and Sun Yuanhua were accused of favoritism.

sentences.zh: 其子弟家人暴邑中，邑中民熱其廬，發其先壟，為言官所糾。

translations.literal: His sons, younger brothers, and household slaves were violent in the district; the people burned his lodge and opened his ancestral tombs; censors impeached this.
translations.idiomatic: His household terrorized the district until locals burned his lodge and tombs.

sentences.zh: 兄素儒冒錦衣籍，授千戶，又用家人周文郁為副總兵，益為言者所詆。

translations.literal: His elder brother Suru falsely entered Brocade Guard registers and was granted a thousand-household; he also used household slave Zhou Wenyu as vice commander-in-chief—still more reviled by speakers.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Suru fraudulently entered the Brocade Guard; his slave became vice commander—drawing more attacks.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，叛將李九成等陷登州，囚元化。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year rebel generals Li Jiucheng and others took Dengzhou and imprisoned Yuanhua.
