translations.idiomatic: In month 1 of year 5 Li Jiucheng took Dengzhou and imprisoned Yuanhua.

sentences.zh: 侍郎劉宇烈視師無功，言路鹹指延儒庇宇烈。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Liu Yulie supervised the army without success; the censorial route all pointed at Yanru for shielding Yulie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yulie failed in command; censors said Yanru shielded him.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中孫三傑、馮元飆，御史余應桂、衛景瑗、尹明翼、路振飛、吳執禦、王道純、王象雲等，屢劾延儒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretaries Sun Sanjie and Feng Yuanbiao, Censors Yu Yinggui, Wei Jingyuan, Yin Mingyi, Lu Zhenfei, Wu Zhiyu, Wang Daochun, Wang Xiangyun, and others repeatedly impeached Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Many censors repeatedly impeached Yanru.

sentences.zh: 應桂並謂延儒納巨盜神一魁賄。

translations.literal: Yinggui also said Yanru took bribes from the great bandit Shen Yikui.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui charged he took bribes from the bandit Shen Yikui.

sentences.zh: 而監視中官鄧希詔與總督曹文衡相訐奏，語侵延儒。

translations.literal: Supervising eunuch Deng Xizhao and Grand Coordinator Cao Wenheng impeached each other, words touching Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Deng Xizhao and Cao Wenheng's mutual impeachments touched Yanru.

sentences.zh: 給事中李春旺亦論延儒當去。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Chunwang also said Yanru should go.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunwang said Yanru should resign.

sentences.zh: 延儒數上疏辯，帝雖慰留，心不能無動。

translations.literal: Yanru repeatedly memorialized in defense; though the emperor comforted and kept him, in his heart he could not be unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him but was shaken.

sentences.zh: 已而延儒令于泰陳時政四事，宣府太監王坤承體仁指，直劾延儒庇於泰。

translations.literal: Before long Yanru had Yutai present four items on current policy; Xuanfu eunuch Wang Kun, following Tiren's intent, directly impeached Yanru for shielding Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun impeached Yanru for shielding Yutai.

sentences.zh: 給事中傅朝佑言中官不當劾首揆，輕朝廷，疑有邪人交構，副都御史王志道亦言之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fu Chaoyou said eunuchs should not impeach the chief assistant, slighting the court, suspecting evil men plotting; Vice Censor-in-chief Wang Zhidao also spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chaoyou said eunuchs should not impeach the chief assistant.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，削志道籍，延儒不能救。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and struck Wang Zhidao from the rolls; Yanru could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck Wang Zhidao from the rolls; Yanru could not help.

sentences.zh: 體仁各處嗾給事中陳贊化劾延儒「昵武弁李元功等，招搖罔利。

translations.literal: Tiren incited Supervising Secretary Chen Zanhua to impeach Yanru for intimacy with military officer Li Yuangong and others, swaying for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren incited Chen Zanhua to impeach Yanru for Li Yuangong.

sentences.zh: 陛下特恩停刑，元功以為延儒功，索獄囚賕謝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty specially favored stopping punishment; Yuangong thought it Yanru's merit and demanded bribes from prisoners for thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangong extorted prisoners, thinking Yanru had saved him.

sentences.zh: 而延儒至目陛下為羲皇上人，語誖逆。

translations.literal: Yanru even called Your Majesty a ruler of the age of Fuxi; the words were rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru called the emperor a Fuxi-era ruler—treasonous words.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，下元功詔獄，且窮詰贊化語所自得。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sent Yuangong to the imperial prison, and pressed to the end where Zanhua's words came from.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor imprisoned Yuangong and pressed Zanhua for sources.

sentences.zh: 贊化言得之上林典簿姚孫渠、給事中李世祺，而副使張鳳翼亦具述延儒語。

translations.literal: Zanhua said he got it from Upper Forest clerk Yao Sunqu and Supervising Secretary Li Shiqi; Vice Commissioner Zhang Fengyi also fully related Yanru's words.
translations.idiomatic: Zanhua implicated Yao Sunqu, Li Shiqi, and Zhang Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛帥王世盛拷掠元功無所承。

translations.literal: Brocade Guard commander Wang Shisheng tortured Yuangong but obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shisheng tortured Yuangong without result.

sentences.zh: 獄上，鐫世盛五級，令窮治其事。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted Shisheng was reduced five ranks and ordered to press the investigation to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng was demoted and ordered to press the case.

sentences.zh: 延儒覬體仁為援，體仁卒不應，且陰黜與延儒善者，延儒大困。

translations.literal: Yanru looked to Tiren for aid; Tiren in the end did not respond and secretly dismissed those friendly to Yanru; Yanru was greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru sought Tiren's aid in vain as Tiren purged his allies.

sentences.zh: 六年六月引疾乞歸，賜白金、彩緞，遣行人護行。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year he cited illness and begged to return home; white gold and colored silk were bestowed and a courier was sent to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: In month 6 of year 6 he retired ill with honors.

sentences.zh: 體仁遂為首輔矣。

translations.literal: Tiren then became chief assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren became chief assistant.

sentences.zh: 始延儒裏居，頗從東林游，善姚希孟、羅喻義。

translations.literal: At first when Yanru lived at home he rather associated with the Donglin faction and was friendly with Yao Ximeng and Luo Yuyi.
translations.idiomatic: At home he had associated with Donglin figures.

sentences.zh: 既陷錢謙益，遂仇東林。

translations.literal: After entrapping Qian Qianyi he then hated the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: After destroying Qianyi he hated the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 及主會試，所取士張溥、馬世奇等，又皆東林也。

translations.literal: When he presided over the metropolitan examination the scholars he took—Zhang Pu, Ma Shiji, and others—were again Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars he selected were Donglin men.

sentences.zh: 至是歸，失勢，心內慚。

translations.literal: Now returning, he lost power and was inwardly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in disgrace, he was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 而體仁益橫，越五年始去。

translations.literal: Yet Tiren grew all the more overbearing; only after five years did he leave.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren ruled harshly five more years.

sentences.zh: 去而張至發、薛國觀相繼當國，與楊嗣昌等並以娼嫉稱。

translations.literal: After he left Zhang Zhifa and Xue Guoguan succeeded in government, and with Yang Sichang and others were all called lewd and jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Later ministers were called lewd and jealous.

sentences.zh: 一時正人鄭三俊、劉宗周、黃道周等，皆得罪。

translations.literal: Upright men Zheng Sanjun, Liu Zongzhou, and Huang Daozhou were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men were punished.

sentences.zh: 溥等憂之，說延儒曰：「公若再相，易前轍，可重得賢聲。

translations.literal: Pu and others worried and said to Yanru: If you become chancellor again and change your former track you can regain a reputation for worth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu urged him to reform if recalled.

sentences.zh: 」延儒以為然。

translations.literal: Yanru thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru agreed.

sentences.zh: 溥友吳昌時為交關近侍，馮銓復助為謀。

translations.literal: Pu's friend Wu Changshi traded with close attendants; Feng Quan again helped plot.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changshi and Feng Quan helped plot his return.

sentences.zh: 會帝亦頗思延儒，而國觀適敗。

translations.literal: It happened the emperor also rather missed Yanru, and Guoguan happened to fall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor missed Yanru; Guoguan fell.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月詔起延儒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year an edict recalled Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: In month 2 of year 14 Yanru was recalled.

sentences.zh: 九月至京，復為首輔。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached the capital and again became chief assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In month 9 he became chief assistant again.

sentences.zh: 尋加少師兼太子太師，進吏部尚書、中極殿大學士。

translations.literal: Soon added junior master and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, advanced to minister of Personnel and grand secretary of the Central Peak Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of Personnel and Central Peak grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 延儒被召，溥等以數事要之。

translations.literal: When Yanru was summoned Pu and others required several matters of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu demanded promises on his recall.

sentences.zh: 延儒慨然曰：「吾當銳意行之，以謝諸公。

translations.literal: Yanru said resolutely: I shall carry them out vigorously to thank you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru vowed to reform to thank them.

sentences.zh: 」既入朝，悉反體仁輩弊政。

translations.literal: After entering court he entirely reversed the evil policies of Tiren and his kind.
translations.idiomatic: In court he reversed Tiren's policies.

sentences.zh: 首請釋漕糧白糧欠戶，蠲民間積逋，凡兵殘歲荒地，減見年兩稅。

translations.literal: First he requested release of grain-tax and white-grain debtors, remission of popular accumulated arrears, and for lands wasted by war or famine reduction of the current year's two taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted debts and reduced taxes on war-ravaged land.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、常、嘉、湖諸府大水，許以明年夏麥代漕糧。

translations.literal: Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou flooded; he permitted next year's summer wheat in place of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Flooded lower Yangtze prefectures could pay in summer wheat instead of transport grain.

sentences.zh: 宥戍罪以下，皆得還家。

translations.literal: Those below garrison punishment were all pardoned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Those below garrison punishment were sent home.

sentences.zh: 復注誤舉人，廣取士額及召還言事遷謫諸臣李清等。

translations.literal: Restored misregistered candidates, broadened examination quotas, and recalled remonstrating exiled ministers such as Li Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He restored candidates, broadened quotas, and recalled exiles like Li Qing.

sentences.zh: 帝皆忻然從之。

translations.literal: The emperor gladly followed all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly agreed to all.

sentences.zh: 延儒又言：「老成名德，不可輕棄。

translations.literal: Yanru also said: Old and established virtue must not be lightly discarded.
translations.idiomatic: He said established worthies must not be discarded.

sentences.zh: 」於是鄭三俊長吏部，劉宗周掌都察院，范景文長工部，倪元璐佐兵部，皆起自廢籍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng Sanjun headed Personnel, Liu Zongzhou managed the Censorate, Fan Jingwen headed Works, Ni Yuanlu assisted War—all raised from dismissed registers.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun, Liu Zongzhou, Fan Jingwen, and Ni Yuanlu were restored.

sentences.zh: 其他李邦華、張國維、徐石麒、張瑋、金光辰等，佈滿九列。

translations.literal: Others such as Li Banghua, Zhang Guowei, Xu Shilin, Zhang Wei, and Jin Guangchen filled the nine ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua and others filled the ministries.

sentences.zh: 釋在獄傅宗龍等，贈已故文震孟、姚希孟等官。

translations.literal: Released Fu Zonglong and others in prison; posthumously granted offices to the deceased Wen Zhenmeng, Yao Ximeng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He released prisoners and honored the dead.

sentences.zh: 中外翕然稱賢。

translations.literal: Within and without the court all together praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country praised him as worthy.

sentences.zh: 嘗燕侍，帝語及黃道周，時道周方謫戍辰州。

translations.literal: Once at a banquet in attendance the emperor spoke of Huang Daozhou; at the time Daozhou was demoted to garrison Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor mentioned Huang Daozhou, then garrisoned at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 延儒曰：「道周氣質少偏，然學與守皆可用。

translations.literal: Yanru said: Daozhou's temperament is somewhat biased, yet his learning and integrity can both be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said Daozhou was biased but learned and upright enough to use.

sentences.zh: 」蔣德璟請移道周戍近地。

translations.literal: Jiang Dejing requested moving Daozhou's garrison nearer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dejing asked to move Daozhou nearer.

sentences.zh: 延儒曰：「上欲用即用之耳，何必移戍。

translations.literal: Yanru said: If Your Majesty wishes to use him, use him—why move the garrison?
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said the emperor could simply recall him.

sentences.zh: 」帝即日復道周官。

translations.literal: The emperor that very day restored Daozhou's office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored Daozhou that day.

sentences.zh: 其因事開釋如此。

translations.literal: His opening releases on affairs were like this.
translations.idiomatic: He often secured releases this way.

sentences.zh: 帝尊禮延儒特重，嘗於歲首日東向揖之，曰：「朕以天下聽先生。

translations.literal: The emperor honored Yanru especially; once on New Year's Day he bowed eastward to him, saying: I entrust the realm to you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the emperor bowed to him and entrusted him with the realm.

sentences.zh: 」因遍及諸閣臣。

translations.literal: He then extended this to all grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: He extended the gesture to all grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 然延儒實庸駑無材略，且性貪。

translations.literal: Yet Yanru was in truth mediocre and without strategy, and greedy by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yanru was mediocre, strategy-less, and greedy.

sentences.zh: 當邊境喪師，李自成殘掠河南，張獻忠破楚、蜀，天下大亂，延儒一無所謀畫。

translations.literal: When borders lost armies, Li Zicheng ravaged Henan, Zhang Xianzhong broke Chu and Shu, and the realm was in great disorder, Yanru had not a single plan.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm collapsed he offered no plan.

sentences.zh: 用侯恂、範志完督師，皆僨事，延儒無憂色。

translations.literal: He used Hou Xun and Fan Zhigang as grand coordinators; both failed; Yanru had no troubled look.
translations.idiomatic: His grand coordinators failed; he seemed untroubled.

sentences.zh: 而門下客盛順、董廷獻因緣為奸利。

translations.literal: Yet his clients Sheng Shun and Dong Tingxian used connections for illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: Clients Sheng Shun and Dong Tingxian profited corruptly.

sentences.zh: 又信用文選郎吳昌時及給事中曹良直、廖國遴、楊枝起、曾應遴輩。

translations.literal: He also trusted Selection Bureau director Wu Changshi and Supervising Secretaries Cao Liangzhi, Liao Guolin, Yang Zhiqi, and Zeng Yinglin.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted Wu Changshi and several supervising secretaries.

sentences.zh: 昌時，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Changshi was a man of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Changshi was from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 有幹材，頗為東林效奔走。

translations.literal: He had executive talent and rather ran errands for the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: He had talent and served the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 然為人墨而傲，通廠衛，把持朝官，同朝鹹嫉之。

translations.literal: Yet he was corrupt and proud, communicated with the factory guards, controlled court officials—all at court resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was corrupt, proud, and tied to the eunuch factories.

sentences.zh: 行人司副熊開元廷劾延儒納賄狀，觸帝怒，與給事中薑埰俱廷杖，下詔獄。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Courier Office Xiong Kaiyuan impeached Yanru for taking bribes at court; touching the emperor's anger, he and Supervising Secretary Jiang Cai were both beaten at court and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Kaiyuan impeached Yanru for bribery; he and Jiang Cai were beaten and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 左都御史宗周、僉都御史光辰以救開元、埰罷，尚書石麒又以救宗周等罷，延儒皆弗救，朝議皆以咎延儒。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-chief Zongzhou and Vice Censor-in-chief Guangchen were dismissed for saving Kaiyuan and Cai; Minister Shilin was dismissed for saving Zongzhou and others—Yanru saved none; court opinion all blamed Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou, Guangchen, and Shilin fell trying to save prisoners; Yanru did not help.

sentences.zh: 會昌時以年例出言路十人於外，言路大嘩。

translations.literal: It happened Changshi by annual rule sent ten censors outside the capital; the censorial route was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Changshi posted ten censors outside the capital; censors were furious.

sentences.zh: 掌科給事中吳麟徵、掌道御史祁彪佳劾昌時挾勢弄權，延儒頗不自安。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary Wu Linzheng and Chief Censor Qi Biaojia impeached Changshi for wielding power; Yanru was rather ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Linzheng and Qi Biaojia impeached Changshi; Yanru grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 初，延儒奏罷廠衛緝事，都人大悅。

translations.literal: At first Yanru memorialized to stop factory-guard secret arrests; the capital greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He had ended factory secret arrests to popular joy.

sentences.zh: 朝士不肖者因通賂遺，而廠衛以失權，胥怨延儒。

translations.literal: Unworthy courtiers therefore communicated bribes, while the factory guards, losing power, all resented Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials bribed; factory guards resented him.

sentences.zh: 又傲同官陳演，演銜刺骨。

translations.literal: He also looked down on colleague Chen Yan; Yan bore a bone-deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: He slighted Chen Yan, who hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 掌錦衣者駱養性，延儒所薦也，養性狡狠背延儒，與中官結，刺延儒陰事。

translations.literal: Brocade Guard commander Luo Yangxing, whom Yanru recommended, was crafty and turned on Yanru, joining with inner eunuchs to spy on Yanru's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yangxing, whom he promoted, spied on him with eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月，大清兵略山東，還至近畿，帝憂甚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year the Great Qing army overran Shandong and returned near the capital; the emperor was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: In month 4 of year 16 the Qing army neared the capital; the emperor was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 大學士吳甡方奉命辦流寇，延儒不得已自請視師。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wu Shen was just ordered to handle roving bandits; Yanru had no choice but to request supervising the army himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru volunteered to supervise the army when Wu Shen was sent against bandits.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，降手敕，獎以召虎、裴度，賜章服、白金、文綺、上駟，給金帛賞軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, sent a hand-edict praising him with Zhao Hu and Pei Du, bestowed insignia, robes, white gold, patterned silk, and fine horses, and gave gold and silk to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him like Zhao Hu and Pei Du and sent rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 延儒駐通州不敢戰，惟與幕下客飲酒娛樂，而日騰章奏捷，帝輒賜璽書褒勵。

translations.literal: Yanru stationed at Tongzhou and dared not fight, only drinking and amusing himself with clients, yet daily sent memorials of victory; the emperor repeatedly bestowed sealed edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed at Tongzhou feasting while reporting false victories.

sentences.zh: 偵大清兵去，乃言敵退，請下兵部議將吏功罪。

translations.literal: When he learned the Great Qing army had left he then said the enemy had withdrawn and requested the Ministry of War discuss merit and guilt of generals and officers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing withdrew he claimed victory and asked for merit reviews.

sentences.zh: 既歸朝，繳敕諭，帝即令藏貯，以識勳勞。

translations.literal: Returning to court he surrendered the edict; the emperor ordered it stored to mark meritorious toil.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the commendation edict for the archives.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太師，廕子中書舍人，賜銀幣、蟒服。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was added Grand Preceptor, his son ennobled as Secretariat draftsman, and given silver, coins, and python robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Preceptor and his son ennobled.

sentences.zh: 延儒辭太師，許之。

translations.literal: Yanru declined Grand Preceptor; permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined Grand Preceptor and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 居數日，養性及中官盡發所刺軍中事。

translations.literal: After several days Yangxing and inner eunuchs fully exposed what they had spied in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Yangxing and eunuchs exposed his army deceits.

sentences.zh: 帝乃大怒，諭府部諸臣責延儒蒙蔽推諉，事多不忍言，令從公察議。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, told ministry ministers Yanru had deceived and shirked, affairs too many to bear speaking, and ordered public deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged and ordered public judgment on Yanru's deceit.

sentences.zh: 陳演等公揭救之，延儒席槁待罪，自請戍邊。

translations.literal: Chen Yan and others jointly memorialized to save him; Yanru sat on straw awaiting punishment and requested garrison on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues tried to save him; he awaited punishment and asked for frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 帝猶降溫旨，言「卿報國盡忱，終始勿替，」許馳驛歸，賜路費百金，以彰保全優禮之意。

translations.literal: The emperor still sent a mild edict saying you served the state with full loyalty from start to finish without change, permitted return by courier post, and gave a hundred cash travel expenses to show care in preservation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a mild edict and travel money.

sentences.zh: 及廷臣議上，帝復諭延儒功多罪寡，令免議。

translations.literal: When court ministers submitted deliberation the emperor again said Yanru's merit was great and guilt small and ordered exemption from deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted deliberation, citing great merit.

sentences.zh: 延儒遂歸。

translations.literal: Yanru then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru went home.

sentences.zh: 既去，給事中郝絅疏請除奸，以指延儒。

translations.literal: After he left Supervising Secretary Hao Jiong memorialized requesting removal of traitors, pointing at Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jiong asked to remove Yanru as a traitor.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 山東僉事雷縯祚糾範志完，亦及延儒。

translations.literal: Shandong Assistant Commissioner Lei Peizuo impeached Fan Zhigang and also touched Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Peizuo impeached Fan Zhigang and Yanru.

sentences.zh: 已而御史蔣拱宸劾吳昌時贓私巨萬，大抵牽連延儒，而中言昌時通中官李端、王裕民，洩漏機密，重賄入手，輒預揣溫旨告人。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Jiang Gongchen impeached Wu Changshi for tens of thousands in illicit wealth, mostly implicating Yanru; inner words said Changshi communicated with eunuchs Li Duan and Wang Yumin, leaked secrets, took heavy bribes, and always guessed warm edicts to inform others.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongchen charged Changshi with vast graft tied to Yanru and eunuch leaks.

sentences.zh: 給事中曹良直亦劾延儒十大罪。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Cao Liangzhi also impeached Yanru for ten great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liangzhi charged ten great crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，禦中左門，親鞫昌時，折其脛，無所承，怒不解，拱宸面訐其通內，帝察之有跡，乃下獄論死，始有意誅延儒。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry, attended the central left gate, personally tried Changshi, broke his shins—nothing confessed; anger unabated; Gongchen face-to-face denounced his communicating with the inner palace; the emperor perceived traces and sent him to prison for death; he then intended to execute Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried Changshi brutally, then turned on Yanru.

sentences.zh: 初，薛國觀賜死，謂昌時致之。

translations.literal: At first when Xue Guoguan was granted death it was said Changshi caused it.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guoguan's death was blamed on Changshi.

sentences.zh: 其門人魏藻德新入閣有寵，恨昌時甚，因與陳演共排延儒，養性復騰蜚語。

translations.literal: His student Wei Zaode newly entered the Grand Secretariat with favor and hated Changshi deeply; he therefore with Chen Yan jointly overturned Yanru; Yangxing again spread slander.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode and Chen Yan joined Yangxing to destroy Yanru.

sentences.zh: 帝遂命盡削延儒職，遣緹騎逮入京師。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered all Yanru's offices stripped and brocade riders to arrest him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru was stripped and arrested to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時舊輔王應熊被召，延儒知帝怒甚，宿留道中，俟應熊先入，冀為請。

translations.literal: At the time old assistant Wang Yingxiong was summoned; Yanru knew the emperor's anger was great and lodged on the road, waiting for Yingxiong to enter first, hoping he would plead.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru delayed on the road hoping Yingxiong would plead for him.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，應熊既抵京，命之歸。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this; when Yingxiong reached the capital he was ordered to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yingxiong home.

sentences.zh: 延儒至，安置正陽門外古廟，上疏乞哀，不許。

translations.literal: When Yanru arrived he was lodged at an old temple outside Zhengyang Gate, memorialized begging pity—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was lodged outside Zhengyang Gate and denied mercy.

sentences.zh: 法司以戍請，同官申救，皆不許。

translations.literal: The judiciary requested garrison; colleagues interceded—all not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The judiciary and colleagues failed to save him.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，昌時棄市，命勒延儒自盡，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the twelfth winter month Changshi was executed in the market; Yanru was ordered to take his own life; his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Changshi was executed; Yanru was ordered to kill himself; his estate was seized.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁

translations.literal: Wen Tiren
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren

sentences.zh: 溫體仁，字長卿，烏程人。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren, style Zhangqing, was a man of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren, courtesy name Zhangqing, was a native of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Wanli year 26.

sentences.zh: 改庶起士，授編修，累官禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Changed to commoner graduate, appointed compiler, and rose in successive offices to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin compiler and rose to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初遷尚書，協理詹事府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was transferred to minister and assisted in the Grand Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he became minister and assisted the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為人外謹而中猛鷙，機深刺骨。

translations.literal: Outwardly cautious yet inwardly fierce and crafty, deep in scheming and piercing.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly cautious, inwardly fierce and scheming.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年冬，詔會推閣臣，體仁望輕，不與也。

translations.literal: In the first winter of Chongzhen year 1 an edict ordered collective recommendation for Grand Secretariat members; Tiren's standing was light and he was not included.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 1 he was omitted from Grand Secretariat recommendation.

sentences.zh: 侍郎周延儒方以召對稱旨，亦弗及。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhou Yanru was then praised for summoned audience; he also was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yanru was also omitted.

sentences.zh: 體仁揣帝意必疑，遂上疏訐謙益關節受賄，神奸結黨，不當與閣臣選。

translations.literal: Tiren guessed the emperor must be suspicious and therefore memorialized attacking Qianyi for taking bribes in the metropolitan examination, divine treachery forming factions—unfit for Grand Secretariat selection.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren attacked Qian Qianyi for examination bribery and faction.

sentences.zh: 先是，天啟二年，謙益主試浙江，所取士錢千秋者，首場文用俚俗詩一句，分置七義結尾，蓋奸人紿為之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the second year of Tianqi, Qianyi presided over the Zhejiang examination; the scholar he took, Qian Qianqiu, in the first session used a vulgar verse line, placing it in the seven exegesis endings—a trick by villains.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year 2 Qianyi's candidate Qian Qianqiu used a fraudulent examination trick.

sentences.zh: 為給事中顧其仁所摘，謙益亦自發其事。

translations.literal: It was exposed by Supervising Secretary Gu Qiren; Qianyi also himself reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Qiren exposed it; Qianyi reported it himself.

sentences.zh: 法司戍千秋及奸人，奪謙益俸，案久定矣。

translations.literal: The judiciary garrisoned Qianqiu and the villains and stripped Qianyi's salary—the case had long been settled.
translations.idiomatic: The case had long been settled with punishments.

sentences.zh: 至是體仁復理其事，帝心動。

translations.literal: Now Tiren revived the affair; the emperor's mind was moved.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren revived the case and moved the emperor.

sentences.zh: 次日，召對閣部科道諸臣於文華殿，命體仁、謙益皆至。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Grand Secretariat, ministries, and censorial officials to audience at Wenhua Hall and ordered Tiren and Qianyi both to come.
translations.idiomatic: The next day both men were summoned to Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 謙益不虞體仁之劾己也，辭頗屈，而體仁盛氣詆謙益，言如湧泉，因進曰：「臣職非言官不可言，會推不與，宜避嫌不言，但枚卜大典，宗社安危所系。

translations.literal: Qianyi did not expect Tiren's impeachment of himself; his words were rather bent, while Tiren with full air reviled Qianyi, words like a spring, and advanced: My office is not that of a speaking official and I should not speak; I was not in collective recommendation and should avoid suspicion and not speak—but the great ceremony of divination is what the altars and state safety depend on.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was unprepared; Tiren denounced him fiercely at the divination ceremony.

sentences.zh: 謙益結黨受賄，舉朝無一人敢言者，臣不忍見皇上孤立於上，是以不得不言。

translations.literal: Qianyi forms factions and takes bribes; not a single person in court dares speak; your servant cannot bear to see Your Majesty alone above—therefore I must speak.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren claimed Qianyi's faction silenced the court.

sentences.zh: 」帝久疑廷臣植党，聞體仁言，輒稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor had long suspected court ministers of planting factions; hearing Tiren he repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, suspecting factions, praised Tiren.

sentences.zh: 而執政皆言謙益無罪，吏科都給事中章允儒爭尤力，且言：「體仁熱中觖望，如謙益當糾，何俟今日。

translations.literal: Yet those in power all said Qianyi was innocent; Chief Supervising Secretary Zhang Yunru argued especially forcefully and also said: Tiren is eager and looks sideways; if Qianyi should be impeached, why wait until today.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers defended Qianyi; Zhang Yunru said Tiren was eager and late.

sentences.zh: 」體仁曰：「前此，謙益皆閑曹，今者糾之，正為朝廷慎用人耳。

translations.literal: Tiren said: Before this Qianyi was all idle posts; now impeaching him is just being careful in employing men for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren said he impeached Qianyi only now that it mattered.

sentences.zh: 如允儒言，乃真黨也。

translations.literal: As Yunru says, that is true faction.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren called Yunru the real faction.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，命禮部進千秋卷，閱意，責謙益，謙益引罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, ordered the Ministry of Rites to bring Qianqiu's paper, read it, blamed Qianyi; Qianyi confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Qianqiu's paper and blamed Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「微體仁，朕幾誤！

translations.literal: He sighed: Without Tiren I would nearly have erred!
translations.idiomatic: He sighed that without Tiren he would have erred.

sentences.zh: 」遂叱允儒下詔獄，並切責諸大臣。

translations.literal: He then shouted Yunru down to the imperial prison and sharply rebuked all great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yunru was imprisoned; ministers were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 時大臣無助體仁者，獨延儒奏曰：「會推名雖公，主持者止一二人，餘皆不敢言，即言，徒取禍耳。

translations.literal: At this time no great minister aided Tiren; only Yanru memorialized: Though collective recommendation's name is public, only one or two preside; the rest dare not speak; even if they speak they only invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanru defended Tiren on collective recommendation.

sentences.zh: 且千秋事有成案，不必復問諸臣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Qianqiu affair has a settled case; there is no need to ask the ministers again.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said the Qianqiu case was closed.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃即日罷謙益官，命議罪。

translations.literal: The emperor then that day dismissed Qianyi from office and ordered deliberation on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was dismissed that day.

sentences.zh: 允儒及給事中瞿式耜、御史房可壯等，皆坐謙益黨，降謫有差。

translations.literal: Yunru and Supervising Secretary Qu Shigao, Censor Fang Kezhuang, and others were all judged Qianyi's faction and demoted with varying severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yunru and others were punished as Qianyi's faction.

sentences.zh: 亡何，御史毛九華劾體仁居家時，以抑買商人木，為商人所訴，賂崔呈秀以免。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Mao Jihua impeached that when Tiren was at home he suppressed merchants buying timber and was sued by merchants, bribing Cui Chengxiu to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jihua charged Tiren with timber extortion and bribing Cui Chengxiu.

sentences.zh: 又困杭州建逆祠，作詩頌魏忠賢。

translations.literal: Also in Hangzhou he was forced to build a traitor shrine and composed poetry praising Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was said to have praised Wei Zhongxian in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝下浙江巡撫核實。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Zhejiang grand coordinator to verify.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered verification in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明年春，御史任贊化亦劾體仁娶娼、受金，奪人產諸不法事。

translations.literal: The next spring Censor Ren Zanhua also impeached Tiren for marrying a prostitute, taking gold, and seizing others' property—many unlawful matters.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zanhua charged prostitution, bribes, and seizure of property.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其語褻，貶一秩調外。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at the vulgar words and demoted one rank and transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted Ren Zanhua one rank.

sentences.zh: 體仁乞罷，因言：「比為謙益故，排擊臣者百出。

translations.literal: Tiren begged to resign, saying: Lately because of Qianyi, attacks on your servant number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren begged to resign, citing attacks over Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 而無一人左袒臣，臣孤立可見。

translations.literal: Yet not a single person takes your servant's side—your servant's isolation is visible.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he stood alone.

sentences.zh: 」帝再召內閣九卿質之，體仁與九華、贊化詰辯良久，言二人皆謙益死黨。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned the Grand Secretariat and nine ministers to examine; Tiren and Jihua and Zanhua argued for a long time, saying the two were both Qianyi's dead faction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned ministers; Tiren called his accusers Qianyi's faction.

sentences.zh: 帝心以為然，獨召大學士韓爌等於內殿，諭諸臣不憂國，惟挾私相攻，當重繩以法。

translations.literal: The emperor in his heart thought it so, alone summoned Grand Secretary Han Kuang and others in the inner hall, telling them the ministers did not worry for the state but only attacked with private motives—should be heavily punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Han Kuang the ministers attacked from private motives.

sentences.zh: 體仁復力求去以要帝，帝優詔慰答焉。

translations.literal: Tiren again strongly sought to leave to compel the emperor; the emperor replied with gracious edict of comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren threatened resignation; the emperor comforted him.

sentences.zh: 已，給事中祖重曄、南京給事中錢允鯨、南京御史沈希詔相繼論體仁熱中會推，劫言者以黨，帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: Before long Supervising Secretary Zu Chongye, Nanjing Supervising Secretary Qian Yunjing, and Nanjing Censor Shen Xichao in succession discussed Tiren's eagerness in collective recommendation and coercing speakers with faction charges—the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: More censors attacked Tiren; the emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 法司上千秋獄，言謙益自發在前，不宜坐。

translations.literal: The judiciary submitted the Qianqiu case, saying Qianyi reported it himself first and should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The judiciary said Qianyi had reported first and should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 詔令再勘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered renewed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered reinvestigation.

sentences.zh: 體仁復疏言獄詞皆出謙益手。

translations.literal: Tiren again memorialized that the case words all came from Qianyi's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren said the case was Qianyi's fabrication.

sentences.zh: 於是刑部尚書喬允升，左都御史曹於汴，大理寺卿康新民，太僕寺卿蔣允儀，府丞魏光緒，給事中陶崇道，御史吳甡、樊尚璟、劉廷佐，各疏言：「臣等雜治千秋，觀聽者數千人，非一手一口所能掩。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng, Left Censor-in-chief Cao Yubian, Court of Justice Director Kang Xinmin, Court of the Imperial Stud Director Jiang Yunyi, prefectural vice director Wei Guangxu, Supervising Secretary Tao Chongdao, and Censors Wu Shen, Fan Shangjing, and Liu Tingzuo each memorialized: Your servants jointly tried Qianqiu; observers numbered several thousand—not one hand and mouth can cover it.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials said the Qianqiu case could not be covered up.

sentences.zh: 體仁顧欺岡求勝。

translations.literal: Tiren only deceives and seeks victory.
translations.idiomatic: They said Tiren deceived to win.

sentences.zh: 」體仁見於汴等詞直，乃不復深論千秋事，惟詆於汴等黨護而已。

translations.literal: Tiren, seeing Yubian and others' words were straight, then did not deeply discuss the Qianqiu affair, only reviled Yubian and others for factional protection.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren stopped pressing Qianqiu and attacked factional protection.

sentences.zh: 謙益坐杖論贖，而九華所論體仁媚璫詩，亦卒無左驗。

translations.literal: Qianyi was punished with beating and ransom; Jihua's charge of Tiren flattering the eunuchs in poetry also in the end had no corroboration.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was beaten and ransomed; the Wei praise charge failed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，體仁以私憾撐拒諸大臣，輾轉不肯詘。

translations.literal: At this time Tiren with private resentment resisted the great ministers, turning and refusing to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren resisted ministers from private grudges.

sentences.zh: 帝謂體仁孤立，益響之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Tiren isolated and was all the more pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought him isolated and favored him more.

sentences.zh: 未幾，延儒入閣。

translations.literal: Before long Yanru entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yanru entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其明年六月，遂命體仁以禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: The next year in the sixth month he was ordered that Tiren be minister of Rites concurrently with Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In month 6 of the next year Tiren became Eastern Pavilion grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 體仁既藉延儒力得輔政，勢益張。

translations.literal: Tiren, relying on Yanru's power to obtain assisting government, grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on Yanru, Tiren grew more powerful.

sentences.zh: 逾年，吏部尚書王永光去，用其鄉人閔洪學代之，凡異己者，率以部議論罷，而體仁陰護其事。

translations.literal: After a year Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang left; his townsman Min Hongxue replaced him; whoever differed from him was mostly dismissed through ministry deliberation while Tiren secretly protected the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Min Hongxue replaced Wang Yongguang and Tiren purged opponents through the ministry.

sentences.zh: 又用御史史褷、高捷及侍郎唐世濟、副都御史張捷等為腹心，忌延儒居己上，並思傾之。

translations.literal: He also used Censors Shi Qian and Gao Jie and Vice Minister Tang Shiji and Vice Censor-in-chief Zhang Jie as heart and belly, jealous that Yanru was above him, and also wished to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: He used Shi Qian, Gao Jie, Tang Shiji, and Zhang Jie against Yanru.

sentences.zh: 初，帝殺袁崇煥，事牽錢龍錫，論死。

translations.literal: At first the emperor executed Yuan Chonghuan; the affair implicated Qian Longxi and judged death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chonghuan's case implicated Qian Longxi.

sentences.zh: 體仁與延儒、永光主之，將興大獄，梁廷棟不敢任而止，事詳龍錫傳。

translations.literal: Tiren with Yanru and Yongguang presided and were about to raise a great case; Liang Tingdong dared not undertake it and stopped—affairs detailed in Longxi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: They nearly raised a great case until Liang Tingdong stopped it.

sentences.zh: 比龍錫減死出獄，延儒言帝盛怒解救殊難，體仁則佯曰：「帝固不甚怒也。

translations.literal: When Longxi's death was reduced and he left prison, Yanru said the emperor's great anger made rescue very hard; Tiren then falsely said: The emperor in fact is not very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said rescue was hard; Tiren claimed the emperor was not angry.

sentences.zh: 」善龍錫者，因薄延儒。

translations.literal: Those friendly to Longxi therefore thought lightly of Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi's friends despised Yanru.

sentences.zh: 其後太監王坤、給事中陳贊化先後劾延儒，體仁默為助，延儒遂免歸。

translations.literal: Afterward eunuch Wang Kun and Supervising Secretary Chen Zanhua successively impeached Yanru; Tiren silently assisted; Yanru was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun and Chen Zanhua impeached Yanru with Tiren's help.

sentences.zh: 始與延儒同入閣者何如寵，錢象坤逾歲致政去，無何，如寵亦去。

translations.literal: At first He Rulong entered the Grand Secretariat with Yanru; Qian Xiangkun after a year retired; before long Rulong also left.
translations.idiomatic: He Rulong and others left the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 延儒既罷，廷臣惡體仁當國，勸帝復召如寵。

translations.literal: After Yanru was dismissed court ministers hated Tiren holding the state and urged the emperor to recall Rulong.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged recalling He Rulong.

sentences.zh: 如寵屢辭，給事中黃紹傑言：「君子小人不並立，如寵瞻顧不前，則體仁宜思自處。

translations.literal: Rulong repeatedly declined; Supervising Secretary Huang Shaojie said: Gentlemen and petty men cannot stand together; if Rulong hesitates, Tiren should consider his place.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaojie said Rulong should enter or Tiren should yield.

sentences.zh: 」帝為謫紹傑於外，如寵卒辭不入，體仁遂為首輔。

translations.literal: The emperor demoted Shaojie outside; Rulong in the end declined and did not enter; Tiren then became chief assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie was exiled; Rulong refused; Tiren became chief assistant.

sentences.zh: 體仁荷帝殊寵，益忮橫，而中阻深。

translations.literal: Tiren received the emperor's special favor and grew all the more jealous and overbearing, yet inwardly obstructed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by the emperor, Tiren grew jealous and obstructive.

sentences.zh: 所欲推薦，陰令人發端，己承其後。

translations.literal: Whomever he wished to recommend he secretly had others raise the matter; he then followed after.
translations.idiomatic: He had others start recommendations he then endorsed.

sentences.zh: 欲排陷，故為寬假，中上所忌，激使自怒。

translations.literal: When he wished to entrap someone he purposely showed leniency, hitting what the emperor tabooed, inciting self-incrimination.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned leniency to trap victims into provoking the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝往往為之移，初未嘗有跡。

translations.literal: The emperor often shifted because of this; at first there was never a trace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often shifted without visible cause.

sentences.zh: 姚希孟為講官，以才望遷詹事。

translations.literal: Yao Ximeng as lecturer was transferred to junior mentor for talent and standing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ximeng was promoted for talent.

sentences.zh: 體仁惡其逼，乃以冒籍武生事，奪希孟一官，使掌南院去。

translations.literal: Tiren hated his pressing close and used a military-student false-registration affair to strip Ximeng one rank and send him to manage the southern academy.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren stripped Yao Ximeng and sent him to the southern academy.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎羅喻義，故嘗與基命、謙益同推閣臣，有物望。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Luo Yuyi had once with Jiming and Qianyi been jointly recommended for the Grand Secretariat and had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuyi had once been recommended for the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 會進講章中有「左右未得人」語，體仁欲去之，喻義執不可。

translations.literal: It happened in advancing lecture chapters there were words the left and right have not obtained the right men; Tiren wished to remove him; Yuyi insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren tried to remove Luo Yuyi over lecture wording.

sentences.zh: 體仁因自劾：「日講進規例從簡，喻義駁改不從，由臣不能表率。

translations.literal: Tiren therefore impeached himself: Daily lecture admonitions are routinely brief; Yuyi refuted and changed without following—because your servant cannot set an example.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren impeached himself to attack Luo Yuyi.

sentences.zh: 」帝命吏部議，洪學等因謂：「聖聰天亶，何俟喻義多言。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Personnel to deliberate; Hongxue and others therefore said: The sage's hearing is heavenly—why wait for Yuyi's many words.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel ministry sided with Tiren against Luo Yuyi.

sentences.zh: 」喻義遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Yuyi was then dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuyi was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時魏忠賢遺黨日望體仁翻逆案，攻東林。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Zhongxian's remnant faction daily hoped Tiren would reverse the traitor case and attack the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei loyalists hoped Tiren would reverse the traitor case.

sentences.zh: 會吏部尚書、左都御史缺，體仁陰使侍郎張捷舉逆案呂純如以嘗帝。

translations.literal: It happened the Ministry of Personnel and left censor-in-chief were vacant; Tiren secretly had Vice Minister Zhang Jie recommend traitor-case Lu Chunru to please the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren tried to install Lu Chunru via Zhang Jie.

sentences.zh: 言者大嘩，帝亦甚惡之。

translations.literal: Speakers were in uproar; the emperor also greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: The court and emperor rejected Lu Chunru.

sentences.zh: 捷氣沮，體仁不敢言，乃薦謝升、唐世濟為之。

translations.literal: Jie lost spirit; Tiren dared not speak and then recommended Xie Sheng and Tang Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie failed; Tiren recommended Xie Sheng and Tang Shiji.

sentences.zh: 世濟尋以薦逆案霍維華得罪去。

translations.literal: Shiji soon was punished for recommending traitor-case Huo Weihua and left.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shiji fell for recommending Huo Weihua.

sentences.zh: 維華之薦，亦體仁主之也，體仁自是不敢訟言用逆黨，而愈側目諸不附己者。

translations.literal: Weihua's recommendation was also presided over by Tiren; Tiren himself then dared not openly argue for using traitor-faction men, yet all the more glared at those not attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren stopped openly using traitor men but attacked opponents.

sentences.zh: 文震孟以講《春秋》稱旨，命入閣。

translations.literal: Wen Zhenmeng was pleasing for lecturing on the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered into the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhenmeng entered the cabinet for lecturing on the Annals.

sentences.zh: 體仁不能沮，薦其党張至發以間之，而日伺震孟短，遂用給事中許譽卿事，逐之去。

translations.literal: Tiren could not obstruct and recommended his faction member Zhang Zhifa to come between; daily he watched for Zhenmeng's faults; then used Supervising Secretary Xu Yuqing's affair to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren used Zhang Zhifa and Xu Yuqing's case to oust Wen Zhenmeng.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦、楚盜起，議設五省總督，兵部侍郎彭汝楠、汪慶百當行，憚不敢往，體仁庇二人，罷其議。

translations.literal: Earlier Qin and Chu bandits rose; they discussed setting five-province grand coordinators; Vice Minister of War Peng Runan and Wang Qingbai should go; they feared and dared not go; Tiren sheltered the two and stopped the discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren blocked five-province coordinators when Peng Runan and Wang Qingbai refused.

sentences.zh: 賊犯鳳陽，南京兵部尚書呂維祺等議，令淮撫、操江移鎮，體仁又卻不用。

translations.literal: Bandits invaded Fengyang; Nanjing Minister of War Lu Weiqi and others discussed ordering Huai grand coordinator and river commander to shift garrison; Tiren again rejected and did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren rejected shifting troops when bandits threatened Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大至，焚皇陵。

translations.literal: Before long bandits came in force and burned the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits burned the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 譽卿言：「體仁納賄庇私，貽憂要地，以皇陵為孤注，使原廟震驚，誤國孰大焉。

translations.literal: Yuqing said: Tiren takes bribes and shelters private interests, brings worry to key places, stakes the imperial tombs as a lone wager, makes the original temples shaken in alarm—who errs against the state more?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing charged Tiren with risking the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 」體仁素忌譽卿，見疏益憾。

translations.literal: Tiren had long been jealous of Yuqing; seeing the memorial he hated all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren hated Xu Yuqing more.

sentences.zh: 會謝升以營求北缺劾譽卿，體仁擬旨降調，而故重其詞。

translations.literal: It happened Xie Sheng impeached Yuqing for seeking a northern vacancy; Tiren drafted the rescript for demotion yet purposely made the wording heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren drafted a harsh rescript against Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 帝果命削籍，震孟力爭之，大學士何吾騶助為言。

translations.literal: The emperor indeed ordered struck from the rolls; Zhenmeng strongly argued; Grand Secretary He Wuzuo assisted in speaking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck Yuqing from the rolls despite Wen Zhenmeng's protest.

sentences.zh: 體仁訐奏震孟語，謂言官罷斥為至榮，蓋以朝廷賞罰為不足懲勸，悖理蔑法。

translations.literal: Tiren memorialized attacking Zhenmeng's words, saying that dismissing censors was supreme glory, treating court reward and punishment as insufficient warning—rebellious to reason and scorning law.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren accused Wen Zhenmeng of scorning punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝遂逐震孟並罷吾騶。

translations.literal: The emperor then drove out Zhenmeng and also dismissed Wuzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhenmeng and He Wuzuo were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 震孟既去，體仁憾未釋。

translations.literal: After Zhenmeng left Tiren's resentment was not released.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren's resentment continued.

sentences.zh: 庶起士鄭鄤與震孟同建言，相友善也，其從母舅大學士吳宗達謝政歸。

translations.literal: Commoner graduate Zheng Man with Zhenmeng together remonstrated and were friendly; his mother's elder brother Grand Secretary Wu Zongda retired home.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Man was allied with Wen Zhenmeng; Wu Zongda had retired.

sentences.zh: 體仁劾鄤假乩仙判詞，逼父振先杖母，言出宗達。

translations.literal: Tiren impeached Man for false spirit-writing verdicts, forcing his father Zhenxian to beat his mother, words coming from Zongda.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren charged Zheng Man with forcing his father to beat his mother.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，下鄤獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was shocked and angry and sent Man to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Man was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 其後體仁已去，而帝怒鄤甚，不俟佐證，磔死。

translations.literal: Afterward Tiren had already left yet the emperor's anger at Man was great; without waiting for corroboration he was dismembered alive.
translations.idiomatic: After Tiren left, Zheng Man was dismembered without trial.

sentences.zh: 滋陽知縣成德，震孟門人，以強直忤巡按御史禹好善，被誣劾，震孟為不平。

translations.literal: Ziyang Magistrate Cheng De, Zhenmeng's student, for bluntness offended surveillance censor Yu Haoshan and was falsely impeached; Zhenmeng was indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng De, Wen Zhenmeng's student, was impeached for offending a censor.

sentences.zh: 體仁劾德，杖戍之。

translations.literal: Tiren impeached De, beat him and sent him to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren had Cheng De beaten and exiled.

sentences.zh: 體仁輔政數年，念朝士多與為怨，不敢恣肆，用廉謹自結於上，苞苴不入門。

translations.literal: Tiren assisted government several years, thinking many courtiers bore him resentment and not daring to act wildly, used frugality and caution to bind himself to the emperor; gifts did not enter his gate.
translations.idiomatic: For years Tiren acted cautiously and refused gifts publicly.

sentences.zh: 然當是時，流寇躪畿輔，擾中原，邊警雜遝，民生日困，未嘗建一策，惟日與善類為仇。

translations.literal: Yet at this time roving bandits trampled the capital region and disturbed the central plain; border alarms came in succession; people's lives daily grew distressed—he never established a single policy, only daily made enemies of the good.
translations.idiomatic: Amid collapse he offered no policy and only attacked the good.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉孔昭劾倪元璐，給事中陳啟新劾黃景昉，皆奉體仁指。

translations.literal: Earl of Sincerity Liu Kongzhao impeached Ni Yuanlu; Supervising Secretary Chen Qixin impeached Huang Jingfang—both followed Tiren's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kongzhao and Chen Qixin attacked Ni Yuanlu and Huang Jingfang for Tiren.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎陳子壯嘗面責體仁，尋以議宗籓事忤帝指，竟下獄削籍。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Chen Zizhuang once face-to-face rebuked Tiren; soon on discussing imperial clan affairs offended the emperor's intent and was sent to prison and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zizhuang rebuked Tiren and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 其所引與同列者，皆庸材，苟以充位，且藉形己長，固上寵。

translations.literal: Those he introduced as colleagues were all mediocre talents, merely filling posts and also by contrast showing his own length, solidifying imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were mediocrities who made him look capable.

sentences.zh: 帝每訪兵餉事，輒遜謝曰：「臣夙以文章待罪禁林，上不知其駑下，擢至此位。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor inquired on military pay affairs he would defer, saying: Your servant long served with literary talent awaiting punishment in the forbidden academy; Your Majesty did not know my dullness and promoted me to this post.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed ignorance of military affairs when asked.

sentences.zh: 盜賊日益眾，誠萬死不足塞責。

translations.literal: Bandits daily grow numerous; truly ten thousand deaths cannot fill the blame.
translations.idiomatic: He said he deserved death as bandits multiplied.

sentences.zh: 顧臣愚無知，但票擬勿欺耳。

translations.literal: Yet your servant is foolish and without knowledge; only drafting rescripts without deception.
translations.idiomatic: He said he could only draft rescripts honestly.

sentences.zh: 兵食之事，惟聖明裁決。

translations.literal: Military and food affairs—only the sage may decide.
translations.idiomatic: He deferred military decisions to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」有詆其窺帝意旨者，體仁言：「臣票擬多未中窾要，每經御筆批改，頌服將順不暇，詎能窺上旨。

translations.literal: Some reviled him for peering at the emperor's intent; Tiren said: Your servant's drafts mostly miss the crux; each time corrected by the imperial brush, praising and following without leisure—how could he peer at Your Majesty's intent?
translations.idiomatic: He denied reading the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 」帝以為樸忠，愈親信之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought him plain and loyal and was all the more intimate and trusting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found him plain and loyal.

sentences.zh: 自體仁輔政後，同官非病免物故，即以他事去。

translations.literal: After Tiren assisted government, colleagues unless ill, dismissed, or dead left on other affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues left through illness, death, or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 獨體仁居位八年，官至少師兼太子太師，進吏部尚書、中極殿大學士，階左柱國，兼支尚書俸，恩禮優渥無與比。

translations.literal: Only Tiren held office eight years, rising to junior master and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, minister of Personnel and grand secretary of the Central Peak Hall, rank left Pillar of the State, concurrently receiving ministerial salary—favor and ritual unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren held power eight years with unmatched honors.

sentences.zh: 而體仁專務刻核，迎合帝意。

translations.literal: Yet Tiren devoted himself to harsh scrutiny, meeting the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to harsh policies pleasing the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝以皇陵之變，從子壯言，下詔寬恤在獄諸臣，吏部以百餘人名上。

translations.literal: The emperor because of the imperial tomb change, following Zizhuang's words, issued an edict of lenient relief for prisoners; the Ministry of Personnel submitted more than a hundred names.
translations.idiomatic: After the tomb disaster the emperor ordered prisoner relief.

sentences.zh: 體仁靳之，言於帝，僅釋十餘人。

translations.literal: Tiren was stingy and told the emperor; only a dozen were released.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren allowed only a dozen releases.

sentences.zh: 秋決論囚，帝再三諮問，體仁略無平反。

translations.literal: Autumn execution discussed prisoners; the emperor repeatedly consulted; Tiren had almost no reversals.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren rarely reversed death sentences.

sentences.zh: 陝西華亭知縣徐兆麟涖任甫七日，以城陷論死，帝頗疑之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Huating Magistrate Xu Zhaolin had been in office only seven days when the city fell and he was judged to death; the emperor was rather suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhaolin was executed after seven days in office; the emperor doubted.

sentences.zh: 體仁不為救，竟棄市。

translations.literal: Tiren did not save him and in the end he was executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren let Xu Zhaolin be executed.

sentences.zh: 帝憂兵餉急，體仁惟倡眾捐俸助馬修城而已。

translations.literal: The emperor worried military pay was urgent; Tiren only advocated all donating salary to help horses and repair walls.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren only proposed salary donations for walls.

sentences.zh: 所上密揭，帝率報可。

translations.literal: Secret memorials submitted were mostly approved by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His secret memorials were usually approved.

sentences.zh: 體仁自念排擠者眾，恐怨歸己，倡言密勿之地，不宜宣洩，凡閣揭皆不發，並不存錄閣中，冀以滅跡，以故所中傷人，廷臣不能盡知。

translations.literal: Tiren himself thought those he excluded were many and feared blame would return to himself; he advocated that secret places should not be leaked; all cabinet rescripts were not issued and not kept in the Grand Secretariat, hoping to erase traces—therefore those he harmed, court ministers could not fully know.
translations.idiomatic: He hid cabinet records to conceal whom he harmed.

sentences.zh: 當國既久，劾者章不勝計，而劉宗周劾其十二罪、六奸，皆有指實。

translations.literal: Long holding the state, impeachment memorials were beyond counting; Liu Zongzhou impeached twelve crimes and six treacheries—all with concrete pointers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou charged twelve crimes and six treacheries.

sentences.zh: 宗籓如唐王聿鍵，勳臣如撫寧侯硃國弼，布衣如何儒顯、楊光先等，亦皆論之，光先至輿櫬待命。

translations.literal: Imperial clans such as Tang Prince Yuyi, meritorious nobles such as Marquis Zhu Guobi of Funing, commoners such as He Ruxian and Yang Guangxian—all were discussed; Guangxian even carried his coffin awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, nobles, and commoners all attacked him; Yang Guangxian awaited death in a coffin.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省，愈以為孤立，每斥責言者以慰之，至有杖死者。

translations.literal: The emperor paid no heed, all the more thought himself isolated, daily rebuked speakers to comfort Tiren—even to beating to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked and killed his critics.

sentences.zh: 庶起士張溥、知縣張采等倡為復社，與東林相應和。

translations.literal: Commoner graduates Zhang Pu and Magistrate Zhang Cai initiated the Restoration Society, echoing the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu and Zhang Cai founded the Restoration Society with the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 體仁因推官周之夔及奸人陸文聲訐奏，將興大獄。

translations.literal: Tiren through investigating censor Zhou Zhi and villain Lu Wensheng memorialized impeachment and was about to raise a great case.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren tried to raise a great case against the Restoration Society.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨察治，以提學御史倪元珙、海道副使馮元颺不承風指，皆降謫之。

translations.literal: Stern edict ordered investigation; because provincial censor Ni Yuanqi and coastal vice commissioner Feng Yuanbiao did not follow his intent, both were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanqi and Feng Yuanbiao were demoted for defying him.

sentences.zh: 最後復有張漢儒訐錢謙益、瞿式耜居鄉不法事。

translations.literal: Finally there was again Zhang Hanru impeaching Qian Qianyi and Qu Shigao for unlawful conduct at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hanru impeached Qianyi and Shigao at home.

sentences.zh: 體仁故仇謙益，擬旨逮二人下詔獄嚴訊。

translations.literal: Tiren, old enemy of Qianyi, drafted an edict arresting both and sending them to the imperial prison for strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren had Qianyi and Shigao arrested.

sentences.zh: 謙益等危甚，求解於司禮太監曹化淳。

translations.literal: Qianyi and others were in extreme peril and sought rescue from Director of Rites Eunuch Cao Huachun.
translations.idiomatic: They sought Cao Huachun's help.

sentences.zh: 漢儒偵知之，告體仁。

translations.literal: Hanru spied and knew, informing Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru informed Tiren.

sentences.zh: 體仁密奏帝，請並坐化淳罪。

translations.literal: Tiren secretly memorialized the emperor requesting joint punishment of Huachun.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren asked to punish Huachun too.

sentences.zh: 帝以示化淳，化淳懼，自請案治，乃盡得漢儒等奸狀及體仁密謀。

translations.literal: The emperor showed Huachun; Huachun was afraid and requested to investigate; then fully obtained Hanru and others' treacherous conduct and Tiren's secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: Huachun investigated and exposed Tiren's plot.

sentences.zh: 獄上，帝始悟體仁有黨。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted the emperor first understood Tiren had a faction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor realized Tiren had a faction.

sentences.zh: 會國弼再劾體仁，帝命漢儒等立枷死。

translations.literal: It happened Guobi again impeached Tiren; the emperor ordered Hanru and others immediately cangued to death.
translations.idiomatic: Guobi impeached Tiren; Hanru was cangued.

sentences.zh: 體仁乃佯引疾，意帝必慰留。

translations.literal: Tiren then falsely cited illness, thinking the emperor would certainly comfort and keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren feigned illness expecting retention.

sentences.zh: 及得旨竟放歸，體仁方食，失匕箸，時十年六月也。

translations.literal: When he received the edict he was actually released home; Tiren was eating and dropped his chopsticks—it was the sixth month of the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed in month 6 of year 10 and dropped his chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，帝猶惜之，贈太傅，諡文忠。

translations.literal: After a year he died; the emperor still regretted it, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the emperor posthumously honored him Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，福王立於南京，以尚書顧錫疇議，削其贈諡，天下快焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen when the Prince of Fu was established at Nanjing, on Minister Gu Xichou's deliberation his posthumous gifts were stripped—the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's court stripped his honors; the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 尋用給事中戴英言，復如初。

translations.literal: Soon on Supervising Secretary Dai Ying's words it was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: His honors were soon restored.

sentences.zh: 體仁雖前死，其所推薦張至發、薛國觀之徒，皆效法體仁，蔽賢植黨，國事日壞，以至於亡。

translations.literal: Though Tiren had died earlier, those he recommended—Zhang Zhifa, Xue Guoguan, and their kind—all imitated Tiren, screening the worthy and planting factions; state affairs daily worsened until ruin.
translations.idiomatic: His successors imitated him until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 馬士英

translations.literal: Ma Shiying
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying

sentences.zh: （阮大鋮）〉

translations.literal: (Ruan Dacheng)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ruan Dacheng)]〉

sentences.zh: 馬士英，貴陽人。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying was a man of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying was a native of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年，與懷寧阮大鋮同中會試。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he together with Huaining Ruan Dacheng passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 44 he and Ruan Dacheng passed the metropolitan exam.

sentences.zh: 又三年，士英成進士，授南京戶部主事。

translations.literal: Three years later Shiying passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he passed the jinshi and became a Nanjing Revenue director.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，遷郎中，曆知嚴州、河南、大同三府。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was transferred to director, served successively as prefect of Yanzhou, Henan, and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he became director and served as prefect of three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，遷山西陽和道副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Yanghe circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 3 he became Yanghe vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became Xuanfu grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 到官甫一月，檄取公帑數千金，饋遺朝貴，為鎮守太監王坤所發，坐遣戍。

translations.literal: One month after taking office he requisitioned several thousand cash of public funds to bribe court nobles; exposed by garrison eunuch Wang Kun, he was sentenced to garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was caught bribing with public funds and exiled.

sentences.zh: 尋流寓南京。

translations.literal: Before long he drifted to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon drifted to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時大鋮名掛逆案，失職久廢，以避流賊至，與士英相結甚歡。

translations.literal: At the time Dacheng's name hung on the traitor case; long dismissed from office; to avoid roving bandits he arrived and joined Shiying in great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng, long disgraced in the traitor case, joined Shiying in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 大鋮機敏猾賊，有才藻。

translations.literal: Dacheng was clever, slippery, and talented in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was clever, treacherous, and literary.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，由行人擢給事中，以憂歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was promoted from courier to supervising secretary and returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he became supervising secretary then mourned at home.

sentences.zh: 同邑左光斗為御史有聲，大鋮倚為重。

translations.literal: His townsman Zuo Guangdou was a famous censor; Dacheng relied on him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on censor Zuo Guangdou of his town.

sentences.zh: 四年春，吏科都給事中缺，大鋮次當遷，光斗招之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Section was vacant; Dacheng was next to be promoted; Guangdou summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 spring Dacheng was due for chief supervising secretary; Guangdou summoned him.

sentences.zh: 而趙南星、高攀龍、楊漣等以察典近，大鋮輕躁不可任，欲用魏大中。

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Yang Lian, and others, because the evaluation was near, thought Dacheng light and rash and unfit for office, wishing to use Wei Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Donglin leaders preferred Wei Dazhong over Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 大鋮至，使補工科。

translations.literal: When Dacheng arrived they made him supplement the Engineering Section.
translations.idiomatic: They assigned Dacheng to the Engineering Section instead.

sentences.zh: 大鋮心恨，陰結中璫寢推大中疏。

translations.literal: Dacheng hated this in his heart and secretly joined inner eunuchs to suppress Dazhong's memorial overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng secretly had eunuchs suppress Dazhong's promotion.

sentences.zh: 吏部不得已，更上大鋮名，即得請。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel had no choice but to resubmit Dacheng's name; he immediately obtained the post.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel had to submit Dacheng's name; he got the post.

sentences.zh: 大鋮自是附魏忠賢，與霍維華、楊維垣、倪文煥為死友，造《百官圖》，因文煥達諸忠賢。

translations.literal: From this time Dacheng attached to Wei Zhongxian, with Huo Weihua, Yang Weiyuan, and Ni Wenhuai as sworn friends, made the Hundred Officers Chart, and through Wenhuai reached Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng joined Wei Zhongxian and made the Hundred Officers Chart.

sentences.zh: 然畏東林攻己，未一月遽請急歸。

translations.literal: Yet fearing Donglin attacks on himself, within a month he urgently requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Donglin, he fled home within a month.

sentences.zh: 而大中掌吏科，大鋮憤甚，私謂所親曰：「我猶善歸，未知左氏何如耳。

translations.literal: When Dazhong took the Personnel Section Dacheng was furious and privately told intimates: I can still go home well—who knows how the Zuo family will fare.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng raged when Dazhong won Personnel.

sentences.zh: 」已而楊、左諸人獄死，大鋮對客詡詡自矜。

translations.literal: Before long Yang, Zuo, and others died in prison; Dacheng boasted to guests.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang and Zuo died in prison Dacheng boasted.

sentences.zh: 尋召為太常少卿，至都，事忠賢極謹，而陰慮其不足恃，每進謁，輒厚賄忠賢閽人，還其刺。

translations.literal: Soon summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; reaching the capital he served Zhongxian extremely carefully yet secretly feared he could not be relied on; each audience he heavily bribed Zhongxian's gatekeepers and returned their cards.
translations.idiomatic: At court he served Zhongxian but bribed his gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 居數月，復乞歸。

translations.literal: After several months he again begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon begged leave again.

sentences.zh: 忠賢既誅，大鋮函兩疏馳示維垣。

translations.literal: After Zhongxian was executed Dacheng sent two memorials in a box to show Weiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongxian's fall Dacheng sent two memorials to Yang Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其一專劾崔、魏。

translations.literal: One solely impeached Cui and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: One impeached Cui and Wei.

sentences.zh: 其一以七年合算為言，謂天啟四年以後，亂政者忠賢，而翼以呈秀，四年以前，亂政者王安，而翼以東林。

translations.literal: One used a seven-year reckoning, saying after Tianqi year 4 the disorderly government was Zhongxian aided by Chengxiu, and before year 4 it was Wang An aided by the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: One blamed Donglin before year 4 and Wei after.

sentences.zh: 傳語維垣，若時局大變，上劾崔、魏疏，脫未定，則上算疏。

translations.literal: He told Weiyuan if the situation changed greatly, submit the Cui-Wei memorial first; if undecided, submit the reckoning memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He told Weiyuan which memorial to use when.

sentences.zh: 會維垣方並指東林、崔、魏為邪黨，與編修倪元璐相詆，得大鋮疏，大喜，為投合算疏以自助。

translations.literal: It happened Weiyuan was attacking Donglin, Cui, and Wei together as evil faction, quarreling with Compiler Ni Yuanlu; receiving Dacheng's memorial he was greatly pleased and submitted the reckoning memorial to help himself.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan used Dacheng's reckoning memorial against the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was raised as director of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 1 he was raised as director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 御史毛羽健劾其黨邪，罷去。

translations.literal: Censor Mao Yujian impeached his faction as evil; he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yujian impeached him; he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明年定逆案，論贖徒為民，終莊烈帝世，廢斥十七年，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: The next year the traitor case was settled; judged ransom exile as commoner; through Emperor Zhuanglie's reign he was rejected seventeen years, depressed and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor case exiled him for seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 流寇逼皖，大鋮避居南京，頗招納遊俠為談兵說劍，覬以邊才召。

translations.literal: When roving bandits pressed Anhui Dacheng fled to Nanjing, rather recruiting wandering knights to discuss arms and swords, hoping to be summoned for border talent.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjing he recruited bravos hoping for border appointment.

sentences.zh: 無錫顧杲、吳縣楊廷樞、蕪湖沈士柱、餘姚黃宗羲、鄞縣萬泰等，皆復社中名士，方聚講南京，惡大鋮甚，作《留都防亂揭》逐之。

translations.literal: Gu Gao of Wuxi, Yang Tinghu of Wu, Shen Shizhu of Wuhu, Huang Zongxi of Yuyao, Wan Tai of Yin, and others were all famous in the Restoration Society, then lecturing together in Nanjing, hated Dacheng greatly, and made the Nanjing Petition Against Disorder to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration Society figures expelled Dacheng with a public petition.

sentences.zh: 大鋮懼，乃閉門謝客，獨與士英深相結。

translations.literal: Dacheng was afraid, closed his door and declined guests, only joining deeply with Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Dacheng only clung to Shiying.

sentences.zh: 周延儒內召，大鋮輦金錢要之維揚，求湔濯。

translations.literal: When Yanru was summoned inward Dacheng carted gold to Weiyang to request cleansing.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng bribed Yanru at Weiyang for rehabilitation.

sentences.zh: 延儒曰：「吾此行，謬為東林所推。

translations.literal: Yanru said: My going this time was wrongly pushed by the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said the Donglin had pushed him.

sentences.zh: 子名在逆案，可乎？

translations.literal: Your name is on the traitor case—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Your name is on the traitor case—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」大鋮沉吟久之，曰：「瑤草何如？

translations.literal: Dacheng hesitated long and said: How about Yaocao?
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng suggested Yaocao—Shiying's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 」瑤草，士英別字也，延儒許之。

translations.literal: Yaocao is Shiying's other name; Yanru agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru agreed to use Shiying.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，鳳陽總督高鬥光以失五城逮治。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year Fengyang Grand Coordinator Gao Douguang was arrested for losing five cities.
translations.idiomatic: In month 6 of year 15 Gao Douguang was arrested for losing five cities.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎王錫兗薦士英才，延儒從中主之，遂起兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督廬、鳳等處軍務。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Wang Xiyao recommended Shiying's talent; Yanru backed it from within; he was then made right vice minister of War concurrently right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Luzhou, Fengyang, and other military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiyao and Yanru made Shiying grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 永城人劉超者，天啟中以征安邦彥功，積官至四川遵義總兵官，坐罪免，數營復官不得。

translations.literal: Liu Chao of Yongcheng in Tianqi for merit against An Bangyan rose to Datong zongbing in Sichuan, was dismissed for crime, and several times sought restoration without success.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao, a disgraced general, sought restoration.

sentences.zh: 李自成圍開封，超請募士冠協擊，乃用為保定總兵官，令率兵赴救。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng Chao requested recruiting volunteers to assist; he was used as Baoding zongbing and ordered to lead troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was made Baoding zongbing to relieve Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 超憚不敢行，宿留家中，以私怨殺御史魏景琦等三家，遂據城反。

translations.literal: Chao feared and dared not go, lingered at home, and from private grudge killed Censor Wei Jingqi and three households, then held the city in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Chao rebelled at home instead of marching.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王漢討之，被殺。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Han attacked him and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han was killed attacking him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命士英偕太監盧九德、河南總兵官陳永福進討。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Shiying with eunuch Lu Jiude and Henan zongbing Chen Yongfu to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying, Lu Jiude, and Chen Yongfu were sent against him.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，圍其城，連戰，賊屢挫，築長圍困之。

translations.literal: The next year in the fourth month they besieged the city; after repeated battles the rebels were often defeated and a long encirclement was built.
translations.idiomatic: In month 4 of the next year they besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 超官貴州時，與士英相識，緣舊好乞降。

translations.literal: When Chao was in Guizhou he knew Shiying; through old friendship he begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chao knew Shiying and offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 士英佯許之，超出見，不肯去佩刀。

translations.literal: Shiying pretended to agree; Chao came out to meet but would not leave his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying feigned agreement; Chao kept his sword.

sentences.zh: 士英笑曰：「若既歸朝，安用此？

translations.literal: Shiying laughed: If you have submitted to the court, what use is this?
translations.idiomatic: Shiying asked why he needed a sword if he submitted.

sentences.zh: 」手解其刀。

translations.literal: He personally unbuckled the sword.
translations.idiomatic: He took the sword.

sentences.zh: 已，潛去其親信，遂就縛。

translations.literal: Before long he secretly removed Chao's trusted men and then bound him.
translations.idiomatic: He disarmed Chao's men and seized him.

sentences.zh: 獻俘於朝，磔死。

translations.literal: Presented the captive at court; dismembered alive.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was dismembered at court.

sentences.zh: 時流寇充斥，士英捍禦數有功。

translations.literal: At the time roving bandits filled the land; Shiying had several defensive merits.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying had some merit against bandits.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，京師陷，帝崩，南京諸大臣聞變，倉卒議立君。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year the capital fell; the emperor died; Nanjing great ministers heard the change and hastily discussed establishing a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In month 3 of year 17 the capital fell; Nanjing debated a new ruler.

sentences.zh: 而福王由崧、潞王常淓俱避賊至淮安，倫序當屬福王。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Yousong and Prince Lu Changfan both fled bandits to Huai'an; by succession Fu should be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Lu princes fled to Huai'an; succession favored Fu.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣慮福王立，或追怨「妖書」及「挺擊」、「移宮」等案；

translations.literal: The great ministers feared establishing Fu might revive grievances over the Demon Book, Stick Assault, and Palace Shift cases.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers feared Fu would revive old case grievances.

sentences.zh: 潞王立，則無後患，且可邀功。

translations.literal: Establishing Lu would have no later trouble and merit could be sought.
translations.idiomatic: They preferred Lu for lack of backlash and possible merit.

sentences.zh: 陰主之者，廢籍禮部侍郎錢謙益，力持其議者兵部侍郎呂大器，而右都御史張慎言、詹事姜曰廣皆然之。

translations.literal: Those secretly leading were dismissed Minister Qian Qianyi; those strongly holding the argument were Vice Minister Lu Daqi; Right Censor-in-chief Zhang Shenyan and Mentor Jiang Yueguang all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qianyi led secretly for Lu; Lu Daqi and others favored Fu.

sentences.zh: 前山東按察使僉事雷縯祚、禮部員外郎周鑣往來遊說。

translations.literal: Former Shandong Assistant Commissioner Lei Peizuo and Rites Bureau director Zhou Biao went about lobbying.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Peizuo and Zhou Biao lobbied for Lu.

sentences.zh: 時士英督師廬、鳳，獨以為不可，密與操江誠意伯劉孔昭，總兵高傑、劉澤清、黃得功、劉良佐等結，而公致書於參贊機務兵部尚書史可法，言倫序親賢，無如福王。

translations.literal: Shiying alone supervising Luzhou and Fengyang thought it could not be done; secretly joined river-commander Earl Liu Kongzhao and generals Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, Huang Degong, and Liu Liangzuo, while openly writing to Coordinator Shi Kefa that by succession the close and worthy was none like Prince Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying allied with generals and eunuchs for Fu while writing Kefa on succession.

sentences.zh: 可法意未決。

translations.literal: Kefa had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa hesitated.

sentences.zh: 及廷臣集議，吏科給事中李沾探士英指，面折大器。

translations.literal: When court ministers assembled, Supervising Secretary Li Zhan probed Shiying's intent and face-to-face refuted Daqi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan refuted Daqi at assembly per Shiying's cue.

sentences.zh: 士英亦自廬、鳳擁兵迎福王至江上，諸大臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Shiying also from Luzhou and Fengyang led troops to welcome Prince Fu to the river; great ministers then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying marched troops to welcome Fu; ministers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 王之立，士英力也。

translations.literal: The prince's establishment was Shiying's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's throne was Shiying's work.

sentences.zh: 當王監國時，廷推閣臣，劉孔昭攘臂欲得之，可法折以勳臣無入閣例。

translations.literal: When the prince supervised the state, grand secretaries were collectively recommended; Liu Kongzhao stretched his arm wishing to obtain it; Kefa refused on the ground that meritorious nobles had no precedent for entering the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa blocked Kongzhao from the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 孔昭乃訟言：「我不可，士英何不可？

translations.literal: Kongzhao then argued: I cannot—why can Shiying not?
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao demanded Shiying enter the cabinet too.

sentences.zh: 」於是進士英東閣大學士兼兵部尚書、都察院右副都御史，與可法及戶部尚書高弘圖並命，士英仍督師鳳陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shiying was advanced Eastern Pavilion grand secretary concurrently minister of War and right vice censor-in-chief, appointed with Kefa and Minister Gao Hongtu; Shiying still supervised Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying became grand secretary with Kefa and Hongtu.

sentences.zh: 士英大慍，令高傑、劉澤清等疏趣可法督師淮、揚，而士英留輔政，仍掌兵部，權震中外。

translations.literal: Shiying was greatly angry, ordered Gao Jie and Liu Zeqing to memorialize urging Kefa to supervise Huai-Yang armies while Shiying remained assisting government, still holding War, power shaking within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying forced Kefa to the front while he held power in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋論定策功，加太子太師，廕錦衣衛指揮僉事。
