translations.literal: Soon discussing merit in fixing the succession, added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and ennobled a Brocade Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Guardian and ennobled his son.

sentences.zh: 九月，敘江北歷年戰功，加少傅兼太子太師、建極殿大學士，廕子如前。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, recounting years of merit north of the river, added junior tutor, Grand Guardian, Jianji Hall grand secretary, ennobling son as before.
translations.idiomatic: In month 9 he received more honors for northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 十二月，進少師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month advanced junior master.
translations.idiomatic: In month 12 he became junior master.

sentences.zh: 明年，進太保。

translations.literal: The next year advanced grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 當是時，中原郡縣盡失，高傑死睢州，諸鎮權侔無統。

translations.literal: At this time central plain commanderies and counties were all lost; Gao Jie died at Suizhou; the towns' power equaled each other without unity.
translations.idiomatic: The central plain was lost; generals were divided.

sentences.zh: 左良玉擁兵上流，跋扈有異志。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu held troops upstream, overbearing with different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu was rebellious upstream.

sentences.zh: 而士英為人貪鄙無遠略，復引用大鋮，日事報復，招權罔利，以迄於亡。

translations.literal: Shiying was greedy, base, and without far strategy, again employing Dacheng, daily taking revenge, usurping power for profit, until ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was greedy and employed Dacheng until ruin.

sentences.zh: 初，可法、弘圖及薑曰廣、張慎言等皆宿德在位，將以次引海內人望，而士英必欲起大鋮。

translations.literal: At first Kefa, Hongtu, Jiang Yueguang, Zhang Shenyan, and others were all established worthies in office, about to draw in turn the realm's hopes, yet Shiying must raise Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Established ministers were pushed aside for Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 有詔廣搜人材，獨立逆案不可輕議。

translations.literal: An edict broadly searched talent but alone said the traitor case could not be lightly discussed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict barred reopening the traitor case.

sentences.zh: 士英令孔昭及侯湯國祚、伯趙之龍等攻慎言去之，而薦大鋮知兵。

translations.literal: Shiying had Kongzhao and Marquis Tang Guozuo and Earl Zhao Zhilong attack Shenyan to remove him, then recommended Dacheng knew warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying removed Shenyan and praised Dacheng's military skill.

sentences.zh: 初，大鋮在南京，與守備太監韓贊周暱。

translations.literal: At first in Nanjing Dacheng was intimate with garrison eunuch Han Zanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was close to eunuch Han Zanzhou in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，中貴人悉南奔，大鋮因贊周遍結之，為群奄言東林當日所以危貴妃、福王者，俾備言於王，以潛傾可法等。

translations.literal: When the capital fell all inner eunuchs fled south; Dacheng through Zanzhou joined them all; the eunuch group said the Donglin once endangered Consort and Prince Fu, making them speak to the prince to secretly overturn Kefa and others.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng turned eunuchs against the Donglin and Kefa.

sentences.zh: 群奄更極口稱大鋮才，士英亦言大鋮從山中致書與定策謀，為白其附璫贊導無實跡。

translations.literal: The eunuchs extolled Dacheng's talent; Shiying also said Dacheng from the mountains sent letters on fixing the succession, whitewashing his attaching to eunuchs as without real trace.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and Shiying whitewashed Dacheng's past.

sentences.zh: 遂命大鋮冠帶陛見。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to audience in cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 大鋮乃上守江策，陳三要、兩合、十四隙疏，並自白孤忠被陷，痛詆孫慎行、魏大中、左光鬥，且指大中為大逆。

translations.literal: Dacheng then memorialized river defense strategy, three essentials, two unions, fourteen gaps, and self-whitewashed lonely loyalty wronged, bitterly reviling Sun Shenxing, Wei Dazhong, and Zuo Guangdou, even calling Dazhong great traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng attacked the Donglin and claimed loyalty.

sentences.zh: 於是大學士姜曰廣、侍郎呂大器、懷遠侯常延齡等並言大鋮逆案巨魁，不可召。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Secretary Jiang Yueguang, Vice Minister Lu Daqi, Marquis Chang Yanling, and others all said Dacheng was chief of the traitor case and could not be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yueguang and others opposed Dacheng's recall.

sentences.zh: 士英為大鋮奏辨，力攻曰廣、大器，益募宗室統昚、建安王統鏤輩，連疏交攻。

translations.literal: Shiying memorialized defense for Dacheng, fiercely attacking Yueguang and Daqi, further recruiting clansmen Tong Shen and Prince of Jian'an Tong Lou to attack in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying defended Dacheng and attacked opponents.

sentences.zh: 而以大學士高弘圖為御史時嘗詆東林，必當右己，乃言「弘圖素知臣者。

translations.literal: Thinking Grand Secretary Gao Hongtu as censor once reviled the Donglin and must favor himself, he said Hongtu always knew your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying thought Hongtu would favor him.

sentences.zh: 」弘圖則言先帝欽定逆案一書，不可擅改。

translations.literal: Hongtu said the late emperor's fixed traitor-case book could not be altered at will.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtu said the traitor case could not change.

sentences.zh: 士英與爭，弘圖因乞罷。

translations.literal: Shiying argued; Hongtu therefore begged to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtu resigned after arguing.

sentences.zh: 士英意稍折，遲回月余，用安遠侯柳祚昌薦，中旨起大鋮兵部添注右侍郎。

translations.literal: Shiying's intent slightly bent; hesitating over a month, on Marquis of Anyuan Liu Zuochang's recommendation a special edict raised Dacheng as added vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After a month a special edict made Dacheng vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 左都御史劉宗周言：「殺大中者魏璫，大鋮其主使也。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-chief Liu Zongzhou said: Who killed Dazhong was Wei Zhongxian; Dacheng was the mastermind.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou said Dacheng masterminded Dazhong's death.

sentences.zh: 即才果足用，臣慮黨邪害正之才，終病世道。

translations.literal: Even if talent truly sufficed to use, your servant fears talent of factional evil harming the upright will ultimately harm the age.
translations.idiomatic: He feared factional talent would harm the age.

sentences.zh: 大鋮進退，實系江左興亡，乞寢成命。

translations.literal: Dacheng's advance or retreat truly ties to the rise and fall of the left river region; beg to suspend the completed order.
translations.idiomatic: He said Dacheng's appointment threatened the southeast.

sentences.zh: 」有旨切責。

translations.literal: There was an edict sharply rebuking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大鋮兼右僉都御史，巡閱江防。

translations.literal: Before long Dacheng concurrently right vice censor-in-chief inspected river defense.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng inspected river defense.

sentences.zh: 尋轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon transferred left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He became left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 明年二月進本部尚書兼右副都御史，仍閱江防。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month advanced to minister of the ministry concurrently right vice censor-in-chief, still inspecting river defense.
translations.idiomatic: In month 2 of the next year he became minister while inspecting defenses.

sentences.zh: 呂大器、薑曰廣、劉宗周、高弘圖、徐石麒皆與士英齟齬，先後罷歸。

translations.literal: Lu Daqi, Jiang Yueguang, Liu Zongzhou, Gao Hongtu, and Xu Shilin all clashed with Shiying and were dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Opponents of Shiying were dismissed one by one.

sentences.zh: 士英獨握大柄，內倚中官田成輩，外結勳臣劉孔昭、硃國弼、柳祚昌，鎮將劉澤清、劉良佐等，而一聽大鋮計。

translations.literal: Shiying alone grasped great power, inward relying on eunuch Tian Cheng and others, outward joining meritorious nobles Kongzhao, Guobi, and Zuochang and generals Zeqing and Liangzuo, hearing only Dacheng's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying ruled with eunuchs, generals, and Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 盡起逆案中楊維垣、虞廷陛、郭如暗、周昌晉、虞大復、徐復陽、陳以瑞、吳孔嘉；

translations.literal: He fully raised from the traitor case Yang Weiyuan, Yu Tinglu, Guo Ru'an, Zhou Changjin, Yu Dafu, Xu Fuyang, Chen Yirui, and Wu Kongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He restored many traitor-case figures.

sentences.zh: 其死者悉予贈恤，而與張捷、唐世濟等比；

translations.literal: The dead were all granted posthumous consolation and compared with Zhang Jie and Tang Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dead traitor allies were posthumously honored.

sentences.zh: 若張孫振、袁弘勳、劉光鬥皆得罪先朝，復置言路為爪牙。

translations.literal: Zhang Sunzhen, Yuan Hongxun, and Liu Guangdou, all punished under the former court, were again placed on the speaking route as claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Punished men returned as censors.

sentences.zh: 朝政濁亂，賄賂公行。

translations.literal: Court government was turbid and chaotic; bribes were public.
translations.idiomatic: Government was corrupt and bribery rampant.

sentences.zh: 四方警報狎至，士英身掌中樞，一無籌畫，日以鋤正人引凶黨為務。

translations.literal: Alarms from the four directions came in succession; Shiying personally held the central pivot without a single plan, daily taking destroying upright men and introducing vicious factions as his task.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying attacked the upright and promoted villains.

sentences.zh: 初，舉朝以逆案攻大鋮，大鋮憾甚。

translations.literal: At first the whole court attacked Dacheng on the traitor case; Dacheng resented greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng resented the court's attacks.

sentences.zh: 及見北都從逆諸臣有附會清流者，因倡言曰：「彼攻逆案，吾作順案與之對。

translations.literal: When he saw northern capital followers of the bandits who attached to the clear stream, he therefore advocated: They attack the traitor case; I will make a Surrender Case to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a Surrender Case against the traitor case.

sentences.zh: 」以李自成偽國號曰順也。

translations.literal: Because Li Zicheng's false state title was called Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's regime was called Shun.

sentences.zh: 士英因疏糾從逆光時亨等；

translations.literal: Shiying therefore memorialized impeaching followers of the Shun such as Guang Shiheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying impeached those who followed the Shun regime.

sentences.zh: 時亨名附東林，故重劾之。

translations.literal: Shiheng's name attached to the Donglin; therefore heavily impeached.
translations.idiomatic: He especially attacked Shiheng as Donglin.

sentences.zh: 大鋮又誣逮顧杲及左光鬥弟光先下獄，劾周鑣、雷縯祚殺之。

translations.literal: Dacheng also falsely arrested Gu Gao and Zuo Guangdou's younger brother Guangxian and imprisoned them, impeaching Zhou Biao and Lei Peizuo for killing them.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng imprisoned Guangxian and attacked Zhou Biao and Lei Peizuo.

sentences.zh: 時有狂僧大悲出語不類，為總督京營戎政趙之龍所捕。

translations.literal: At the time there was a mad monk Dabei whose words were unlike others; captured by Grand Coordinator of capital camps Zhao Zhilong.
translations.idiomatic: The mad monk Dabei was captured by Zhao Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 大鋮欲假以誅東林及素所不合者，因造十八羅漢、五十三參之目，書史可法、高弘圖、薑曰廣等姓名，內大悲袖中，海內人望，無不備列。

translations.literal: Dacheng wished to use this to execute the Donglin and those he disliked, fabricating lists of eighteen arhats and fifty-three bodhisattvas, writing names of Shi Kefa, Gao Hongtu, Jiang Yueguang, and others; inside Dabei's sleeve—all hopes of the realm were listed.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng forged a list of targets in Dabei's sleeve.

sentences.zh: 錢謙益先已上疏頌士英，且為大鋮訟冤修好矣，大鋮憾不釋，亦列焉，將窮治其事。

translations.literal: Qian Qianyi had already memorialized praising Shiying and reconciling with Dacheng for vindication; Dacheng's resentment was not released and he also listed Qianyi, about to pursue the affair to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Even Qianyi was listed though he had reconciled with Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 獄詞詭秘，朝士皆自危，而士英不欲興大獄，乃當大悲妖言律斬而止。

translations.literal: The case words were strange and secret; courtiers all feared for themselves; Shiying did not wish to raise a great case and only sentenced Dabei under the law of demonic speech by decapitation and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying stopped at executing Dabei for demonic speech.

sentences.zh: 張縉彥以本兵首從賊，賊敗，縉彥竄歸河南，自言集義勇收復列城，即授原官，總督河北、山西、河南軍務，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Zhang Jinyan as head of the military first followed the bandits; when bandits were defeated Jinyan fled to Henan, claiming he gathered volunteers and recovered cities, and was immediately granted original office, grand coordinator of Hebei, Shanxi, and Henan military affairs with discretionary power.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinyan returned from following bandits and was restored.

sentences.zh: 其他大僚降賊者，賄入，輒復其官。

translations.literal: Other great officials who surrendered to bandits, on entering bribes, immediately had office restored.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered officials bought restoration with bribes.

sentences.zh: 諸白丁、錄役輸重賂，立躋大帥。

translations.literal: Common whites and record clerks offered heavy bribes and immediately rose to great command.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners bought high command with bribes.

sentences.zh: 都人為語曰：「職方賤如狗，都督滿街走。

translations.literal: Capital people said in rhyme: Personnel is cheap as dogs; commanders-in-chief fill the streets.
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme mocked that commanders filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 」其刑賞倒亂如此。

translations.literal: Reward and punishment were so inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments were inverted.

sentences.zh: 大清兵抵宿遷、邳州，未幾引還。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops reached Suqian and Pizhou; before long withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops reached Suqian and Pizhou then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 史可法以聞，士英大笑不止，坐客楊士聰問故。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa reported this; Shiying laughed without stopping; guest Yang Shicong asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa reported Qing withdrawal; Shiying laughed.

sentences.zh: 士英曰：「君以為誠有是事耶？

translations.literal: Shiying said: Do you think there really was such a matter?
translations.idiomatic: Shiying denied it was real.

sentences.zh: 」乃史公妙用也。

translations.literal: It is Lord Shi's clever trick.
translations.idiomatic: He called it Kefa's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 歲將暮，防河將吏應敘功，耗費軍資應稽算，此特為序功、稽算地耳。

translations.literal: Year's end river-defense officers should recount merit and audit military funds—this is only ground for sequencing merit and auditing.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed reports were only for merit reviews.

sentences.zh: 」侍講衛胤文兼給事中，監高傑軍。

translations.literal: Lecturer Wei Yinwen concurrently supervising secretary supervised Gao Jie's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yinwen supervised Gao Jie's army.

sentences.zh: 傑死，胤文窺士英指，論可法督師為贅。

translations.literal: When Jie died Yinwen probed Shiying's intent and discussed Kefa's supervision as superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: Yinwen called Kefa's supervision superfluous after Jie's death.

sentences.zh: 士英即擢胤文兵部右侍郎，總督傑營將士以分其權，可法益不得展布。

translations.literal: Shiying immediately promoted Yinwen to right vice minister of War, supervising Jie's camp troops to divide power; Kefa all the more could not deploy.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying promoted Yinwen to divide Kefa's power.

sentences.zh: 先是，左良玉接監國詔書，不肯拜，袁繼咸強之，乃開讀如禮。

translations.literal: Earlier Zuo Liangyu received the regency edict and would not bow; Yuan Jixian forced him and he then opened and read according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu at first refused the regency edict.

sentences.zh: 而屬承天守備何志孔、巡按御史黃澍入賀，陰伺朝廷動靜。

translations.literal: He ordered Chengtian garrison commander He Zhikong and surveillance censor Huang Shu to enter to congratulate and secretly watch court movements.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to watch Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 澍挾良玉勢，當陛見，面數士英奸貪不法，且言嘗受張獻忠偽兵部尚書周文江重賄，為題授參將，罪當斬。

translations.literal: Shu relied on Liangyu's power; at audience he face-to-face counted Shiying's treacherous greed and unlawfulness, and said he once received Zhang Xianzhong's false Minister Zhou Wenjiang's heavy bribe, titled acting commander—a crime deserving decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shu denounced Shiying at audience.

sentences.zh: 志孔亦論士英岡上行私諸罪。

translations.literal: Zhikong also discussed Shiying's selfish acts on the road and other crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhikong also attacked Shiying.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監韓贊周叱志孔退，士英跪乞處分，澍舉笏直擊其背曰：「願與奸臣同死。

translations.literal: Director of Rites Eunuch Han Zanzhou shouted Zhikong down; Shiying knelt begging disposition; Shu raised his tablet and struck his back: I wish to die with the traitor minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shu struck Shiying's back in audience.

sentences.zh: 」士英大號呼，王搖首不言者久之，贊周即執志孔候命。

translations.literal: Shiying cried out loudly; the prince shook his head long without speaking; Zanzhou immediately seized Zhikong awaiting order.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was silent; Zhikong was seized.

sentences.zh: 王因澍言意頗動，夜諭贊周，欲令士英避位。

translations.literal: The prince because of Shu's words was rather moved; at night told Zanzhou he wished Shiying to avoid office.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was moved to remove Shiying.

sentences.zh: 士英佯引疾，而賂福邸舊奄田成等向王泣曰：「上非馬公不得立，逐馬公，天下將議上背恩矣。

translations.literal: Shiying feigned citing illness but bribed Fu's old eunuchs Tian Cheng and others to weep to the prince: Without Lord Ma Your Majesty could not be established; driving Lord Ma away the realm will say Your Majesty repays kindness with betrayal.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying's eunuchs pleaded he was needed to enthrone the prince.

sentences.zh: 且馬公去，誰念上者？

translations.literal: And if Lord Ma goes, who will think of Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Who would care for the prince without Shiying?

sentences.zh: 」王默然，即慰留士英。

translations.literal: The prince was silent and comforted and kept Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: The prince kept Shiying.

sentences.zh: 士英亦畏良玉，請釋志孔，而命澍速還湖廣。

translations.literal: Shiying also feared Liangyu, requested releasing Zhikong, and ordered Shu to hurry back to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying released Zhikong and sent Shu away.

sentences.zh: 故都督掌錦衣衛劉僑者，嘗遣戍，由周文江賄張獻忠，受偽命，為錦衣指揮使。

translations.literal: Former commander Brocade Guard Liu Qiao had been sent to garrison; through Zhou Wenjiang bribing Zhang Xianzhong he received false appointment as Brocade Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao had served Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 及良玉復蘄、黃，僑削髮逃去，澍持之急。

translations.literal: When Liangyu recovered Qi and Huang Qiao shaved his head and fled; Shu pressed urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao fled when Liangyu recovered Qi and Huang.

sentences.zh: 而士英納僑賄，令訐澍，遂復僑官，削澍職。

translations.literal: Shiying accepted Qiao's bribe, had him impeach Shu, and restored Qiao's office, stripping Shu's office.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying restored Qiao and stripped Shu.

sentences.zh: 尋以楚府中尉言，逮澍。

translations.literal: Soon on Chu palace inner prince's words Shu was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was arrested on a prince's accusation.

sentences.zh: 良玉令部將群嘩，欲下南京索餉，因保救澍。

translations.literal: Liangyu ordered subordinates to clamor, wishing to descend on Nanjing demanding pay, thereby protecting Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's troops clamored to save Shu.

sentences.zh: 袁繼鹹為上疏代澍申理，士英不得已，乃免逮。

translations.literal: Yuan Jixian memorialized for Shu; Shiying had no choice and exempted arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jixian saved Shu from arrest.

sentences.zh: 澍遂匿良玉軍中，良玉與士英由此有隙。

translations.literal: Shu then hid in Liangyu's army; Liangyu and Shiying thereby had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Shu hid with Liangyu; a rift opened.

sentences.zh: 及偽太子獄起，良玉遂假為兵端。

translations.literal: When the false crown prince case arose Liangyu then falsely used it as military pretext.
translations.idiomatic: The false prince case became Liangyu's pretext for war.

sentences.zh: 太子之來也，識者指其偽，而都下士民譁然是之。

translations.literal: When the prince came knowledgeable men pointed to the fraud, yet capital gentry and people clamored agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Many knew the prince was false yet the crowd believed.

sentences.zh: 時又有童氏者，自稱王妃，亦下獄。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Lady Tong who called herself consort; she too was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tong claiming to be consort was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 督撫、鎮將交章爭太子及童妃事。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators and generals memorialized in succession disputing prince and Lady Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Officials disputed the prince and Lady Tong.

sentences.zh: 王亟出獄詞，遍示中外，眾論益籍籍，謂士英等朋奸，導王滅絕倫理。

translations.literal: The prince urgently issued prison words shown throughout within and without; public opinion grew more noisy, saying Shiying and others were factional traitors guiding the prince to extinguish human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's statement failed to calm opinion against Shiying.

sentences.zh: 澍在良玉軍中，日夜言太子冤狀，請引兵除君側惡。

translations.literal: Shu in Liangyu's army daily spoke the prince's injustice and requested leading troops to remove evil at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Shu urged Liangyu to purge Shiying.

sentences.zh: 良玉亦上疏請全太子，斥士英等為奸臣。

translations.literal: Liangyu also memorialized requesting preserving the prince and reviling Shiying and others as traitor ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu defended the prince and attacked Shiying.

sentences.zh: 又以士英裁其餉，大憾，移檄遠近，聲士英罪。

translations.literal: Also because Shiying cut his pay he was greatly resentful, issued proclamations far and near voicing Shiying's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu resented pay cuts and denounced Shiying.

sentences.zh: 復上疏言：「自先帝之變，士英利災擅權，事事為難。

translations.literal: He again memorialized saying: Since the late emperor's change Shiying profited from disaster and usurped power, making difficulty in every affair.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu listed Shiying's crimes since the capital's fall.

sentences.zh: 逆案先帝手定，士英首翻之。

translations.literal: The traitor case the late emperor fixed by hand; Shiying was first to overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying overturned the fixed traitor case.

sentences.zh: 《要典》先帝手焚，士英復修之。

translations.literal: The Canon the late emperor burned by hand; Shiying restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying restored the burned Canon.

sentences.zh: 越其傑貪焚遣戍濫授節鉞。

translations.literal: Transgressing Gao Jie, greedy and burning, sent to garrison, recklessly granting seals of command.
translations.idiomatic: He abused appointments including Gao Jie.

sentences.zh: 張孫振贓汙絞犯，驟畀京卿。

translations.literal: Zhang Sunzhen corrupt and strangling criminal suddenly given capital office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sunzhen was promoted despite crimes.

sentences.zh: 他如袁弘勳、楊文、劉泌、王燧、黃鼎等，或行同狗彘，或罪等叛逆，皆用之當路。

translations.literal: Others such as Yuan Hongxun, Yang Wen, Liu Bi, Wang Sui, and Huang Ding—some acted like dogs and pigs, some crimes equaled rebellion—all used on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Villains were placed in high office.

sentences.zh: 己為首輔，用腹心阮大鋮為添注尚書。

translations.literal: Already chief assistant he used confidant Ruan Dacheng as added minister.
translations.idiomatic: He made Dacheng added minister.

sentences.zh: 又募死士伏皇城，詭名禁軍，動曰廢立由我。

translations.literal: Also recruited dead soldiers hidden in the imperial city, falsely named forbidden army, moving saying deposition and establishment were in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: He hid soldiers in the palace threatening deposition.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之初，恭儉明仁，士英百計誑惑，進優童豔女，傷損盛德。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended he was respectful, frugal, clear, and humane; Shiying by a hundred schemes deceived, advancing pretty boys and seductive women, injuring sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying corrupted the prince with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 復引用大鋮，睚眥殺人，如雷縯祚、周鑣等，鍛煉周內，株連蔓引。

translations.literal: Again employing Dacheng, killing over grudges such as Lei Peizuo and Zhou Biao, forging cases within the palace, implicating branches and tendrils.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng murdered enemies like Lei and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 尤其甚者，借三案為題，凡生平不快意之人，一網打盡。

translations.literal: Especially using the three cases as theme, netting in one sweep all disliked in life.
translations.idiomatic: The three cases became a net for enemies.

sentences.zh: 令天下士民，重足解體。

translations.literal: Making realm gentry and people tread on eggs and lose substance.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lived in terror.

sentences.zh: 目今皇太子至，授受分明。

translations.literal: Now the true crown prince has come; succession is clear.
translations.idiomatic: The true prince had come with clear succession.

sentences.zh: 大鋮一手握定抹殺識認之方拱乾，而信朋謀之劉正宗，忍以十七年嗣君，付諸幽囚。

translations.literal: Dacheng with one hand grasped and erased witness Fang Gongqian who recognized him, trusting conspirator Liu Zhengzong, bearing to place the seventeen-year heir in hidden imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng suppressed recognition of the prince.

sentences.zh: 凡有血氣，皆欲寸磔士英、大鋮等，以謝先帝。

translations.literal: All with blood and breath wish to dismember Shiying and Dacheng to apologize to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: All wished to kill Shiying and Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 乞立肆市朝，傳首抒憤。

translations.literal: Beg establish market execution at court and transmit heads to vent anger.
translations.idiomatic: He begged public execution.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，遂引兵而東。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up he then led troops east.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu marched east.

sentences.zh: 士英懼，乃遣阮大鋮、硃大黃、黃得功、劉孔昭等禦良玉，而撤江北劉良佐等兵，從之西。

translations.literal: Shiying was afraid and sent Ruan Dacheng, Zhu Dahuang, Huang Degong, and Liu Kongzhao to resist Liangyu, withdrawing northern Liu Liangzuo's troops to follow west.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying sent armies against Liangyu and pulled northern troops west.

sentences.zh: 時大清兵日南下，大理少卿姚思孝，御史喬可聘、成友謙請無撤江北兵，亟守淮、揚。

translations.literal: At the time Great Qing troops daily pressed south; Vice Minister of Justice Yao Sixiao and Censors Qiao Keping and Cheng Youqian requested not withdrawing northern troops and urgently defending Huai-Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Officials begged to keep northern troops for Huai-Yang.

sentences.zh: 士英厲聲叱曰：「若輩東林，猶藉口防江，欲縱左逆入犯耶？

translations.literal: Shiying shouted harshly: You Donglin still use defending the river as pretext, wishing to let the Zuo rebel enter and attack?
translations.idiomatic: Shiying accused them of letting Zuo Liangyu in.

sentences.zh: 北兵至，猶可議款。

translations.literal: When northern troops arrive negotiation can still be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops might be negotiated with.

sentences.zh: 左逆至，則若輩高官，我君臣獨死耳！

translations.literal: When the Zuo rebel arrives you high officials—we ruler and ministers alone die!
translations.idiomatic: If Zuo came only the court would die.

sentences.zh: 」力排思孝等議，淮、揚備禦益弱。

translations.literal: He forcefully rejected Sixiao and others' discussion; Huai-Yang defenses grew weaker.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected defense plans; Huai-Yang weakened.

sentences.zh: 會良玉死，其子夢庚連陷郡縣，率兵至採石。

translations.literal: It happened Liangyu died; his son Menggeng in succession took commanderies and counties, leading troops to Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangyu died Menggeng advanced to Caishi.

sentences.zh: 得功等與相持，大鋮、孔昭方虛張捷音，以邀爵賞，而大清兵已破揚州，逼京城。

translations.literal: Degong and others confronted them; Dacheng and Kongzhao falsely trumpeted victory to seek ennoblement, while Great Qing troops had already broken Yangzhou and pressed the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: While they fought false victories, Qing troops took Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月三日，王出走太平，奔得功軍。

translations.literal: On the third day of the fifth month the prince fled to Taiping, running to Degong's army.
translations.idiomatic: On month 5 day 3 the prince fled to Degong.

sentences.zh: 孔昭斬關遁。

translations.literal: Kongzhao cut the pass and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao fled.

sentences.zh: 明日，士英奉王母妃，以黔兵四百人為衛，走浙江。

translations.literal: The next day Shiying escorted the queen mother consort with four hundred Qian troops as guard fleeing to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying fled to Zhejiang with the queen mother.

sentences.zh: 經廣德州，知州趙景和疑其詐，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Passing Guangde prefecture Magistrate Zhao Jinghe suspected fraud and closed the gate refusing defense.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde magistrate Zhao Jinghe refused them.

sentences.zh: 士英攻破，執景和殺之，大掠而去。

translations.literal: Shiying broke through, seized Jinghe and killed him, and plundered greatly before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying killed Zhao Jinghe and plundered Guangde.

sentences.zh: 走杭州，守臣以總兵府為母妃行宮。

translations.literal: Reaching Hangzhou the defending ministers used the commander's mansion as the queen mother's traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou gave the queen mother the commander's mansion.

sentences.zh: 不數日，大鋮、大典、方國安俱倉皇至，則得功已兵敗死，王被擒，次日，請潞王監國，不受。

translations.literal: Within days Dacheng, Dadian, and Fang Guoan all arrived in panic; Degong had already been defeated and died, the prince captured; the next day they requested Prince Lu supervise the state—not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: All fled to Hangzhou; the prince was captured; Lu was asked to supervise and refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大兵至，王率眾降，尋同母妃北去。

translations.literal: Before long Great Qing troops arrived; the prince led the masses to surrender, soon going north with the queen mother.
translations.idiomatic: The prince surrendered and went north.

sentences.zh: 此即大器等之所議欲立者也。

translations.literal: This was the one Daqi and others had discussed wishing to establish.
translations.idiomatic: This was the Lu prince they had once preferred.

sentences.zh: 杭州既降，士英欲謁監國魯王，魯王諸臣力拒之。

translations.literal: After Hangzhou surrendered Shiying wished to audience Supervising Prince Lu; Lu's ministers forcefully refused.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was refused by Prince Lu's court.

sentences.zh: 大鋮投硃大典於金華，亦為士民所逐，大典乃送之嚴州總兵方國安軍。

translations.literal: Dacheng went to Zhu Dadian at Jinhua and was also driven by the people; Dadian sent him to Yanzhou zongbing Fang Guoan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was driven from Jinhua to Fang Guoan.

sentences.zh: 士英，國安同鄉也，先在其軍中。

translations.literal: Shiying and Guoan were townsfolk; Shiying was first in his army.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying and Guoan were fellow townsfolk.

sentences.zh: 大鋮掀髯指掌，日談兵，國安甚喜。

translations.literal: Dacheng stroked beard and pointed, daily discussing warfare; Guoan was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng talked war; Guoan was pleased.

sentences.zh: 而士英以南渡之壞，半由大鋮，而己居惡名，頗以為恨。

translations.literal: Shiying because the southern crossing's ruin was half from Dacheng while he bore the evil name was rather resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying blamed Dacheng for the southern disaster.

sentences.zh: 已，我兵擊敗士英、國安。

translations.literal: Before long our troops defeated Shiying and Guoan.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops defeated them.

sentences.zh: 無何，士英、國安率眾渡錢塘，窺杭州，大兵擊敗之，溺江死者無算。

translations.literal: Before long Shiying and Guoan led troops across the Qiantang, spying on Hangzhou; Great Qing troops defeated them; drowned in the river beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Qiantang and were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 士英擁殘兵欲入閩，唐王以罪大不許。

translations.literal: Shiying led remnant troops wishing to enter Fujian; Prince Tang did not permit because the crime was great.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian refused Shiying for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 明年，大兵巢湖賊，士英與長興伯吳日生俱擒獲，詔俱斬之。

translations.literal: The next year Great Qing troops on Chaohu Lake; Shiying and Changxing Earl Wu Risheng were both captured; edict both beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying and Wu Risheng were captured and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 事具國史。

translations.literal: Affairs are detailed in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed in the national history.

sentences.zh: 大鋮偕謝三賓、宋之晉、蘇壯等赴江幹乞降，從大兵攻仙霞關，僵僕石上死。

translations.literal: Dacheng with Xie Sanbin, Song Zhiqin, Su Zhuang, and others went to the riverbank begging surrender, followed Great Qing troops attacking Xianxia Pass, died rigid on the stone.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng died attacking Xianxia Pass after surrendering.

sentences.zh: 而野乘載士英遁至台州山寺為僧，為我兵搜獲，大鋮、國安先後降。

translations.literal: Yet unofficial histories say Shiying fled to a Taizhou mountain temple as monk, was searched and captured; Dacheng and Guoan successively surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Unofficial histories say Shiying was caught as a monk.

sentences.zh: 尋唐王走順昌。

translations.literal: Soon Prince Tang fled to Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tang fled to Shunchang.

sentences.zh: 我大兵至，搜龍扛，得士英、大鋮、國安父子請王出關為內應疏，遂駢斬士英、國安於延平城下。

translations.literal: When our Great Qing troops arrived, searching Longgang, they obtained Shiying, Dacheng, and Guoan father and son's memorial asking the prince to leave the pass as inner response; they were then jointly beheaded at Yanping city.
translations.idiomatic: A letter exposing them as inner agents led to joint execution at Yanping.

sentences.zh: 大鋮方遊山，自觸石死，仍戮屍云。

translations.literal: Dacheng was touring mountains, died by striking stone himself, yet the corpse was still dismembered—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng killed himself on a rock but was still dismembered.
